dervis-irab:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ لِمَنْ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): a resumptive statement, brought to rebuke and reproach the disbelievers for the lagging behind in disbelief that has come from them, and their inability to reflect and gain insight. (لمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (من) is an interrogative noun for rebuke and disapproval; (ما) is a relative noun, a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (في السموات) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted element that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; and (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات).
(قُلْ لِلَّهِ كَتَبَ عَلى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ): a resumptive statement, brought so that the Messenger begins with the answer besides which there is no other answer. (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is Allah's"; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech. The clause (كتب على نفسه الرحمة) is resumptive, because it is independent of what precedes it and not included in the thread of what is said. (على نفسه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كتب); and (الرحمة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ): the lām is the answer to an omitted oath understood from His words «كتب على نفسه», as though He swore to that. The clause (يجمعنكم) has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. There has been much disagreement about this clause, but what we have chosen is closer to the truth. (إلى يوم القيامة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "resurrected" or "gathered" to the Day of Resurrection. (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (ريب) is its noun, (فيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl.
(الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): (الذين) is accusative as dispraise (al-naṣb ʿalā al-dhamm); it is also permissible to parse it as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause (فهم لا يؤمنون), the fāʾ being brought because of the scent of condition in the relative noun. The clause (خسروا أنفسهم) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يؤمنون) is its khabar. The clause (الذين خسروا أنفسهم), on the reading of accusative as dispraise, is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; and on the reading of the nominative it is resumptive, brought to explain the cause of their loss.

dervis-irab:13-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَكَنَ): it may be from al-suknā (dwelling), and it is made transitive with (في); its meaning is "to settle and remain". It may also be from al-sukūn (stillness), the opposite of movement. One of the two opposites suffices, because it indicates its opposite; and it is singled out for mention because stillness is the original state, while movement is incidental. It too is made transitive with (في).
(فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): their Originator.
It is related that Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I did not know (فاطر السموات والأرض) until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a well, and one of them said: 'I faṭartuhā', i.e. I originated it." Further discussion of this root will come.

* I'rab:
(وَلَهُ ما سَكَنَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ): the wāw is resumptive; (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (ما) is a relative noun, a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause (سكن في الليل والنهار) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. Al-Zamakhsharī preferred that the wāw be a conjunction, coordinated with His words «لله», i.e. with the clause reported by «قل», that is: Say: it is Allah's; and Say: and His is whatever dwells. There is no harm in that.
(وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (السميع) is a first khabar and (العليم) a second khabar.
(قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيًّا): a resumptive statement brought to continue the reply to them when they called him to the religion of his forefathers. (قل) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; (غير الله) is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (أتخذ) and (وليا) the second mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
(فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ وَلا يُطْعَمُ): (فاطر السموات والأرض) is a naʿt (adjective) or badal (substitute) of (الله); the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يطعم), in the active voice, is the khabar; and the clause (لا يطعم), in the passive, is conjoined to it.
(قُلْ إِنِّي أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): a resumptive statement brought to repeat the reply to them. (إن) and its noun; the clause (أمرت) is its khabar; and (إن) with its noun and khabar is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech. (أمرت) is a passive past verb and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (أن) and what falls within its scope are an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (أمرت). (أول) is the khabar of (أكون); (من) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause (أسلم) is the ṣila. (ولا تكونن): the wāw is a conjunction, (لا) is prohibitive, and (تكونن) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive by «لا»; and the clause is the object of an omitted speech, conjoined to what preceded, i.e. "and it was said to me: do not be". (من المشركين) is the khabar of (تكونن).
The meaning: I was commanded to submit (Islam) and forbidden from associating partners (shirk).

dervis-irab:15-18.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ إِنِّي أَخافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ): a resumptive statement, to be a third answer in reply to them. (إن) and its noun; the clause (أخاف) is its khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (إن) is conditional; (عصيت ربي) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The conditional clause may be parenthetical between the verb (أخاف) and its object, which is (عذاب يوم عظيم), and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial); the first is preferable. (يوم) is muḍāf ilayhi, and (عظيم) is an adjective.
(مَنْ يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ): the clause is an adjective of (عذاب يوم عظيم). (من) is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يصرف) is the protasis, and it is passive, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he". (عنه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يصرف); (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to one like it, attached to (يصرف), and the tanwīn in «إذ» is a substitute for a clause; its discussion will come under Benefits. The fāʾ links the apodosis; (قد) is a particle of verification; (رحمه) is a verb and its mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. The clause of the protasis and its apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «من».
(وَذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ): the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (الفوز) is the khabar and (المبين) an adjective; and the clause is resumptive or a ḥāl.
(وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ فَلا كاشِفَ لَهُ إِلَّا هُوَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional and (يمسسك) is the protasis, the kāf being its fronted mafʿūl bihi and (الله) its fāʿil, delayed in wording; (بضر) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يمسسك). (فلا): the fāʾ links the apodosis because the apodosis is a nominal clause; (لا) is the lā of generic negation, and (كاشف) is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كاشف); (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (هو) is a badal (substitute) of the position of (لا) and its noun; the khabar of «لا» is omitted, i.e. "existing"; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.
(وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): conjoined to what preceded. The clause «وهو على كل شيء قدير» gives the reason for the omitted apodosis, i.e. "then there is none to repel it but He". (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (قدير) the khabar, and (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير).
(وَهُوَ الْقاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبادِهِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ): the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (القاهر) the khabar; (فوق عباده) is an adverb attached to (القاهر), and it may be attached to an omitted second khabar or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being exalted". The image is a splendid one of subjugation and loftiness through dominance and power.

* Benefits:
(يَوْمَئِذٍ): the tanwīn that attaches to «إذ» in the like of يومئذ and حينئذ is a substitute for the clause to which «إذ» is annexed. The original is: "on the day when it is averted from him, He has had mercy on him"; the clause «يصرف عنه» was omitted and the tanwīn brought as a substitute for the omitted clause, for concision and elegance. Two quiescent letters then met: the dhāl of «إذ» and the tanwīn, so the dhāl was given a kasra according to the rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters. This kasra is not a kasra of declension due to the annexation of «يوم» to it, because «إذ» is permanently indeclinable owing to its resemblance to a particle in needing a clause and in being formed of two letters. The annexation in «يومئذ» and its like is not the annexation of one of two synonyms to the other, but the annexation of the more general to the more specific, as in "شجر أراك" (arāk trees).

dervis-irab:65-65.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَلْبِسَكُمْ): He mixes you up; their being mixed up means that fighting breaks out among them so that they become mingled or entangled in the fierce battles of war, in the manner of the poet's words:
وكتيبة لبّستها بكتيبة ... حتى إذا التبست نفضت لها يدي
(A squadron I entangled with another squadron, until, when they were locked together, I shook my hand free of them.)
(شِيَعاً): plural of شيعة, like سدرة and سدر. Al-Rāghib said: the شيعة are those through whom a person gains strength; the plural is شيع and أشياع.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: هُوَ الْقادِرُ عَلى أَنْ يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذاباً مِنْ فَوْقِكُمْ أَوْ مِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ) The speech is resumptive, brought to show His power, Exalted is He, to fling them into ruin and destruction. (هو) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (القادر) the khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (على) is a preposition, and (أن يبعث) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by (على); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (القادر). (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يبعث); (عذابا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من فوقكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of His word «عذابا»; and (أو من تحت أرجلكم) is conjoined to His word (من فوقكم). (أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعاً وَيُذِيقَ بَعْضَكُمْ بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ) (أو) is a conjunction; (يلبسكم) is conjoined to (يبعث); (شيعا) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (يذيق) is conjoined to (يلبس); (بعضكم) is the first object of (يذيق), and (بأس بعض) is the second object of (يذيق). (انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآياتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَفْقَهُونَ) The clause is resumptive.
(كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl or as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (نصرف الآيات) is an imperfect verb and its direct object, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of (انظر). (لعلهم) is laʿalla and its noun, and the clause (يفقهون) is its khabar; the clause of hope is a ḥāl.

dervis-irab:66-67.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُسْتَقَرٌّ) is a noun of time, and it may also be a noun of place; it is from استقر in the sense of "to be fixed, settled".

* I'rab:
(وَكَذَّبَ بِهِ قَوْمُكَ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ) Resumptive speech showing their denial of the punishment mentioned before. The pronoun may also refer back to the Qur'an. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (كذب), and (قومك) is the fāʿil (agent). The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial, so the clause is either resumptive or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «به», i.e. while it is the truth — which goes deeper into ugliness. (قُلْ لَسْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِوَكِيلٍ) The clause is resumptive, brought to answer them. The clause (لست) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (ليس) is a defective past verb and the tāʾ is its noun; (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (وكيل); the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (وكيل) is a noun genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is the khabar of (ليس). (لِكُلِّ نَبَإٍ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ) The clause is resumptive, brought to indicate that matters are bound to their times or their places. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (نبأ) is muḍāf ilayhi; (مستقر) is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). The wāw is a conjunction and (سوف) is a particle of the future; (تعلمون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn.

dervis-irab:68-68.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا رَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ يَخُوضُونَ فِي آياتِنا) The speech is resumptive, brought to command him ﷺ to turn away from them while they plunge into Our signs. (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the sense of condition, attached to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), which is (فأعرض عنهم). (رأيت) is a verb and its agent; the seeing here is visual, and therefore it takes a single object. In that case a ḥāl (circumstantial) must be supplied as omitted, i.e. "And when you see those who plunge into Our signs, engaged in plunging into them." The seeing may also be mental, with the second object omitted for brevity. (الذين) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يخوضون) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (في آياتنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يخوضون). (فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ) The fāʾ links the apodosis; (أعرض) is an imperative verb; (عنهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أعرض). (حتى) is a particle of limit and a preposition; (يخوضوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after (حتى); (في حديث) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يخوضوا). Genitive-governing (حتى) together with its interpreted genitive are attached to «أعرض». (غيره) is an adjective of (حديث); the pronoun refers back to the signs, and it is masculine in view of their being Qur'an or discourse. (وَإِمَّا يُنْسِيَنَّكَ الشَّيْطانُ فَلا تَقْعُدْ بَعْدَ الذِّكْرى مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) The speech is resumptive, brought to posit forgetfulness arising through the whispering of Satan. (إن) is conditional and (ما) is redundant (zāʾida), the nūn of «إن» being assimilated into it, i.e. if Satan occupies you with his whispering until you forget the prohibition while sitting with them. (ينسينك) is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; the kāf is the object of (ينسينّك), and (الشيطان) is its agent. The fāʾ links the apodosis; (لا) is prohibitive; (تقعد) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by the prohibitive (لا). (بعد الذكرى) is an adverb of time attached to (تقعد), and (مع) is an adverb of place also attached to (تقعد); (القوم) is muḍāf ilayhi, and (الظالمين) is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metaphor (istiʿāra) in (الخوض): in the language it means setting about wading into water and crossing through it; it has been borrowed for taking up talk and launching into it in various modes and manifold ways, by way of frivolity and idle play. It is thus an implicit, dependent metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya tabaʿiyya).
2- The difference in the condition: in the verse it is said «وإذا رأيت», the condition coming with (إذا) because their plunging into the signs is a matter not in doubt; and the second condition comes with (إن) because Satan's causing him to forget is a doubtful matter which may or may not happen, since he is protected from it. The rule has been given before. So glory be to the Speaker of these words!
3- Placing the overt noun in the place of the pronoun. Its discussion has been given before; it is to draw attention to their wrongdoing.

dervis-irab:69-70.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ذِكْرى) is the maṣdar of ذكر; no other word has come on the pattern فِعْلى with kasra on the fāʾ.
(عَدْلٍ) with fatḥa on the ʿayn, i.e. a ransom, because the ransomer makes the ransomed equal (يعدل) to its like.
العدل is the ransom.
(تُبْسَلَ) from البسل, whose origin in the language is prohibition and prevention. One says:
هذا عليك بسل, i.e. forbidden and barred to you. الإبسال is a maṣdar like البسل, meaning prevention. From it comes أسد باسل (a fierce lion), because its prey does not escape it, or because it is unassailable. And الباسل is the brave one, because he holds out against his adversary. In al-Mukhtār: «أبسله:
he surrendered him to destruction, so he is مبسل; and the words of the Exalted «أن تبسل نفس بما كسبت» — Abū ʿUbayda said: that is, that it be surrendered. المستبسل is one who resigns himself to death or to blows. استبسل means استقتل (he fought to the death), which is that he throws himself into war wishing to kill or be killed without fail.»

* I'rab:
(وَما عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ مِنْ حِسابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ) The wāw may be a conjunction to complete the discourse, or it may be resumptive, brought for the same purpose. (ما) is negating; (على الذين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); the clause (يتقون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (من حسابهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (شيء) is genitive in form by (من) and nominative in position as the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَلكِنْ ذِكْرى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and (لكن) is lightened and inoperative. (ذكرى) may be accusative as a maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq) by an implied verb, i.e. "but they remind them a reminding"; or nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a reminder"; or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "but upon them is a reminder." (لعلهم) is laʿalla and its noun, and the clause (يتقون) is its khabar; the clause of hope is a ḥāl. (وَذَرِ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ لَعِباً وَلَهْواً) The wāw is a conjunction; (ذر) is an imperative verb whose past tense the Arabs let die out — its discussion will come later in this book — and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت). (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (اتخذوا) is the ṣila; (دينهم) is the first object of (اتخذوا), (لعبا) the second object, and (لهوا) is conjoined to it. (اتخذوا) may also be in the sense of "acquired", taking a single object, in which case (لعبا) and (لهوا) are accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا) The clause is conjoined; it is a verb, a direct object, an agent and an adjective. (وَذَكِّرْ بِهِ أَنْ تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ بِما كَسَبَتْ لَيْسَ لَها مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلِيٌّ وَلا شَفِيعٌ) (ذكّر) is an imperative verb; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ذكّر). (أنّ) and what follows it are to be interpreted as a maṣdar that is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "for fear that it be surrendered to punishment and destruction." [Translator's note: the source writes «أنّ» with shadda here, while the particle in the verse is the lightened أَنْ.] The bāʾ is a preposition and (ما) is maṣdariyya; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تبسل). The clause (ليس) with what falls in its scope is an adjective of (نفس), or resumptive. (لها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (من دون الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; (ولي) is the noun of (ليس), and (شفيع) is conjoined to (ولي). (وَإِنْ تَعْدِلْ كُلَّ عَدْلٍ لا يُؤْخَذْ مِنْها) The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (تعدل) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (كل عدل) is accusative as a maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq); (لا) is negating; (يؤخذ) is a passive imperfect verb; and (منها) is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (يؤخذ). It is not permissible for the deputy agent to be a pronoun referring to (العدل), because here it remains a maṣdar, since the verb reaches it without an intermediary. Had what is offered (as ransom) been meant, it would have been a direct object, and the verb would only have reached it through the bāʾ, and the proper form of the speech would have been "وإن تعدل بكل عدل"; since this was departed from, it is known that it is a maṣdar. This is one of the subtleties that escape the mind. (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ أُبْسِلُوا بِما كَسَبُوا) The clause is resumptive, brought to show the ugliness of what they committed. (أولئك) is the mubtadaʾ and (الذين) its khabar; the clause (أبسلوا) is the ṣila; (بما كسبوا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أبسلوا), (ما) being maṣdariyya, i.e. "because of their earning". The relative noun may also be a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative, in which case His words (لَهُمْ شَرابٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَعَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِما كانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ) are the khabar, and the reference is to those who took their religion as play and amusement. (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (شراب) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; on the first parsing the clause is a second khabar, a ḥāl, or resumptive. (من حميم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of (شراب); (عذاب) is conjoined to (شراب), and (أليم) is an adjective. As for His words «بما كانوا يكفرون», the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is "أعدلهم" [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably أُعِدَّ لهم "has been prepared for them"], so it serves as an explanation of (أبسلوا). (ما) is maṣdariyya; the clause (كانوا) has no grammatical position, and the clause (يكفرون) is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of (كانوا).

dervis-irab:152-153.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأشد): one says «بلغ فلان أشدّه», i.e. he reached his full strength, in the sense of maturity and puberty. It is the age between eighteen and thirty. It is a plural with no singular, or a singular that came on the pattern of a plural. This is the gist of what is in al-Qāmūs.
Someone else said: «It is said that الأشدّ is a noun singular in form and meaning. It is also said that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ); on this view its singular is شدّة, like نعمة, or شدّ like كلب, or شدّ like ضرّ — three opinions about its singular.» It may also be said of it: it is the firm establishment of the strength of youth and age until one reaches, at the end of youth, the stage of grown men.
(الْكَيْلَ)
It is the instrument with which one measures; originally it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) applied to the instrument.
(الْمِيزانَ)
Originally on the pattern مفعال, from الوزن; its phonological change (iʿlāl) was discussed under ميقات in al-Baqara. From الوزن, so it is originally a maṣdar transferred to the instrument. Similar are المصباح and المقياس, for that by which one obtains light and that by which one measures.

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَقْرَبُوا مالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ)
The و is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تقربوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; the و (of the plural) is the fāʿil (agent), and مال اليتيم is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and بالتي: the relative noun is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to تقربوا, i.e. "except with the manner that is best". هي is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أحسن its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The form of the elative (ism al-tafḍīl) is used to draw attention to the fact that one should take the utmost care in this and do what is best. حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive, and يبلغ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تقربوا, and أشده is a direct object. (وَأَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزانَ بِالْقِسْطِ)
The clause is conjoined. أوفوا الكيل is a verb, agent and direct object; الميزان is a direct object conjoined to الكيل; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of أوفوا, i.e. "being equitable and just"; it may also be a ḥāl of the direct object, i.e. "complete". (لا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْساً إِلَّا وُسْعَها)
The clause is parenthetical between the two conjoined clauses and has no grammatical position; it serves to draw attention to the fact that the matter of measure and weight and observing justice in them requires precision and struggle against desire. لا is negating, نكلف is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), نفسا is a direct object, إلا is a particle of restriction, and وسعها is a second direct object; as if it were said: "Do all that is within your capacity and power." (وَإِذا قُلْتُمْ فَاعْدِلُوا وَلَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى وَبِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ أَوْفُوا)
The و is a conjunction, إذا is conditional and adverbial, and the clause قلتم is in the position of the genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (by annexation). The ف is connective (rābiṭa), and اعدلوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the ن. The و is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), لو is a non-jussive conditional particle, كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, and ذا قربى is its khabar. بعهد الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوفوا, and أوفوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the ن. (ذلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ)
The i'rab of its parallel has already been given. (وَأَنَّ هذا صِراطِي مُسْتَقِيماً فَاتَّبِعُوهُ) It is conjoined to what preceded. أنّ and its noun; صراطي is its khabar, and مستقيما is an emphatic ḥāl of صراطي, the governing agent in it being the sense of the demonstrative. The ف is the faṣīḥa ف, and اتبعوه is an imperative verb, its agent and its object; the clause has no grammatical position. The meaning is: if you want success and salvation from the pits of innovations and the falls of error. اتبعوه is an imperative verb, agent and direct object, and the clause has no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source repeats this last sentence.] (وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ) The و is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تتبعوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا; the و is the agent and السبل is a direct object. فتفرّق: the ف is causative (al-sababiyya), and تفرق — originally تتفرق — is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the ف in answer to the prohibition. بكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تفرق, and عن سبيله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "far removed from His path". (ذلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ) Its i'rab has already been given.

dervis-irab:19-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(شَيْءٍ): al-shayʾ (thing) is whatever can properly be known and reported about; its plural is ashyāʾ. The discussion of why ashyāʾ is a diptote has already preceded. In the terminology of the theologians (al-mutakallimūn), al-shayʾ is the most general of general terms, since it applies to everything that can properly be included under it. A disagreement arose among the theologians that we point to for its curiosity: the Ashʿarites — who are among Ahl al-Sunna — held that it is the existent and nothing else, while the Muʿtazilites differed from them, holding that it is that whose existence is possible, so it includes the non-existent. But both parties agreed that the impossible is excluded from its concept. The linguistic concept is that it does not include it [Translator's note: i.e. the impossible]. Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī said:
وضاقت الأرض حتى كاد هاربهم ... إذا رأى غير شيء ظنّه رجلا
(The earth grew so narrow that their fugitive, whenever he saw a no-thing, almost took it for a man.)

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهادَةً): a resumptive statement brought in reply to those who asked the Messenger ﷺ to show them someone who would testify for him that he is the Messenger of Allah. (قل) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you"; (أي شيء) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أكبر) is the khabar (predicate); (شهادة) is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the mubtadaʾ; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
(قُلِ: اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ): the clause is resumptive, brought to prepare the reply to them. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (شهيد) its khabar; the two adverbs are attached to (mutaʿalliq) (شهيد); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech. And if Allah is the witness between them and him, then He is greatest in testimony.
(وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هذَا الْقُرْآنُ لِأُنْذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَنْ بَلَغَ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (أوحي) is a passive past verb; (إليّ) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوحي); (هذا) is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (أوحي); (القرآن) is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; and the clause is conjoined, or resumptive, serving as a statement of reason. The meaning is that Allah's testimony for me that I am His Messenger is sufficient in the revelation of this Qur'an. The lām is for giving the reason, and (أنذركم) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām, the kāf being its object. (ومن): the wāw is a conjunction and (من) is a relative noun coordinated with the kāf in (أنذركم), i.e. "that I may warn you and warn everyone whom the Qur'an reaches".
(أَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ مَعَ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً أُخْرى): the hamza is for disapproving, affirmative interrogation; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and the clause (تشهدون) is its khabar. (أن) with its noun and khabar stands in place of the object of (تشهدون). The interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of an omitted speech, i.e. "and He says: do you indeed testify". (أن) is a particle resembling the verb; (مع) is an adverb of place attached to the omitted, fronted khabar of (أن); (آلهة) is its delayed noun; and (أخرى) is an adjective of (آلهة).
(قُلْ لا أَشْهَدُ قُلْ إِنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ وَإِنَّنِي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to affirm the reply to them. (لا) is negative and (أشهد) an imperfect verb, and the clause is accusative as the object of the speech. (قل) is an imperative verb with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being "you", and the clause is likewise resumptive for the same purpose. (إنما) is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (إله) the khabar and (واحد) an adjective. (وإنني): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) and its noun; (بريء) its khabar; and the clause is coordinated with what precedes it. (مما) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (بريء); and «ما» may be maṣdariyya or a relative noun, i.e. "from your associating partners with Allah", or "from the idols that you associate with Allah".

dervis-irab:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَما يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْناءَهُمُ): a resumptive statement brought in reply to those who claim that the People of the Book do not recognize him, i.e. the Messenger; the pronoun may also refer to the Qur'an. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (آتيناهم) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (الكتاب) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause (يعرفونه) is the khabar (predicate) of (الذين). (كما): the kāf is a preposition, and (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by the kāf; and the preposition with its genitive noun is accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). Many parallels to it have preceded. (أبناءهم) is a mafʿūl bihi.
(الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): (الذين) is likewise a mubtadaʾ; the clause (خسروا) is the ṣila; (أنفسهم) is a mafʿūl bihi; the fāʾ is linking because of the scent of condition in the relative noun; (هم) is a second mubtadaʾ, and the clause (لا يؤمنون) is the khabar of «هم»; and the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of (الذين). You may also parse it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who lost themselves". Ibn Jarīr parsed it as a naʿt (adjective) of the first «الذين», and that is acceptable. It has also been said that it is accusative as dispraise (ʿalā al-dhamm), and that too is possible.
(وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation and rebuke, i.e. "no one is more unjust", and it is a mubtadaʾ; (أظلم) is the khabar; (ممن) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أظلم); the clause (افترى) is the ṣila; (على الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (افترى); and (كذبا) is a mafʿūl bihi.
(أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآياتِهِ): conjoined to the clause (افترى), falling within the scope of the ṣila.
(إِنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ): (إن) and its noun; the clause (لا يفلح الظالمون) is the khabar; and the clause gives the reason for what preceded.

dervis-irab:22-23.t:
* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعاً): the wāw is resumptive; (يوم) is an adverb whose governor is omitted and left vague to increase the fear and terror; the meaning is: "and on the Day We gather them, such-and-such will be". It may also be the object of an implied «اذكر» (remember). The clause (نحشرهم) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (جميعا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا: أَيْنَ شُرَكاؤُكُمُ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ): (ثم) is a conjunction of delay, because of the length of time between the gathering and the saying; (للذين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نقول); the clause (أشركوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (أين) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, the adverb being attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (شركاؤكم) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); (الذين) is a relative noun, an adjective of (شركاء); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila; the tāʾ is the noun of (كنتم) and the clause (تزعمون) its khabar; and the two objects of (تزعمون) are omitted because they are known, i.e. "you claimed them to be partners".
(ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا): (ثم) is a conjunction of delay; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; (تكن) is a defective imperfect verb, jussive by (لم); (فتنتهم) is the noun of (تكن); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (أن) with what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, the khabar of (تكن).
(وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنا ما كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ): the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive; the Name of Majesty is genitive by the wāw, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to an omitted element, its implied form being «نقسم» (we swear); (ربنا) is a badal (substitute) or naʿt (adjective) of «الله»; the clause of the oath is in the position of the accusative as the object of their speech; (ما) is negative; (كان) and its noun; and (مشركين) is its khabar.

dervis-irab:154-157.t:
* Vocabulary:
(دِراسَتِهِمْ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «درس العلم» (he studied knowledge), of the pattern قتل, also درسا; this is the meaning intended here. This root has remarkable meanings. One says «درس الحنطة دراسا»: he threshed the wheat. «درس الناقة»: he broke in the she-camel and tamed her. «رجل مدرّس», and «درس الكتاب» for memorisation: he repeated its reading, درسا and دراسة. «درس المرأة»: he had intercourse with the woman. «درست المرأة»: the woman menstruated. «درس الثوب»: the garment wore out, so it is درس and دريس. «بسط دريسا», i.e. he spread a worn-out garment or carpet. A man killed another man in the assembly of al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir, and he ordered him to be killed. The man said: «أيقتل الملك جاره؟ ويضيع ذماره؟» (Will the king kill his protégé and neglect what he is bound to protect?) He said: «نعم إذا قتل جليسه، وخضب دريسه» (Yes, if he killed his companion and stained his carpet with blood),
i.e. his carpet. «طريق مدروس»: a road on which people have walked much until they have made it smooth.
And «ربع دارس ومدروس» (an effaced encampment). So you see that it points to the meaning of training, subduing and smoothing in all its senses, and this is of great subtlety.
(صَدَفَ): he turned away. It is mostly used intransitively, and here it is used intransitively. In al-Qāmūs: «صدف عنه»: he turned away from him, of the pattern ضرب or جلس; and «صدف فلانا»: he turned him away, like أصدفه. From this the error of using صدفة in the sense of المصادفة (chance encounter) becomes clear.

* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ تَماماً عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ وَتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ) The basic function of ثم is sequence with delay and an interval of time; hence the exegetes and grammarians hesitated over the real nature of the conjunction by it here, and I have not found in what they said anything convincing. I will first relate what they said, then indicate what is more deserving of preference. Some said that «ثمّ» comes for sequence in the reporting, as if this speaker wanted to avoid [the implication of] Moses, peace be upon him, being earlier in time. Al-Akhfash claimed that «ثم» may lack the sense of interval, as evidenced by your saying: «أعجبني ما صنعت اليوم ثم ما صنعت أمس أعجب» (What you did today pleased me; then what you did yesterday is more pleasing), because «ثم» in that is for the sequence of the reporting and there is no interval between the two reports. Ibn Mālik counted among this His saying the Exalted: «ثم آتينا موسى الكتاب». In al-Mughnī he said: «The apparent view is that «ثمّ» occurs in place of the ف». The grammarians have stated explicitly that «ثم» is put in place of the ف, as in the saying of Abū Duwād Jāriya ibn al-Ḥajjāj:
كهزّ الرّدينيّ تحت العجاج ... جرى في الأنابيب ثم اضطرب
(Like the shaking of a Rudaynī lance beneath the dust: it ran through the joints, then quivered.)
Al-Zajjāj said: it is conjoined to «أتل», the implied form being: «Recite what He has forbidden, then recite what We gave.»
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: to what is His saying «ثم آتينا موسى الكتاب» conjoined? I say: to «وصّاكم به». If you say: how is it valid to conjoin it to it with «ثم» when the giving was a long time before the enjoining? I say: this enjoining is ancient; every nation has continued to be enjoined with it on the tongue of its prophet. So it is as if it were said: That is what We enjoined upon you, O children of Adam, of old and recently; then, greater than that, We gave Moses the Book.» Perhaps this is the closest thing that can be said about it. [Translator's note: the source does not close the quotation mark of al-Zamakhsharī's passage; it is unclear whether the preceding sentence belongs to him or to the author.] آتينا موسى الكتاب is a verb, agent and its two objects. تماما is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of completing the favour and honour; it may also be a maṣdar in the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it means "We gave it to him with a complete giving, without deficiency"; or a maṣdar in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of آتينا, i.e. "completing", or of الكتاب, i.e. "while it is complete" [Translator's note: the source has «ماما», evidently a misprint for «تماما»]. على الذي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تماما», i.e. upon whoever carried it out well; the clause أحسن is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. تفصيلا is conjoined to «تماما», and لكل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تفصيلا». (وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً لَعَلَّهُمْ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ) هدى and رحمة are conjoined to تماما and تفصيلا. لعل and its noun; the clause of hope is circumstantial; بلقاء ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤمنون, and the clause يؤمنون is the khabar (predicate) of لعل. (وَهذا كِتابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ مُبارَكٌ فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَاتَّقُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ) The و is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, set forth to magnify the status of the Quran. هذا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and كتاب its khabar; the clause أنزلناه is a first adjective (ṣifa) and مبارك a second adjective. فاتبعوه: the ف is the faṣīḥa ف, i.e. "if you want to benefit from its blessing"; it serves to make what follows it consequent upon what precedes it. اتبعوه is a verb, agent and direct object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. اتقوا is conjoined to فاتبعوه, and the clause of hope is circumstantial. (أَنْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّما أُنْزِلَ الْكِتابُ عَلى طائِفَتَيْنِ مِنْ قَبْلِنا) أن and what falls in its scope are to be interpreted as a maṣdar that is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "out of dislike that you should say". إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); أنزل is a passive past verb, الكتاب is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and على طائفتين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل — the Jews and the Christians are meant by them. The clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). من قبلنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of طائفتين. (وَإِنْ كُنَّا عَنْ دِراسَتِهِمْ لَغافِلِينَ) The و is circumstantial, and إن is lightened from the heavy (inna), and it is inoperative (muhmala); its discussion has already been given. كان and its noun; عن دراستهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to غافلين; the لام is the distinguishing lām between the lightened إن and the negating إن, and غافلين is the khabar of كنا. (أَوْ تَقُولُوا لَوْ أَنَّا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا الْكِتابُ لَكُنَّا أَهْدى مِنْهُمْ) Conjoined to أن تقولوا. لو is conditional, أنّ and its noun; the clause أنزل علينا الكتاب is its khabar; الكتاب is the deputy agent, and علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل. The لام occurs in the apodosis of لو; كان and its noun, أهدى is its khabar, and منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أهدى. (فَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ) The ف is the faṣīḥa ف, because it is the answer to an omitted [statement] that it gives the reason for, i.e. "Do not make excuses, for the grounds for excuse have escaped you." فقد جاءكم: قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), and جاءكم is a verb and a direct object placed before [the agent], and بينة is the agent. The omitted element may also be a condition, i.e. "if you are truthful in the false promises and wild dreams with which you beguile yourselves". من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of بينة, or to جاءكم; هدى and رحمة are conjoined to بينة. Both views are fine and acceptable. (فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَذَّبَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وَصَدَفَ عَنْها) The ف is a conjunction making what follows it consequent upon what precedes it, for the revelation of the Quran — containing all the factors of guidance and mercy — requires that whoever denies it and turns his face away from it be the most unjust of people. من is interrogative, containing the sense of negation, i.e. "no one"; it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and أظلم is the khabar. ممن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أظلم; the clause كذب is the ṣila of the relative noun; بآيات الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كذّب; and صدف عنها is conjoined to كذب. (سَنَجْزِي الَّذِينَ يَصْدِفُونَ عَنْ آياتِنا سُوءَ الْعَذابِ) The clause is resumptive, set forth to establish the recompense resulting from this obstinate stance. نجزي is an imperfect verb, its agent latent (mustatir), and الذين is its object; the clause يصدفون is the ṣila of the relative noun. سوء العذاب is accusative as a second direct object of نجزي, or accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). The annexation of السوء to العذاب is an annexation of the adjective to the qualified noun, i.e. "the evil punishment". (بِما كانُوا يَصْدِفُونَ) The ب is a preposition, and ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows as a maṣdar in the genitive by the ب; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نجزي. كان and its noun, and the clause يصدفون is its khabar, i.e. "because of their turning away and aversion".

dervis-irab:71-71.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اسْتَهْوَتْهُ): its origin is from الهويّ, which is descending from a height to a low place; so it is as if the devils, when they lured him away in the earth, sought his falling in it.
(حَيْرانَ): straying, lost from the main road. It is a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle), whose feminine is حيرى, and therefore it is a diptote. Its verb is حار يحار, with the maṣdars حيرة, حيران and حيرورة. The common people err and say احتار.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ أَنَدْعُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَنْفَعُنا وَلا يَضُرُّنا) Resumptive speech, brought to show the state of one who calls to the worship of idols, as will come in the section on rhetoric. The hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (ندعو) is an imperfect verb, and the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (من دون الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ندعو); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the object of (ندعو); the clause (لا ينفعنا) is the ṣila (relative clause), and likewise the clause (ولا يضرنا) conjoined to it. (وَنُرَدُّ عَلى أَعْقابِنا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدانَا اللَّهُ) The wāw is a conjunction; (نرد) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (ندعو), falling under the same disapproval and negation; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن). (على أعقابنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. returning to polytheism after Allah has rescued us from it. (بعد) is an adverb attached to «نردّ»; (إذ) is an adverb of past time in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the clause (هدانا الله) is in the position of the genitive by annexation to «إذ»; (هدانا الله) is a verb, a direct object and an agent. (كَالَّذِي اسْتَهْوَتْهُ الشَّياطِينُ فِي الْأَرْضِ حَيْرانَ) This kāf may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "we are turned back a turning-back like the turning-back of the one whom the devils lured away"; or it may be a ḥāl from the deputy agent of (نرد), i.e. "we are turned back resembling the one whom the devils lured away." The clause (استهوته الشياطين) is the ṣila; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استهوته); and (حيران) is a ḥāl from the object of (استهوته). (لَهُ أَصْحابٌ يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى الْهُدَى ائْتِنا) (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and (أصحاب) is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in (حيران), and it may also be resumptive. The clause (يدعونه) is an adjective of (أصحاب); (إلى الهدى) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يدعونه); (ائتنا) is an imperative verb and (نا) is its object, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of an omitted speech, i.e. "they say: come to us"; the clause of speech is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (قُلْ: إِنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ هُوَ الْهُدى وَأُمِرْنا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The clause is resumptive. (إن) and its noun; (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and (الهدى) is its khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of (إن), and the clause of (إن) with what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech. (وأمرنا): the wāw is a conjunction; (أمرنا) is a passive past verb, and (نا) is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as the deputy agent; the clause is conjoined to the clause (إن هدى الله هو الهدى), falling within the scope of the speech. (ولنسلم): the wāw is a conjunction. There are many opinions about this lām which yield no benefit, and we have passed over them. The closest view seems to be that it keeps its basic function of giving the reason (taʿlīl); it gives the reason for the command, and the meaning is: "it was said to us: submit, so that we may submit." The purpose of its entry is to convey the future in a firmer way, since command and will relate only to what is future. (نسلم) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after it [Translator's note: i.e. after the lām], and (لرب العالمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نسلم).

* Rhetoric:
The negated representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī) in His words: «كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض». The thing compared is that it is neither fitting for us nor possible that we worship other than Allah after He has guided us, because if we did that we would be like one whom the devils have bewildered. It is thus the comparison of a clause with a clause, and the negation is derived from the disapproval in His words: «أندعو».

dervis-irab:72-73.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصُّورِ): the horn that is blown into; it is what is known today as البوق (the trumpet).

* I'rab:
(وَأَنْ أَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَهُوَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and (أن) with what follows it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "and we were commanded to establish the prayer." There is disagreement about this conjoining. It was said:
it is in the position of the accusative by the speech (القول), conjoined to His words (إن هدى الله هو الهدى), i.e. "say these two things." Sībawayh said: it is conjoined to (لنسلم), the implied meaning being: "we were commanded such-and-such for submission and that we establish the prayer"; and «أن» is joined to the imperative, as in their saying: كتبت إليه بأن قم ("I wrote to him: stand up"). Al-Zamakhsharī chose this view, saying:
«If you ask: to what are His words "وأن أقيموا" conjoined? I say: to the position of «لنسلم», as if it were said: we were commanded to submit and to establish (the prayer).» (أقيموا) is an imperative verb and (الصلاة) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (اتقوه) is conjoined to (أقيموا). (وهو): the wāw is resumptive; (هو) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) its khabar (predicate); the clause (تحشرون) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تحشرون). (وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ) The wāw is resumptive; (هو) is the mubtadaʾ and (الذي) its khabar; the clause (خلق السموات والأرض) is the ṣila; and (بالحق) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. in truth and earnest, not mocking nor in vain. (وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ) The wāw is resumptive, and the adverb is attached to an implied «اذكر» (remember); the clause is resumptive, brought to show the speed of bringing into being. The clause (يقول) is in the position of the genitive by annexation. (كن) is a complete imperative verb, not a defective one, so it is satisfied with its nominative; the agent of (كن) is a pronoun for all that Allah the Exalted creates on the Day of Resurrection. The fāʾ is a conjunction, and (يكون) is a complete imperfect verb conjoined to (كن). (قَوْلُهُ الْحَقُّ) There has been much disagreement about the i'rab of this speech. What I choose is that it is a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, the clause being resumptive; there is no benefit in the views that were put forward [Translator's note: the source has «أوردها», "that he put forward", without naming the person]. He, Glorified is He, informs about His word that it is never other than truth. (وَلَهُ الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (الملك) is the delayed mubtadaʾ. (يوم) is an adverb of time attached to an omitted element that is a badal (substitute) from the first adverb in His words «يوم يقول»; the clause (ينفخ) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; and (في الصور) is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (ينفخ). (عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ) (عالم) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the wāw is a conjunction, and (الحكيم) and (الخبير) are its two khabars [Translator's note: i.e. of (هو)]. The clause is resumptive.

dervis-irab:74-75.t:
* Vocabulary:
(آزَرَ): The exegetes and the scholars of language have disagreed about the word آزر in ways that yield no benefit. The closest thing said about it is that it is a non-Arabic proper name, and therefore it is a diptote.
(مَلَكُوتَ): meaning His dominion (ملكه); the tāʾ was added to it as it was added in الجبروت.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ آزَرَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to an implied «اذكر» (remember), conjoined to (قل أندعو), i.e.:
"and mention to Quraysh — after you have disapproved of their worshipping what neither benefits nor harms — the time when Ibrāhīm, whose religion they claim to follow, said..." The clause (قال إبراهيم) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; (لأبيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (قال); and (آزر) is a badal (substitute) from (أبيه). (أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْناماً آلِهَةً إِنِّي أَراكَ وَقَوْمَكَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) The hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (أصناما) is the first object of (تتخذ), and (آلهة) the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (إن) and its noun, and the clause (أراك) is its khabar (predicate); the clause gives the reason for the disapproval. (قومك) is conjoined to the kāf, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). (في ضلال) is either the second object if the seeing is mental, or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) if the seeing is visual; (مبين) is an adjective. (وَكَذلِكَ نُرِي إِبْراهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) The wāw is parenthetical; the kāf with its genitive is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its implied form being: "and like that making-known and giving of insight, We make known to Ibrāhīm and give him insight into the dominion of the heavens and the earth." Abū Ḥayyān objected to this implied form, saying: «This is remote from what the wording indicates.» Someone answered him, saying: it was remote only because the omitted element is not from what is pronounced; had he supplied it as "and just as We showed you guidance, O Muḥammad", it would have been close, since both the wording and the meaning indicate it. Abū al-Baqāʾ supplied it in two ways. One of them — he said: «It is accusative by an implied «أريناه» (We showed him), its implied form being:
"and just as he saw his father and his people in manifest error, We showed him that."» It may also be accusative by the (نري) after it, as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being:
"We show him the dominion of the heavens and the earth with a showing like the showing of his father's error." [Translator's note: the source does not clearly mark where Abū al-Baqāʾ's quotation ends; the closing quotation mark is absent.] The kāf may also be in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and the matter is thus." (إبراهيم) is the first mafʿūl bihi, and (ملكوت السموات والأرض) is the second object. The whole clause has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical between His words «وإذ قال» and the drawing of evidence for that in His words «فلما جن عليه الليل». (وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُوقِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction and the conjoined element is omitted, i.e. "and We did that so that he would be". The lām is for giving the reason (taʿlīl); (يكون) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of reason, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted conjoined element. The noun of (يكون) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), and (من الموقنين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of (يكون).

dervis-irab:158-158.t:
* I'rab:
(هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ آياتِ رَبِّكَ) The clause is resumptive, set forth to deem their coming to faith unlikely. هل is an interrogative particle containing the sense of negation, because they were like people waiting for that. ينظرون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the و is the fāʿil (agent). إلا is a particle of restriction, and أن تأتيهم الملائكة is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) that is an "emptied" excepted (mustathnā mufarragh), so it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). أو is a conjunction, and يأتي ربك is conjoined to تأتيهم الملائكة; أو يأتي بعض آيات ربك is likewise conjoined. The meaning is that they are waiting for all the signs of your Lord, or some of them, to come to inform them of the Hour. (يَوْمَ يَأْتِي بَعْضُ آياتِ رَبِّكَ لا يَنْفَعُ نَفْساً إِيمانُها لَمْ تَكُنْ آمَنَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِي إِيمانِها خَيْراً)
The adverb is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying لا ينفع, and the clause يأتي بعض آيات ربك is in the position of the genitive by annexation (as muḍāf ilayhi). لا is negating, and ينفع نفسا إيمانها is a verb, direct object and agent. The clause لم تكن آمنت is an adjective (ṣifa) of «نفسا»; separation between the qualified noun and its adjective is permissible because the agent is not extraneous. The clause may also be resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya). من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause آمنت is the khabar (predicate) of تكن; أو is a conjunction, كسبت is conjoined to آمنت, and خيرا is a direct object. (قُلِ انْتَظِرُوا إِنَّا مُنْتَظِرُونَ) The clause is resumptive, set forth to threaten them.
The clause انتظروا is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). The imperative here is for menace, and the direct object awaited is omitted to increase the fright and terror, as though it is too great to enter within the bounds of guessing and conjecture, and the soul is most fearful of the unknown. إنا منتظرون: إنّ, its noun and its khabar; the clause is also resumptive, set forth to match their waiting with the like of it.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is laff (folding together); the discussion of laff and nashr (folding and unfolding) has already been given. The underlying form of the speech is: "On the day some of the signs of your Lord come, a soul that was not believing before will not benefit from its faith afterwards, nor will a soul that did not earn good in its faith before benefit from the good it earns afterwards." But He folded the two statements together and made them one statement, preferring eloquence and inimitability, and did not follow it with the unfolding (nashr), because the outcome is one, and it is known for both of them.

dervis-irab:24-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَكِنَّةً): al-akinna is the plural of kinān (with kasra on the kāf), which is the protective covering and screen of anything; it is also pluralized as aknān. Kannahu and akannahu: he screened it. Abū Zayd said: the triliteral and the quadriliteral are two dialectal forms meaning both screening and concealing. Istakanna: he hid himself; akanantuhu fī nafsī: I concealed it and kept it hidden. The quiver of arrows is called kināna because it covers them, and when one wishes to take them out he scatters them; from this is the saying of al-Ḥajjāj in his sermon: "He scattered his quiver before him." Kānūn al-shitāʾ is the coldest part of winter, and among their sayings is: "Better than the brazier (al-kānūn) in Kānūn." The first kānūn is the fireplace at which one warms oneself. Al-kanna, with fatḥa on the kāf, is the wife of one's son or brother, its plural being kanāʾin. Among the meanings of al-kānūn is "the burdensome person"; from this is the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa satirizing his mother:
أغر بالًا إذا استودعت سرّا ... وكانونا على المتحدثينا
(Most careless when entrusted with a secret, and a burden upon those who converse.) [Translator's note: the first word appears in the source as printed, «أغر بالًا»; the line is usually cited as «أغِربالًا» (a sieve).]
Among colloquial expressions that are sound Arabic is their saying: "kankana in the house", i.e. he kept to it and settled in it, especially in winter.
(وَقْراً): al-waqr, with fatḥa on the wāw, is the maṣdar of waqarat udhnuhu, i.e. his ear became heavy and his hearing went; the word is metaphorical. Among the curious things about this root is that it indicates heaviness and gravity. One says: waqara yaqiru — with kasra on the middle radical of the imperfect — al-ʿaẓma: he cracked the bone; and waqara yaqiru qira, waqāra and waqr, said of a man: he was grave, possessed of dignity and steadfast. Waqarat udhnuhu, of the pattern taʿiba: it became heavy or his hearing went. Al-waqār: forbearance and gravity; it is the maṣdar of waqura with ḍamma. A woman is waqūr: faʿūl in the sense of an active participle, like ṣabūr and shakūr. Abū Firās said:
وقور وريعان الصبا يستفزّها ... فتأرن أحيانا كما يأرن المهر
(Grave, yet the first bloom of youth stirs her, so at times she frisks as the colt frisks.)
(أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ): in Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-asāṭīr are falsehoods; the singular is usṭūra (with ḍamma) and isṭāra (with kasra). Others said it is a plural of a plural: asāṭīr is the plural of asṭār, and asṭār is the plural of saṭar with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ; as for saṭr with sukūn, its plural of paucity is asṭur and its plural of multitude is suṭūr. It has also been said that it is the plural of the plural of a plural: asāṭīr is the plural of asṭār, asṭār the plural of asṭur, and asṭur the plural of saṭr. Al-Mubarrad said it is the plural of usṭūra, like urjūḥa and arājīḥ, and uḥdūtha and aḥādīth. The meaning of al-asāṭīr is false tales.

* I'rab:
(انْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَذَبُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ): a resumptive statement brought to report their lying. (انظر) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (كذبوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; and the clause is in the position of the accusative by (انظر), because it suspends it from governing. (على أنفسهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كذبوا).
(وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ): the wāw may be a conjunction, so that the clause is coordinated with the clause (كذبوا) and falls within the scope of the looking; and the wāw may be resumptive, so that the clause is resumptive, brought to report through it about their lying. (ضل) is a past verb; (عنهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ضل); (ما) may be a nominal relative, so that it is the fāʿil of (ضل) and the clause (كانوا يفترون) is the ṣila (relative clause); and it may be maṣdariyya, so that the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the fāʿil of (ضل); and the clause (يفترون) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان).
(وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (منهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (من) is a relative noun, a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يستمع) is the ṣila; and (إليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يستمع). The secret of the singular in the ṣila will come under Rhetoric. [Translator's note: no such discussion appears in the Rhetoric section of this entry.]
(وَجَعَلْنا عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِي آذانِهِمْ وَقْراً): the wāw conjoins to the preceding clause, a verbal clause conjoined to a nominal one. It has also been said that the wāw is circumstantial with an implied «قد», i.e. "and We had made". (جعلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (على قلوبهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جعلنا) as its second object — this if we take (جعلنا) as a verb of transformation; but if it means "We created", it takes a single object, which is (أكنة), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl from it, because had they come after it they would have been an adjective of it. (أن يفقهوه) is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "out of aversion to their understanding it". (وفي آذانهم وقرا) is conjoined to the preceding clause.
(وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ آيَةٍ لا يُؤْمِنُوا بِها): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (يروا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and the wāw its fāʿil; (كل آية) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لا) is negative; (يؤمنوا) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and (بها) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمنوا).
(حَتَّى إِذا جاؤُكَ يُجادِلُونَكَ): «حتى» here may be of limit and genitive, so that «إذا جاءوك» is in the position of the genitive, meaning "until the time of their coming", and the clause (يجادلونك) is a ḥāl. And (حتى) may be inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), which is the one followed by clauses. In either case, the clause (يجادلونك) is a ḥāl from the wāw in (جاءوك).
(يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: إِنْ هذا إِلَّا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (الذين) is the fāʿil, the clause (كفروا) the ṣila; (إن) is negative; (هذا) is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أساطير الأولين) is the khabar; and the negated clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy) — in placing coverings on the hearts and heaviness in the ears — for the aversion of their hearts and their hearing from accepting the truth and believing in its soundness. We add here that kināya has the merit of giving meanings the form of things perceived by the senses, and this merit is among the most prominent characteristics of the arts: when a painter draws for you a picture of hope or despair, he dazzles you and makes you see, clear and tangible, what you were unable to express. On this basis the splendour of the image of these people becomes clear to you — those upon whose hearts barriers have been struck and whose minds have grown dull, so that they bring forth no taste, disclose no art and are stirred to no knowledge. Of this kind in displaying splendour is the saying of al-Buḥturī:
يغضّون فضل اللحظ من حيث ما بدا ... لهم عن مهيب في الصدور محبّب
(They lower the overflow of their glances, wherever he appears to them, before one held in awe and beloved in their breasts.)
For he expressed by kināya people's esteem for the one praised and their awe of him through the lowering [Translator's note: the source prints «بعض» (some), evidently for «بغضّ» (lowering)] of the eyes, which is in reality a proof of awe and veneration. This characteristic appears clearly in the kināyas you will meet in the Qur'an concerning the attribute, the one described and the attribution, which we will point out in their places.

dervis-irab:26-27.t:
* I'rab:
(وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَيَنْأَوْنَ عَنْهُ): the wāw is resumptive; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (ينهون) is the khabar (predicate); (عنه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينهون). The pronoun «هم» refers to the disbelievers, and the pronoun of «عنه» refers to the Qur'an or to the Prophet ﷺ. The clause (ينأون عنه) is conjoined to (ينهون عنه).
(وَإِنْ يُهْلِكُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَما يَشْعُرُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (إن) is negative; (يهلكون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أنفسهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; and the clause (يشعرون) is conjoined to (يهلكون).
(وَلَوْ تَرى إِذْ وُقِفُوا عَلَى النَّارِ): a resumptive statement brought to begin describing the contradictory, incoherent states that will issue from them on the Day of Resurrection. The wāw is conditional [Translator's note: so in the source; the conditional particle is (لو), the wāw being resumptive]; (ترى) is an imperfect verb; and the apodosis (jawāb) of (لو) is omitted because the meaning is understood, the implied form being: "you would have seen something astonishing and tremendous". The seeing here may be mental: i.e. if you turned to them with your heart and thought, to contemplate their states and grasp the reality of their affair at that time, you would increase in certainty. And it may be visual, its object omitted, i.e. "if you could see their states and witness them closely". (إذ) is an adverb for past time, attached to (ترى); the clause (وقفوا) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (على النار) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (وقفوا).
(فَقالُوا: يا لَيْتَنا نُرَدُّ وَلا نُكَذِّبَ بِآياتِ رَبِّنا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (قالوا) is conjoined to (وقفوا). (يا) is a vocative particle with the one addressed omitted, or it is merely for drawing attention. (ليت) and its noun; the clause (نرد) is its khabar. The wāw is of accompaniment (al-maʿiyya); (لا) is negative; (نكذب) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the wāw of accompaniment; and (أن) with what follows it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) conjoined to an imagined maṣdar, the implied form being: "would that there were for us a return, and an absence of denial, and being among the believers". The clause of wishing is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī has a lengthy discussion of the reading «ولا نكذب» with the nominative, and he ended by preferring it over the reading with the accusative; that is mere strained reasoning. The wāw is a conjunction; (نكون) is conjoined to (نكذب); the noun of (نكون) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we"; and (من المؤمنين) is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there are two beautiful devices:
1- Jinās (paronomasia) between (ينهون) and (ينأون). It is jinās al-taṣrīf, which is the difference in the form of the two words by substituting one letter for another, or for one close to it in point of articulation, whether the substitution is at the beginning, in the middle or at the end. Among the curious instances of this paronomasia in poetry is the saying of al-Buḥturī:
عجب الناس لاغترابي وفي الأطراف تلقى منازل الأشراف
وقعودي عن التقلب والأر ... ض لمثلي رحيبة الأكناف
ليس عن ثروة بلغت مداها ... غير أني امرؤ كفاني كفافي
(People marvel at my living abroad — yet on the outskirts are found the dwellings of the noble — and at my refraining from roaming, though the earth is wide-sided for one like me. It is not from wealth that has reached its limit, but I am a man whose sufficiency suffices me.)
And beautiful is the saying of Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī:
تعس الحريص وقل ما يأتي به ... عوضا عن الإلحاح والإلحاف
إن الغنيّ هو الغنيّ بنفسه ... ولو انه عاري المناكب حافي
ما كلّ ما فوق البسيطة كافيا ... وإذا قنعت فكلّ شيء كاف
(Wretched is the greedy man, and little is what he gains in return for insistence and importunity. The rich man is the one rich in himself, even if he is bare-shouldered and barefoot. Not all that is on the earth is sufficient, yet when you are content, everything suffices.)
And al-Sharīf al-Raḍī reached the utmost of it when he said:
لا يذكر الرمل إلا حنّ مغترب ... له إلى الرمل أوطار وأوطان
(The sands are not mentioned but an exile yearns, who has in the sands his longings and homelands.)
2- The second device is concision (ījāz) by omitting the apodosis of «لو» in the second verse, and the object of (ترى) in it as well. Omission is frequent and widespread in the Qur'an; its benefit is that the soul goes every way in supplying the omitted element, and the imagination widens to supply it. Among instances of omitting the apodosis of (لو) is the saying of Abū Tammām in his ode rhyming in bāʾ, in which he praised al-Muʿtaṣim bi-llāh upon his conquest of Amorium:
لو يعلم الكفر كم من أعصر كمنت ... له المنيّة بين السّمر والقضب
(If unbelief knew for how many ages death lay in wait for it between the brown lances and the swords...)
I.e. if unbelief knew that, it would have made its preparations, or it would not have ventured upon what it rashly did. However, omitting the apodosis must have some indication pointing to it; for that reason the apodosis appears in His words, Exalted is He: «ولو فتحنا عليهم بابا من السماء فظلّوا فيه يعرجون لقالوا: إنما سكرت أبصارنا بل نحن قوم مسحورون», since if the apodosis had been omitted, the place of the omitted element would not have been known.

* Benefits:
The polytheists thought that they could harm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and could injure him, and his uncle Abū Ṭālib used to stand between them and his nephew. He said in verse of his own composition:
والله لن يصلوا إليك بجمعهم ... حتى أوسد في التراب دفينا
فاصدع بأمرك ما عليك غضاضة ... وابشر بذاك وقرّ منه عيونا
ودعوتني وزعمت أنك ناصح ... ولقد صدقت وكنت ثمّ أمينا
وعرضت دينا لا محالة أنه ... من خير أديان البرية دينا
لولا الملامة أو حذاري سبّةً ... لوجدتني سمحا بذاك مبينا
(By Allah, they will not reach you with all their host until I am laid in the dust, buried. So proclaim your affair — no shame is upon you — and rejoice in that, and let your eyes be gladdened by it. You called me and claimed that you were a sincere adviser; you spoke the truth and were trustworthy therein. You presented a religion which is without doubt among the best religions of mankind. Were it not for blame, or my fear of reproach, you would have found me openly accepting of it.)

dervis-irab:159-161.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ وَكانُوا شِيَعاً لَسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ) A resumptive statement, set forth to urge the unity that Allah commanded and to forbid division.
إنّ and its noun; the clause فرقوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and دينهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause وكانوا is conjoined to the ṣila clause, and شيعا is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا. The clause لست is the khabar of إنّ; ليس and its noun; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar, since the meaning is completed by it; في شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which منهم is attached, i.e. "you are not settled among them in anything". It is also possible that في شيء is the khabar and منهم a ḥāl (circumstantial) placed before it. (إِنَّما أَمْرُهُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ) A resumptive statement, set forth to indicate that the return of all matters is to Allah the Exalted. إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); أمرهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and إلى الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar. ثم is a conjunction; ينبئهم is an imperfect verb and the ه is its object; بما — the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as the second object; the clause كانوا is the ṣila of «ما», and the clause يفعلون is the khabar of كانوا. (مَنْ جاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثالِها)
A resumptive statement, set forth to explain the reward of those who do [good]. The restriction to ten is because it is the lowest degree of multiplication; otherwise the recompense cannot be counted.
من is a jussive conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; جاء is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); بالحسنة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاء. The ف is connective for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar placed first, and عشر is a mubtadaʾ placed after it, and أمثالها is a muḍāf ilayhi. It is to be noted that the rule was not observed in «عشر», namely that it takes the opposite gender to the counted noun when it is in its simple form; we will speak about that in the Benefits section. (وَمَنْ جاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلا يُجْزى إِلَّا مِثْلَها) Conjoined to what preceded. إلا is a particle of restriction, and مثلها is a second direct object, or accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). (وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) The و is a conjunction, هم is a mubtadaʾ, لا is negating, and يظلمون is a passive imperfect verb; the و is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the khabar of «هم». (قُلْ: إِنَّنِي هَدانِي رَبِّي إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) The clause is resumptive, to repeat what must be done and said. إنّ and its noun; the clause هداني is its khabar, and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). إلى صراط is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to هداني as a second object. (دِيناً قِيَماً مِلَّةَ إِبْراهِيمَ حَنِيفاً وَما كانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) دينا is accusative as a badal (substitute) from the position of «إلى صراط», because its meaning is "He guided me to a path" (هداني صراطا). هدى, as we said before, is transitive sometimes with «إلى», as here, and sometimes by itself, as in His saying: «ويهديكم صراطا مستقيما». It may also be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He guided me with the guidance of an upright religion". I do not know how Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed himself to parse «دينا» as a second object, when the second object is «إلى صراط». قيما is an adjective, i.e. "straight". ملة إبراهيم is a badal from دينا, and حنيفا is a ḥāl of إبراهيم. وما: the و is a conjunction, ما is negating, كان and its latent (mustatir) noun; من المشركين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar, and the clause is conjoined to the ḥāl, so it is a ḥāl after a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
