The masculine and feminine forms of numbers:
The number was put in the masculine [Translator's note: so in the source, «ذكّر العدد»; the form عشر without ة is the one normally used with feminine counted nouns, and this is the point being explained], while the counted noun is masculine, for several reasons:
1- Annexation has an effect, as mentioned before; the masculine acquired femininity from the feminine [to which it is annexed], so it was given the rule of the feminine in dropping the ة from its number. For this reason its verb is put in the feminine when it is annexed, as in: «يلتقطه بعض السيارة». And Qays said:
وما حب الديار شغفن قلبي ... ولكن حب من سكن الديار
(It is not love of the dwellings that has smitten my heart, but love of the one who dwelt in them.)
2- This masculine stands for a feminine, so what is meant by it was observed rather than the wording. What counts in masculine and feminine is the state of the intended qualified noun, not its own state. The implied form is: «فله عشر حسنات أمثالها» (he will have ten good deeds like it); then the qualified noun was omitted, its adjective was put in its place, and the number was left as it was.
3- Something accompanied the wording that supports the intended meaning, namely femininity. On this basis is interpreted the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
فكان مجني دون من كنت أتّقي ... ثلاث شخوص كاعبان ومعصر
(My shield against those I feared was three persons: two full-breasted girls and a maiden come of age.)
The regular form would have been «ثلاثة شخوص», but he used شخوص as an allusion to women. What made that easier is his saying كاعبان ومعصر, i.e. "they are two full-breasted girls and a maiden come of age".

dervis-irab:76-78.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جَنَّ): The derivation of this root was given earlier when الجنة was mentioned. Here is what is specific to the verb predicated of the night. One says جنّ عليه الليل and أجنّ عليه in the sense of "it grew dark (over him)", used intransitively; and جنّه and أجنّه, used transitively. This is where the triliteral and quadriliteral forms agree; however, the better usage is جنّ عليه الليل and أجنّه الليل, so that the triliteral is intransitive and the quadriliteral transitive.
(أَفَلَ): (أفل) الشيء with the maṣdar أفول, of the patterns ضرب and قعد: it disappeared (set).
(بازِغاً): البزوغ is rising. One says بزغ with fatḥa on the zāy, يبزغ with ḍamma on it; it is used intransitively and transitively. The bāʾ together with the zāy, as the first and second radicals of a verb, have a common, similar property, namely the meaning of rising and coming out into view. One says بزّه ثوبه and ابتزّه: he stripped him of his garment in his sight; and ابتزت من ثيابها: she stripped off her clothes and appeared in her nakedness. From this are the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
إذا ما الضجيع ابتزّها من ثيابها ... تميل عليه هونة غير متعال
(When her bedfellow strips her of her clothes, she leans toward him gently, without haughtiness.)
And بزل الشراب من المبزل: he let the drink flow out of the tap. Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā said:
سعى ساعيا غيظ بن مرّة بعد ما ... تبزّل ما بين العشيرة بالدم
(The two strivers of Ghayẓ ibn Murra strove [for peace] after what lay between the clan had burst open with blood.)
And البازي is a well-known bird (the falcon); and it is said: "So-and-so bides his time like the soothsayer, then swoops like the falcon." This is quite remarkable.

* I'rab:
(فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ رَأى كَوْكَباً قالَ: هذا رَبِّي) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the clause (قال إبراهيم لأبيه), so His words:
«وكذلك نري إبراهيم» are parenthetical, as was said before. (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking (rābiṭa); (جن) is a past verb; (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (جن); (الليل) is the fāʿil (agent). The clause (جن) is in the position of the genitive by annexation, or has no grammatical position on the second view. The clause (رأى كوكبا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; the clause (قال هذا ربي) is resumptive, and the clause (هذا ربي) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (فَلَمَّا أَفَلَ قالَ لا أُحِبُّ الْآفِلِينَ) (فلما): the fāʾ is a conjunction and (لما) is temporal or linking; the clause (أفل) is in the position of the genitive by annexation, or has no grammatical position; the clause (قال) is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and the clause (لا أحب الآفلين) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech. He said that only because change and movement are not possible for the Lord. (فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْقَمَرَ بازِغاً قالَ هذا رَبِّي) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (بازغا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing is visual; (هذا) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (ربي) its khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech; the clause (قال هذا ربي) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (فَلَمَّا أَفَلَ قالَ: لَئِنْ لَمْ يَهْدِنِي رَبِّي لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الضَّالِّينَ) The lām is the one preparing for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) is conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive; (يهدني) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم); the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (ربي) is the agent. The lām is that of the answer to the oath, and the clause (أكوننّ) is the answer to the oath, having no grammatical position. (من القوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of (أكونن), and (الضالين) is an adjective. (فَلَمَّا رَأَى الشَّمْسَ بازِغَةً قالَ: هذا رَبِّي هذا أَكْبَرُ) Its i'rab has been given. The mubtadaʾ was made to match the khabar [Translator's note: i.e. the masculine هذا], even though the reference is to the sun, because both express one and the same thing, and to protect the Lord from any suspicion of the feminine. Do you not see that they said in describing Him:
علّام, and did not say علّامة, even though علّامة is more intensive, guarding against the feminine marker? More of this discussion will come in the section on benefits. (فَلَمَّا أَفَلَتْ قالَ يا قَوْمِ إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ) (مما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (بريء); (ما) is maṣdariyya, i.e. "free of your associating"; it may also be a relative, i.e. "of that which you associate with Allah in His worship", the resumptive pronoun being omitted. It is to be observed that Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, argued against his people from the setting and not the rising, even though both convey a passing from one state to another, for a subtle secret: setting is a passing accompanied by concealment and obliteration, while rising is a passing accompanied by appearance, radiance and shining.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is the device of taʿrīḍ (oblique allusion), whose discussion has been given before; he was only alluding to their error.
It is to be observed that he alluded to their error in the matter of the moon because he had despaired of them in the matter of the star; and for this reason he openly declared, in the matter of the sun, his disavowal of it, by way of drawing the opponent on step by step and bringing him under the force of the proof.

* Benefits:
It was said: الشمس (the sun) is treated as masculine and as feminine. So it was made feminine first, according to the well-known usage, and masculine in the demonstrative according to the less common dialect, in consideration of and harmony with the khabar; thus the scale of the masculine — which is the less common — outweighed the feminine usage.

dervis-irab:79-80.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنِّي وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ حَنِيفاً وَما أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) Resumptive speech, brought for Ibrāhīm's, peace be upon him, declaration of his holding fast to guidance and the religion of truth. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (وجهت) is its khabar (predicate); (وجهي) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (للذي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (وجهت); the clause (فطر السموات والأرض) is the ṣila (relative clause); (السموات) is the direct object and (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); (حنيفا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the tāʾ in (وجهت). The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating (ما), which operates like (ليس); (أنا) is its noun, and (من المشركين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar. (وَحاجَّهُ قَوْمُهُ قالَ: أَتُحاجُّونِّي فِي اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدانِ) Resumptive speech, brought to mention the disputation between Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, and his people. It is narrated that when his mockery of the idols and his denunciation of them increased, his people disputed with him and wanted to establish the argument against him.
(حاجّه) is a past verb, the hāʾ is the direct object, and (قومه) is the fāʿil (agent). (قال) is a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause is resumptive. The hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (تحاجوني) is with a doubled nūn, by assimilation of the nūn of the nominative into the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), the original being أتحاجونني! (في الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تحاجوني). The wāw is circumstantial; (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (هدان) is a past verb; the nūn is for protection, and the yāʾ, omitted in the script, is the direct object — it may be dropped or retained in continuous recitation. The clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the yāʾ in (أتحاجّوني), i.e.:
"Do you dispute with me about Allah while I am guided by Him?" It may also be a ḥāl from (الله), i.e. "Do you dispute with me about Him while He is guiding me?" So your argument collapses from its foundation. (وَلا أَخافُ ما تُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ رَبِّي شَيْئاً) The wāw may be resumptive, the clause being resumptive: he, peace be upon him, informed them that he does not fear what they associate with Allah, out of trust in Him and reliance on His support and protection. It may also be a conjunction, so that it follows the clause «وقد هدان», i.e.:
in being accusative as a ḥāl. (ما) is a relative noun, the direct object; the pronoun in «به» refers back to «ما», and the meaning is: "and I do not fear that which you associate with Allah." (إلا) is a particle of exception, and the interpreted maṣdar from (أن) and the verb is a connected excepted (mustathnā muttaṣil), because it is of the same kind as the first, the thing excepted from being time. Al-Zamakhsharī supplied it with his words:
"except at the time of my Lord's willing something to be feared", the "time" being omitted. The exception may also be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), in which case «إلا» is in the sense of «لكن», since the will (of Allah) is not among the things they associate with Him. The interpreted maṣdar is then a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being:
"but my Lord's will — I fear it." (شيئا) is the direct object. (وَسِعَ رَبِّي كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً أَفَلا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ) The clause gives the reason for the exception and has no grammatical position. (وسع ربي) is a verb and its agent; (كل شيء) is the direct object; (علما) is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the agent, the implied form being "the knowledge of my Lord encompasses everything." The hamza is for disapproving interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; and (تتذكرون) is conjoined to an omitted element, i.e.:
"Do you turn away from reflecting that your gods are inanimate things that neither harm nor benefit, and so do not remember that they are of this standing?"

dervis-irab:81-82.t:
* I'rab:
(وَكَيْفَ أَخافُ ما أَشْرَكْتُمْ وَلا تَخافُونَ أَنَّكُمْ أَشْرَكْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ ما لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطاناً)
The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to negate fear on the part of the Prophet ﷺ. [Translator's note: so in the source; in context the speaker is Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him.] (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (أخاف) is an imperfect verb; (ما) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (أشركتم) is the ṣila (relative clause). (ما) may also be maṣdariyya, the interpreted maṣdar being the object of (أخاف). (ولا تخافون) is conjoined to (أخاف), and so falls within the scope of the disapproval. The wāw may also be circumstantial, so that the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "How should I fear that which you associate with Him, and your associating, while you yourselves are not afraid?" (أن) and its noun, and the clause (أشركتم بالله) is its khabar (predicate); (ما) is a relative noun, the direct object of (أشركتم); (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ينزل); (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of His word (سلطانا), and when it was placed first it was parsed as a ḥāl; and (سلطانا) is the direct object. (فَأَيُّ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ أَحَقُّ بِالْأَمْنِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ of eloquence, implying an omitted clause); (أي) is an interrogative particle, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أحق) its khabar. (إن) is conditional; (كان) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause (تعلمون) is its khabar. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes indicates it, i.e. "then tell me which of the two parties is more entitled to be followed?" [Translator's note: the verse has «بالأمن» "to security"; the source's paraphrase has «بالاتباع».] (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوا إِيمانَهُمْ بِظُلْمٍ) (الذين) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, on the basis that the speech is uttered by Ibrāhīm in answer to the question in his words (فأي الفريقين). It may also be a mubtadaʾ, on the basis that the speech is from Allah the Exalted. The clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila. (ولم): the wāw is a conjunction, and (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive; (يلبسوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم), conjoined to the ṣila; and (بظلم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يلبسوا). (أُولئِكَ لَهُمُ الْأَمْنُ وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (الأمن) is a second, delayed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. The demonstrative clause with what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative as the object of an omitted speech on the first view, or nominative as the khabar of (الذين) on the second view. The wāw is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (مهتدون) its khabar, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes.

dervis-irab:162-165.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النسك): with the ن taking any of the three vowels and the س vowelless, and with ḍamma on both the ن and the س; likewise النّسوك, النّسكة and المنسكة: asceticism, devotion and austerity. الناسك is the ascetic worshipper; its plural is نسّاك. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said:
صم ثمّ صلّ وطف بمكّة زائرا ... سبعين لا سبعا فلست بناسك
جهل الديانة من إذا عرضت له ... أطماعه لم يلف بالمتماسك
(Fast, then pray, and circle [the House] at Mecca as a visitor seventy times, not seven — still you are no ascetic. He is ignorant of religion who, when his cravings present themselves to him, is not found to hold firm.)
(خَلائِفَ الْأَرْضِ): the annexation is in the sense of «في» (in). الخلائف is the plural of خليفة, like صحيفة and صحائف, so it falls under the saying [of Ibn Mālik]:
والمدّ زيد ثالثا في الواحد ... همزا يرى في مثل كالقلائذ
(The long vowel added as the third letter in the singular is seen as a hamza [in the plural], as in القلائد.) [Translator's note: the source prints «كالقلائذ» with ذ, evidently for «كالقلائد».]
Mention of الخليفة has already been made in al-Baqara.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: إِنَّ صَلاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيايَ وَمَماتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) A resumption set forth to emphasise carrying out the fundamental and subsidiary laws. The clause إنّ and what follows it is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). إنّ and its noun; نسكي, محياي and مماتي are conjoined. The rule of the vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the first person will come in the Benefits section [Translator's note: so in the source, «المنادى المضاف»; the Benefits section actually discusses the noun annexed to the yāʾ of the first person in general, not the vocative specifically]. لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar (predicate); رب is an adjective, and العالمين is a muḍāf ilayhi [genitive by yāʾ] because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; this was discussed in al-Fātiḥa. (لا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَبِذلِكَ أُمِرْتُ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ) The lā of generic negation; شريك is its noun, and له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of رب العالمين or an adjective of it. The و is a conjunction, and بذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أمرت. وأنا: the و is also a conjunction, أنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أول المسلمين is its khabar. (قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِي رَبًّا) The clause is resumptive, set forth to be a [rejoinder] to the invitation of these unbelievers when they said to him: "Return to our religion and the worship of our gods." [Translator's note: the source has «بدا», evidently a misprint for «ردا» (a rejoinder).] The hamza is for interrogation containing the sense of negation, i.e. "I do not seek a lord other than Him". غير الله is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first, and ربا is a tamyīz (specification); it may also be parsed as a ḥāl. (وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ) The و is circumstantial; هو is a mubtadaʾ and رب كل شيء its khabar; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (وَلا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْها) The و is a conjunction, لا is negating, and تكسب كل نفس is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and muḍāf ilayhi. إلا is a particle of restriction, and عليها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "except in the state of its sin being over it, with what harms it and does not benefit it". (وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى) The و is also a conjunction and لا is also negating; تزر وازرة is an imperfect verb and agent, وزر is a direct object, and أخرى is a muḍāf ilayhi. (ثُمَّ إِلى رَبِّكُمْ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ) ثم is a conjunction; إلى ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar placed first, and مرجعكم is a mubtadaʾ placed after it. The ف is a conjunction; ينبئكم is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object. The ب is a preposition of cause, and ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the ب; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the second object. The clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; كان and its noun; فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تختلفون, and the clause تختلفون is the khabar of كنتم. (وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلائِفَ الْأَرْضِ) The و is a conjunction, هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar; the clause جعلكم is the ṣila, and خلائف الأرض is a second direct object of جعلكم. (وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجاتٍ) The و is a conjunction, رفع is a past verb, بعضكم is a direct object, فوق بعض is an adverb of place attached to رفع, and درجات is an adverb; its i'rab and the discussion of it have already been given. (لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي ما آتاكُمْ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ الْعِقابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The لام is causal, and يبلوكم is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the لام; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to رفع. فيما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يبلوكم, and the clause آتاكم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. إنّ and its noun, and سريع العقاب is its khabar; the clause is resumptive, giving the reason. وإنه لغفور رحيم is conjoined to what preceded; the i'rab of that has been given many times.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ورفع بعضكم فوق بعض درجات» there is kināya (metonymy) for nobility and merit. This disparity does not arise from inability to make them equal, but is for trial and testing.

* Benefits:
The noun annexed to the yāʾ of the first person:
The last letter of a noun annexed to the yāʾ of the first person must take kasra to suit the yāʾ, and the yāʾ may take fatḥa or be vowelless. Excepted from this are the maqṣūr noun (ending in alif), the manqūṣ noun (ending in yāʾ), the dual and the sound masculine plural: in these four the last letter must be vowelless and the yāʾ with them must take fatḥa. He said in al-Khulāṣa:
آخر ما يضاف للياء اكسر إذا ... لم يك معتلا كرام وقذى
أو يك كابنين وزيدين ففي ... جميعها اليا بعد فتحها احتذي
(Put kasra on the end of what is annexed to the yāʾ, unless it is weak-ended like رام and قذى, or is like ابنين and زيدين; in all of these the yāʾ follows with fatḥa.)
Its being vowelless after the alif is rare.
An attack on Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī:
Nāfiʿ read محياي ومماتي, in continuous recitation, with the yāʾ of «محياي» vowelless, just as its taking kasra after the alif is rare: al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «هي عصاي» with kasra on the yāʾ, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two vowelless letters. The kasra is regular in the dialect of Banū Yarbūʿ in the yāʾ to which a sound masculine plural is annexed, and on this is the reading of Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash: «وما أنتم بمصرخيّ» with kasra on the yāʾ. Thereby what al-Maʿarrī said in his Epistle falls away: «The masters of Arabic have agreed in disliking the reading of Ḥamza.» Ibn Hishām refuted him and said: «Al-Maʿarrī had an aim of attacking Islam; perhaps those who read with kasra, their dialect has the yāʾ of annexation vowelless, so two vowelless letters met for them.» Al-Murādī said in Sharḥ al-Tashīl: «Al-Maʿarrī was not alone in what he said in his Epistle; what Ibn Hishām said is unfair to him, even though he was accused of heresy.»

Between Abū al-ʿAlāʾ and the grammarians:
We consider it useful to present this dispute that broke out between Abū al-ʿAlāʾ and the grammarians. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ was a grammarian, but he did not want to be a grammarian. He was one of the leading authorities of grammar, but the method of grammar did not satisfy him, so he criticised them bitterly, mocked their leader Sībawayh, and attacked him with criticism and charges of error in places in his epistles, for which there is no room in our book, so we have sufficed with a reference. More of this dispute will come in this book.

dervis-irab:28-29.t:
* I'rab:
(بَلْ بَدا لَهُمْ ما كانُوا يُخْفُونَ مِنْ قَبْلُ): (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction, the digression here being intended to nullify the speech of the disbelievers. (بدا) is a past verb; (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بدا); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of (بدا); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يخفون) is the khabar (predicate) of (كانوا); and (من قبل) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يخفون).
(وَلَوْ رُدُّوا لَعادُوا لِما نُهُوا عَنْهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لو) is conditional; (ردوا) is a past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the lām occurs in the apodosis of (لو); the clause (لعادوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (لما): the lām is a preposition, and (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the lām, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (عادوا); the clause (نهوا عنه) is the ṣila, and the preposition and its genitive noun [(عنه)] are attached to (نهوا).
(وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (كاذبون) is the khabar of (إن).
(وَقالُوا: إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا حَياتُنَا الدُّنْيا وَما نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ): the wāw may be a conjunction to the clause (عادوا), so that the clause falls within the scope of the apodosis, or to His words «وإنهم لكاذبون»; and it may be resumptive. (إن) is negative; (هي) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (حياتنا) is the khabar and (الدنيا) an adjective. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī mā, which governs as (ليس) does; (نحن) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and (مبعوثين) is genitive in wording and, by position, the khabar of the Ḥijāzī «ما».

dervis-irab:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ تَرى إِذْ وُقِفُوا عَلى رَبِّهِمْ): the wāw is resumptive; (لو) is conditional; (ترى) is an imperfect verb and it is the protasis of (لو); its apodosis is omitted because the meaning is understood, the implied form being: "you would have seen something tremendous". «ترى» may be visual, its object omitted, and it may be mental; the meaning then is: if you turned [Translator's note: the source prints «حرفت», evidently for «صرفت»] your heart and thought to contemplate their states and grasp the reality of their affair at that time, you would increase in certainty. (إذ) is an adverb for the past, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترى); the clause (وقفوا) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (على ربهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (وقفوا).
(قالَ: أَلَيْسَ هذا بِالْحَقِّ): the clause is resumptive, brought as the answer to an implied question, its implied form being: "What did their Lord say to them when they were made to stand before Him?" It may also be circumstantial, the one to whom the ḥāl (circumstantial) refers being «ربهم», as though it were said: "they were made to stand before Him while He said to them: Is this not the truth?" The hamza is for rebuking, disapproving interrogation; (ليس) is a defective past verb; (هذا) is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and (الحق) is genitive by the bāʾ in wording and accusative by position as the khabar (predicate) of (ليس).
(قالُوا: بَلى وَرَبِّنا): a resumptive statement brought to confirm their admission with an oath. (بلى) is a particle of answer for affirming [after] a negation. (وربنا): the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive; (ربنا) is genitive by the wāw of oath, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "we swear".
(قالَ: فَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ): a resumptive clause brought to explain what He said to them. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ, i.e. "since you knew this and then deviated from what it required, taste the punishment". (العذاب) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (ذوقوا); the bāʾ is a preposition; (ما) is a relative or maṣdariyya, i.e. "for that which you used to…" or "for your having disbelieved"; (كان) and its noun; and the clause (تكفرون) is the khabar of (كنتم).

* Rhetoric:
The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya) in His words «فذوقوا العذاب»; discussion of it has preceded, so renew your acquaintance with it — and may Allah protect you.

dervis-irab:31-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَوْزارَهُمْ): al-awzār is the plural of wizr, with kasra on the wāw, which is a heavy load. Al-wizr originally means weight; from it comes wazartuhu, and the king's wazīr (minister) is from this, because he bears the burdens of the affairs of the subjects entrusted to him. From it also come awzār al-ḥarb (the burdens of war) for its weapons, equipment and instruments. Al-Aʿshā said:
وأعددت للحرب أوزارها ... رماحا طوالًا وخيلًا ذكورا
(I prepared for war its burdens: long spears and stallion horses.)
And "the war laid down its burdens", i.e. its loads — a kināya (metonymy) for its ceasing.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقاءِ اللَّهِ): a resumptive statement brought to explain the fate of these whose sayings have been related. (قد) is a particle of verification; (خسر) is a past verb; (الذين) is a relative noun, its fāʿil (agent); the clause (كذبوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (بلقاء الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كذبوا).
(حَتَّى إِذا جاءَتْهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً): it was stated a little earlier that «حتى» in a construction like this may be the limit of the denial, not of the loss, or inceptive. (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the sense of condition, and the clause (جاءتهم الساعة) is in the position of the genitive by annexation. (بغتة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). Sībawayh said: it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl; and he said: it is not permissible to make analogies on it, so one does not say "جاء فلان سرعة" (so-and-so came speed).
(قالُوا: يا حَسْرَتَنا عَلى ما فَرَّطْنا فِيها): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (يا) is a vocative particle; (حسرتنا) is an annexed one addressed (munādā muḍāf); (على ما فرطنا) is attached to (الحسرة); and the clause (فرطنا فيها) is the ṣila of «ما».
(وَهُمْ يَحْمِلُونَ أَوْزارَهُمْ عَلى ظُهُورِهِمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يحملون) is the khabar (predicate); and (على ظهورهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يحملون).
(أَلا ساءَ ما يَزِرُونَ): (ألا) is a particle of drawing attention; (ساء) is a past verb for expressing dispraise; (ما) is a complete indefinite noun, accusative as a tamyīz (specification), or a relative noun as the fāʿil; and the clause (يزرون) is an adjective on the first view and the ṣila on the second.

* Rhetoric:
1- The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): sins are likened to heavy burdens; then the thing likened is omitted and the thing it is likened to retained.
2- The device of conjunction (al-muqārana): two kinds of the devices of badīʿ are joined together in the speech, namely al-tankīt (the pointed subtlety) and al-mubālagha (hyperbole). For someone may ask: what is the subtle point that gave preference to specifying the backs for carrying, rather than the heads? The answer is that the subtle point in this is the indication of the heaviness of the burdens, because backs bear weight better than heads. What follows from mentioning the backs — the inability of the heads to carry these burdens — namely the hyperbole in their heaviness, is joined to the tankīt. And around this conjunction there is the paired paronomasia (tajnīs al-muzāwaja) in His words, Exalted is He, «أوزارهم» before «على ظهورهم», and «يزرون» after it; and the reinforcement (tarshīḥ) of this paronomasia to establish the verse-ending through al-taṣdīr (anticipation); and the joining of the tarshīḥ with the taṣdīr.

A poetic example:
Among examples of this device in poetry is the saying of Idrīs ibn al-Yamān:
وكنت إذا استنزلت من جانب الرضا ... نزلت نزول الغيث في البلد المحل
وإن هيّج الأعداء منك حفيظة ... وقعت وقوع النار في الحطب الجزل
(When you were asked to come down on the side of goodwill, you came down as the rain comes down on a barren land; and if enemies stirred your wrath, you fell as fire falls on thick firewood.)
For the poet joined in the line the metaphor in his words «نزلت نزول الغيث» with the simile. He borrowed "coming down" for the one praised, because the reality of what he meant is: when your goodwill was sought, you were pleased. As for the simile, it is in his words «نزول الغيث», for the implied form is: "you came down with a coming down like the coming down of the rain". He joined the paronomasia of difference (tajnīs al-taghāyur) in his words «نزلت نزول الغيث» — the first word being a verb and the second a noun — with the tarshīḥ, for by that paronomasia he reinforced it for al-īghāl (pressing the point to the end). The hyperbole came embedded in the simile, since he likened his coming down to the coming down of the rain. In the second line he joined the metaphor in his words «وقعت» with the simile in the expression «وقوع النار», and embedded the hyperbole in this simile, since his words «وقعت وقوع النار» are hyperbole; and he embedded [it] in the paronomasia of difference in the two words «وقعت» and «وقوع», and the tarshīḥ for al-īghāl.
And beautiful is the conjunction in the saying of Tamīm ibn Muqbil:
لدن غدوة حتى نزعنا عشيّة ... وقد مات شطر الشمس والشطر مدنف
(From morning until we drew back at evening, when half of the sun had died and the other half was mortally ill.)
For in this line he joined al-irdāf (expression by a consequent) and metaphor: he expressed sunset by the death of half the sun at the start of the second hemistich, and this is the irdāf; and he borrowed for the other half al-danaf, which is severe illness. This is very eloquent, since the conjunction came in the second hemistich of the line alone.

dervis-irab:83-87.t:
* I'rab:
(وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنا آتَيْناها إِبْراهِيمَ عَلى قَوْمِهِ) Resumptive speech, brought to point to the proofs mentioned earlier and the prophets through whose hands they were sent down [Translator's note: so literally in the source: «والأنبياء التي أنزلت على أيديهم»]. (تلك):
a demonstrative, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (حجتنا) its khabar (predicate); the clause (آتيناها) is a second khabar or a ḥāl (circumstantial), the governor of the ḥāl being the meaning of the demonstrative. (آتيناها) is a verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إبراهيم) is the second object; and (على قومه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, or to (حجتنا). (نَرْفَعُ دَرَجاتٍ مَنْ نَشاءُ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ) The clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; Abū al-Baqāʾ parsed it as a ḥāl from the agent of (آتيناها), i.e. "while We are raising". (درجات) is a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial); (من) is a relative noun, the direct object; the clause (نشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause). The meaning is: "We raise whom We will in degrees", i.e.:
ranks. (إن) with its noun and its two khabars; the clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position. (وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ إِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ كُلًّا هَدَيْنا) The wāw conjoins to His words (وتلك حجتنا); there is no dispute about the permissibility of conjoining a verbal clause and a nominal clause to each other. (وهبنا) is a verb and its agent; (إسحق) is the direct object and (يعقوب) is conjoined to (إسحق); (كلا) is a fronted direct object of (هدينا); (هدينا) is a verb and its agent, and the clause is conjoined to (وهبنا). (وَنُوحاً هَدَيْنا مِنْ قَبْلُ) (نوحا) is a fronted object of (هدينا), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes; (من قبل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (هدينا). (قبل) is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, i.e. "before Ibrāhīm". (وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِهِ داوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُوسُفَ وَمُوسى وَهارُونَ وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (من ذريته) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "and We guided Dāwūd, Sulaymān" and so on to the last of the prophets He mentioned, "while they were of his offspring." So the whole of the fourteen prophets after Nūḥ are accusative by the verb of guiding which made «نوحا» accusative. The wāw is resumptive; (كذلك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (نجزي) is an imperfect verb, and (المحسنين) is the direct object. (وَزَكَرِيَّا وَيَحْيى وَعِيسى وَإِلْياسَ كُلٌّ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (كل) is a mubtadaʾ, and it was permissible to begin with it because of the meaning of generality in it; the tanwīn in (كل) is a substitute for a word, i.e. "each one". (من الصالحين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar. (وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَيُونُسَ وَلُوطاً وَكلًّا فَضَّلْنا عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ)
(كلّا) is a fronted direct object of (فضلنا), and (على العالمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (فضلنا). (وَمِنْ آبائِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ وَإِخْوانِهِمْ وَاجْتَبَيْناهُمْ) i.e. "and We guided some of their fathers." (اجتبيناهم) is a verb, an agent and a direct object, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes. (وَهَدَيْناهُمْ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; the guiding was repeated to repeat the emphasis and as a preparation for explaining that to which they were guided. (إلى صراط) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (هديناهم), and (مستقيم) is an adjective.

dervis-irab:88-90.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ هُدَى اللَّهِ يَهْدِي بِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ) Resumptive speech, brought to explain what was pointed to, which is either the choosing (al-ijtibāʾ) or the guidance. (ذلك) is a demonstrative, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (هدى الله) the khabar (predicate); the clause (يهدي) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a second khabar. (هدى الله) may also be parsed as a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative, with the clause (يهدي) as the khabar. (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يهدي); (من) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (من عباده) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the relative noun. (وَلَوْ أَشْرَكُوا لَحَبِطَ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is circumstantial; (لو) is conditional; (أشركوا) is a verb and its agent, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause (حبط) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (عنهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (حبط); (ما) is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; and the clause (يعملون) is the khabar of (كانوا). (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ) The clause is resumptive. (أولئك) is a demonstrative, the mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the eighteen prophets mentioned, and (الذين) is the khabar of the demonstrative; the clause (آتيناهم) is the ṣila; (الكتاب) is the second direct object, and what follows is conjoined to it. (فَإِنْ يَكْفُرْ بِها هؤُلاءِ فَقَدْ وَكَّلْنا بِها قَوْماً لَيْسُوا بِها بِكافِرِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (إن) is conditional; (يكفر) is the protasis; (بها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يكفر); (هؤلاء) is the agent, the reference being to the people of Mecca to whose guidance Muḥammad, upon him be blessing and peace, was sent. (فقد): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (وكلنا) is a verb and its agent; (بها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (وكلنا); (قوما) is the direct object; the clause (ليسوا) is an adjective; (بها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كافرين); the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (كافرين) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ليسوا). (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ) The clause is resumptive. (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ, i.e. the prophets mentioned, and (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as the khabar; the clause (هدى الله) is the ṣila. (فبهداهم): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ of eloquence, implying an omitted condition), i.e. "if you wish to follow the upright path and rise to the loftiest of responsibilities, then follow their guidance" — Allah gathered for him the great distinctive qualities of the prophets that had been distributed among them. (اقتد) is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and the hāʾ is the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt), whose discussion has been given before. The clause occurring after the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa is the apodosis of a condition and has no grammatical position. (قُلْ: لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرى لِلْعالَمِينَ)
The clause (قل) is resumptive, and the clause (لا أسألكم) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the pronoun in «عليه» refers back to the conveying (of the message) understood from the context of the speech. (أجرا) is the second direct object of (أسألكم). (إن) is negating; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ذكرى) is the khabar; and (للعالمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective. The clause (إن هو إلا ذكرى) is resumptive.

dervis-irab:91-91.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ) Resumptive speech, brought to answer the Jews who said what follows, in keeping with their ingrained nature of obstinacy and quarrelling. (ما) is negating; (قدروا الله) is a verb, its agent and its object; (حق قدره) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the original being قدره الحقّ ("its true estimation"), the adjective then being annexed to the noun it qualifies. One says قدر الشيء when one probes it and gauges it in order to know its measure and extent; it was then used of describing a thing. (إِذْ قالُوا: ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلى بَشَرٍ مِنْ شَيْءٍ) (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to (قدروا), and the clause (قالوا) is in the position of the genitive by annexation. Those who said it are the Jews, so there was no escape from binding them to what they could not avoid acknowledging, namely the sending down of the Torah upon Mūsā; and included in binding them is rebuking them, heaping blame upon them, and branding them with excessive stupidity and reckless ignorance. The clause (ما أنزل الله) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (شيء) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (قُلْ مَنْ أَنْزَلَ الْكِتابَ الَّذِي جاءَ بِهِ مُوسى نُوراً وَهُدىً لِلنَّاسِ) The clause is resumptive, brought to answer them and cast them into the depths of abasement. (من) is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (أنزل الكتاب) is the khabar (predicate); (الذي) is a relative noun, an adjective of (الكتاب); the clause (جاء به موسى) is the ṣila (relative clause); (نورا) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (هدى) is conjoined to (نورا); and (للناس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of (هدى). (تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَراطِيسَ تُبْدُونَها وَتُخْفُونَ كَثِيراً) The clause is a ḥāl from (الكتاب), or from the pronoun in (به). (تجعلونه) is a verb, an agent and a first direct object, and (قراطيس) is the second direct object: they treated it as mere sheets of paper. What was said about القرطاس has been given before. The clause (تبدونها) is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of «قراطيس»; the clause (وتخفون كثيرا) is conjoined to the clause (تبدونها), and (كثيرا) is the direct object of «تخفون». (وَعُلِّمْتُمْ ما لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا أَنْتُمْ وَلا آباؤُكُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause (علمتم) is conjoined to the clause (تجعلونه) within the domain of the ḥāl. (علمتم) is a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the second direct object; the clause (لم تعلموا) is the ṣila; (أنتم) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the agent, which is the wāw in «لم تعلموا». (ولا): the wāw is a conjunction, and (آباؤكم) is conjoined to his word «أنتم». (قُلِ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ) The clause is resumptive, brought to continue answering them. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "Allah sent it down" or "it is Allah". (ثم) is a conjunction; (ذرهم) is an imperative verb whose past tense the Arabs let die out; (في خوضهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ذرهم), or to (يلعبون), or to an omitted ḥāl; and the clause (يلعبون) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the object of (ذرهم).

dervis-irab:32-33.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلَّا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to affirm what lies beyond nature, that there is another life, and to make clear the reality of those two lives. (ما) is negative; (الحياة) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الدنيا) an adjective; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (لعب) is the khabar (predicate) of (الحياة); and (لهو) is conjoined to (لعب).
(وَلَلدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; the lām is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (الدار) is a mubtadaʾ and (الآخرة) an adjective; (خير) is the khabar; (للذين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خير); the clause (يتقون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). You may also make the wāw resumptive, so that the clause is resumptive, brought to complete the explanation of the state of the two lives. The hamza is for disapproving interrogation, entering upon an implied element; the fāʾ is a conjunction and what it is conjoined to is omitted, the implied form being: "Are you heedless, so that you do not reason?" And the interrogative clause is resumptive.
(قَدْ نَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ الَّذِي يَقُولُونَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to console the Messenger ﷺ. (قد) originally indicates paucity, but here multitude is intended; the explanation of that will come under Rhetoric. (نعلم) is an imperfect verb taking two objects, and what follows it stands in their place, for it is suspended from governing by the lām of commencement; the hamza of (إن) takes kasra because the lām enters its scope. (إنه) is (إن) and its noun; the clause (يحزنك) is the khabar of (إن); (الذي) is the fāʿil (agent) of (يحزنك); and the clause (يقولون) is the ṣila.
(فَإِنَّهُمْ لا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ وَلكِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ): the fāʾ is causal; (إن) and its noun; (لا) is negative; and the clause (لا يكذبونك) is its khabar. (ولكن): the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction; (لكن) and its noun; (بآيات الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يجحدون); and the clause (يجحدون) is the khabar of (لكن).

* Rhetoric:
In the second verse there are two kinds of rhetoric:
1- Reverting to the opposite in what has reached the utmost limit. This is one of the customs and subtleties of the Arabs: they call a woman excessive in her beauty "ugly", and they express a thing by its opposite. Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī glanced at the heaven of this eloquence in his saying:
ولجدت حتى كدت تبخل حائلا ... للمنتهى ومن السرور بكاء
(You were so generous that you almost turned miserly, veering at the limit — and of joy there is weeping.)
He means that you reached the furthest limit in generosity and sought something else beyond it, but did not find it, so you almost turned — i.e. went back — from the end of what you had arrived at, since it is not your way to stop at a limit in generosity after reaching its limit. This is among the finest of speech: i.e. when a person reaches the utmost in generosity, he almost returns to miserliness.
And in the verse the expression is with «قد», which indicates paucity when it enters an imperfect verb, as an alert to the increase of the action; what is meant by the abundance of His knowledge, Exalted is He, is the abundance of its objects. Much of this will come in this book.
2- He put the overt noun in place of the pronoun in His words «ولكن الظالمين», whereas the standard rule for the overt noun requires it to be a pronoun; but He departed from the standard rule to dwell at length on their dispraise, and to state explicitly the word "injustice" and name them by it, so that it becomes a mark by which they are distinguished, as a further emphasis of their dispraise.

dervis-irab:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to console him ﷺ. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (كذبت) is a passive past verb, the tāʾ being the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; (رسل) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (من قبلك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of (رسل).
(فَصَبَرُوا عَلى ما كُذِّبُوا وَأُوذُوا حَتَّى أَتاهُمْ نَصْرُنا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (صبروا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), conjoined to (كذبت); «على ما» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (صبروا), and «ما» is maṣdariyya, interpreted with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "upon their being denied"; (أوذوا) is conjoined to «صبروا». (حتى) may be of limit — and perhaps this is more likely here — and it may be inceptive. (أتاهم نصرنا) is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a delayed fāʿil.
(وَلا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِماتِ اللَّهِ وَلَقَدْ جاءَكَ مِنْ نَبَإِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (لا) is the lā of generic negation, and (مبدل) is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; (لكلمات الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). The wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (جاءك) is a verb and its mafʿūl bihi. The fāʿil of (جاءك) is problematic. What appears is that the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element which is an adjective of the fāʿil, standing in its place, i.e. "some of their tidings came to you" or "more of their tidings and stories". The preposition and its genitive noun may also be attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil latent in (جاء), the referent being what is understood from the preceding clause, i.e. "and this report has come to you, being of the tidings of the messengers". The first is easier and further from strained reasoning.

* Rhetoric:
The splendid shift (iltifāt) from the third-person pronoun to the first-person pronoun in His words, Exalted is He: «حتى أتاهم نصرنا», since before it is: «بآيات الله يجحدون». Had the speech run on its pattern, it would have been said: "His help". The benefit of this shift — in addition to refreshing and varying the speech — is ascribing the help to the first-person pronoun, which conveys majesty, and the incentive to the obligation of persevering in striving, struggle and steadfastness in the path of achieving the great aspiration and delivering the lofty, ideal message.

dervis-irab:35-35.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَفَقاً): al-nafaq is a passage underground with an exit to a known place; from it comes the railway tunnel (nafaq al-sikka al-ḥadīdiyya). The discussion of this root has preceded in full.
(السلم): it is the means of ascent; it has been said: it is a staircase; and it has been said: it is any means whatsoever. The Arabs say: "Take me as a sullam for your need", i.e. a means. It is derived from salāma (safety), because safety is decreed for the one who ascends by it. The more eloquent usage is to make it masculine; al-Farrāʾ related its feminine use from the Arabs.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ كانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكَ إِعْراضُهُمْ): a resumptive statement brought to affirm the obligation of his patience ﷺ. (إن) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the noun of (كان) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause (كبر عليك إعراضهم) is the khabar (predicate); (عليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كبر); and (إعراضهم) is the fāʿil (agent).
(فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي الْأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي السَّماءِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (إن) is conditional as well; (استطعت) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then do it". The meaning: if you are able to find an opening under the earth through which you pass and so emerge to them with a sign, or a ladder by which you climb up to heaven and come down from it with a sign, then do it. (أن تبتغي) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as the object of (استطعت). The second condition with its apodosis is the apodosis of the first condition. (في الأرض) is an adjective of «نفقا», and (في السماء) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of «سلما».
(فَتَأْتِيَهُمْ بِآيَةٍ وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَمَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْهُدى): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تأتيهم) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (تبتغي). The wāw is resumptive; (لو) is conditional; (شاء الله) is a verb and its fāʿil; the lām occurs in the apodosis of (لو); and the clause (جمعهم على الهدى) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(فَلا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ, i.e. "since you know this, then do not be"; (لا) is prohibitive; (تكونن) is a defective imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive by «لا»; and (من الجاهلين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of (تكونن).

dervis-irab:36-38.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّما يَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ وَالْمَوْتى يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ): a resumptive statement brought to affirm that their failure to respond arises from the presence of coverings on their hearts and heaviness in their ears, because they are reckoned among the living while in reality they are dead. (إنما) is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; (يستجيب) is a nominative imperfect verb; (الذين) is its fāʿil (agent); and the clause (يسمعون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, having no grammatical position. (والموتى): the wāw may be resumptive, with (الموتى) a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (يبعثهم الله) its khabar (predicate); and the wāw may be a conjunction, with (الموتى) accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), by an implied verb explained by the overt noun after it, so that the clause (يبعثهم الله) is explicative, having no grammatical position. Perhaps this view is preferable, so that the construction is harmonious. (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يرجعون); and (يرجعون) is an imperfect verb conjoined to the clause (يبعثهم).
(وَقالُوا: لَوْلا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ): the wāw is resumptive; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, to relate another of the kinds of their crimes. (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (نزل) is a passive past verb; (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نزل); (آية) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (من ربه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of (آية); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of their speech.
(قُلْ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ قادِرٌ عَلى أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ آيَةً): the clause is resumptive, brought to indicate their excess in obstinacy and their persistence in corruption despite the succession and continuity of signs. (إن) with its noun and khabar; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (على) is a preposition, and (أن) with what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by (على), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (قادر); and (آية) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (ينزل).
(وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (لكن) and its noun; (لا) is negative; the clause (يعلمون) is its khabar; and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَما مِنْ دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا طائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَناحَيْهِ): a resumptive statement brought to explain His power, knowledge and governance, Exalted is He. (ما) is negative; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (دابة) is a noun genitive by (من) in wording and nominative by position as a mubtadaʾ; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of (دابة); the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; (طائر) is a noun conjoined to (دابة); and the clause (يطير بجناحيه) is an adjective of (طائر). Further discussion of this verse will come under Rhetoric.
(إِلَّا أُمَمٌ أَمْثالُكُمْ): (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أمم) is the khabar of (دابة); and (أمثالكم) is an adjective of (أمم).
(ما فَرَّطْنا فِي الْكِتابِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ثُمَّ إِلى رَبِّهِمْ يُحْشَرُونَ): (ما) is negative; (فرطنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (في الكتاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فرطنا); (من) is a redundant preposition; and (شيء) is genitive in wording and accusative by position, as a maṣdar or as an object. The clause (ما فرطنا) is resumptive; further parsing of this statement will come under Benefits. (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (إلى ربهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يحشرون); and (يحشرون) is an imperfect verb conjoined to what preceded.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «يطير بجناحيه» there is the device of al-infiṣāl (extrication from an objection), for increased generality and comprehensiveness. For someone may say: the clause in His words, Exalted is He, «يطير بجناحيه» apparently has no benefit in being brought, since every bird flies with its two wings, and this is reporting something known. The extrication from that is to say: He, Glorified is He, wished to embed in this report the prohibition of killing, in vain, an animal that does no harm, as indicated by His words «إلا أمم أمثالكم»; for in His equating these with those who are morally responsible there is an indication that a person will be held to account for what he does with every body capable of life. Among the creatures of the earth there are those whose killer incurs no blame, such as flies, mosquitoes, ants, scorpions, dung beetles and all the other vermin. So He wished to specify this kind of this species — and it is the noblest of its kinds, the one whose subjection Allah, Glorified is He, bestowed as a favour upon His Prophet Dāwūd, peace be upon him, and whose speech He taught to his son Sulaymān. Concerning it the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, stating explicitly that a person will be held to account for it: "Whoever kills a sparrow in vain…" (the ḥadīth). So He specified this kind with an attribute distinguishing it from the rest of the kinds, saying «يطير بجناحيه», because the word "wing" is not applied in its literal sense except to the limb which has no [Translator's note: so in the source, «ليس له»; the sense of the argument appears to require "which has"] feathers, quills, primaries, coverts and flight feathers — so that it may be inferred from this kind among all kinds of birds being the one intended by the prohibition of killing and tormenting it, that what is meant by the creature (الدابة) mentioned at the start of the verse is the noble kind among the kinds of creatures, so that insects are excluded from that species, just as vermin were excluded from the species of birds by distinguishing the kind indicated from it. He sufficed with specifying the second rather than specifying the first, knowing that one acquainted with the ordering of the composition of speech will infer the first of it by analogy with the second. In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Rights will surely be rendered to those entitled to them on the Day of Resurrection, even to the point that retaliation is taken for the hornless sheep from the horned sheep."

* Benefits:
Is «من» added redundantly with the rest of the objects? The answer is that it is not added with the mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), the mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or the mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial). The reason for the prohibition of adding it is that these are in meaning equivalent to what is made genitive by annexation, by the lām and by (في), and «من» does not combine with them. But no reason for the prohibition appears in the case of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and Abū al-Baqāʾ explained on this basis His words, Exalted is He, «ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء». He said: (من) is redundant and (شيء) is in the place of the maṣdar, i.e. "any neglect"; the thing described was omitted and its adjective put in its place, then «من» was added. He said: it cannot be a mafʿūl bihi, because «فرّط» is made transitive to it only with «في», and it has been made transitive with it to (الكتاب). He said: on this basis there is no proof in the verse for whoever thinks that the Book contains the mention of everything explicitly. The reply to these who think so is that this is not granted unless «من شيء» is a mafʿūl bihi, because the meaning then is: "We did not neglect", i.e. "We did not leave out anything in the Book"; but if the object is made «في الكتاب» and His words «من شيء» are made a maṣdar, i.e. "We did not neglect the Book [in any way]", then it gives no indication of that.
Ibn Hishām added, saying: "Likewise there is no proof in it even if «شيء» were a mafʿūl bihi, because what is meant by the Book is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ), as in His words, Exalted is He: «ولا رطب ولا يابس إلا في كتاب مبين»." This is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, and the context requires it.

dervis-irab:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا صُمٌّ وَبُكْمٌ فِي الظُّلُماتِ): the wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to explain the fate of the deniers. (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (كذبوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, having no grammatical position; (بآياتنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كذبوا); (صم) is the khabar (predicate); (بكم) is conjoined to (صم); and (في الظلمات) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second khabar. Abū al-Baqāʾ erred, thinking that the two are of the type «الرمان حلو حامض» (the pomegranate is sweet-sour), and so made the two words a single khabar. The matter is not so, because the difference between the two expressions is clear: the two words "sweet" and "sour" express a single meaning, namely "sweet-sour" (muzz), whereas (صم) and (بكم) each have their own meaning: deafness is the lack of hearing and dumbness is the lack of speech. More of this unique discussion will come.
(مَنْ يَشَأِ اللَّهُ يُضْلِلْهُ وَمَنْ يَشَأْ يَجْعَلْهُ عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ): a resumptive statement brought to affirm what preceded of their state. (من) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (يشأ) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and (يضلله) its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (ومن يشأ يجعله على صراط مستقيم) is conjoined to the preceding clause. The object of the willing in both verbs is omitted, and it is the content of the requital, i.e. "his misguidance" and "his guidance".

* Benefits:
The khabar may be multiple, as in: «زيد كاتب شاعر» (Zayd is a writer, a poet). It is not a case of multiple khabar what some have mentioned of their saying «الرّمان حلو حامض», because the meaning of the two khabars goes back to a single thing, since their meaning is "sweet-sour" (muzz).

dervis-irab:92-92.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُمَّ الْقُرى): Mecca was called "the Mother of the Towns" because it is the place of the first House set up for mankind, because it is the qibla of the people of the towns and the destination of their pilgrimage, and because it is the greatest of the towns in standing.
Al-Zamakhsharī recited, attributing it to one of those residing near (the Sanctuary) — and perhaps he means himself, as it is of his own composition:
فمن يلق في بعض القريّات رحله ... فأمّ القرى ملقى رحالي ومنتابي
(Whoever sets down his saddle in some little town — the Mother of the Towns is where my saddles are set down and where I return.)

* I'rab:
(وَهذا كِتابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ مُبارَكٌ مُصَدِّقُ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ) The wāw is resumptive; (هذا) is a demonstrative, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (كتاب) its khabar (predicate); the clause (أنزلناه) is in the position of the nominative as a first adjective of «كتاب», (مبارك) a second adjective, and (مصدق) a third adjective. (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation; the adverb is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause); and (يديه) is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَلِتُنْذِرَ أُمَّ الْقُرى وَمَنْ حَوْلَها) The wāw is a conjunction and the lām is for giving the reason (taʿlīl); (تنذر) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أنزلناه), i.e. "We sent it down for blessings, for confirming the books that preceded it" [and so that you warn]. (أم القرى) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من) is conjoined to (أم القرى), and (حولها) is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila. (وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَهُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; (الذين) is a relative noun, the mubtadaʾ; the clause (يؤمنون بالآخرة) is the ṣila, and the clause (يؤمنون به) is the khabar. The wāw may also be a conjunction, with (الذين) a relative noun conjoined to (أم القرى), i.e. "that you warn the people of the Mother of the Towns and that you warn those who believed"; the second clause (يؤمنون) is then a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun. The wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يحافظون) is the khabar, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
He brought the first adjective as a verbal clause, namely the clause (أنزلناه), because the sending down is renewed time after time, in the manner of the poet's words:
وقال رائدهم: أرسو نزاولها ... فحتف كل امرئ يجري بمقدار
(Their scout said: Drop anchor, let us contend with it — every man's death runs according to a set measure.)
The second adjective occurs as a noun, and likewise the third, to indicate permanence, continuity and the lastingness of the blessing.

dervis-irab:93-93.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غَمَراتِ الْمَوْتِ): its severities and its throes. الغمرات is the plural of غمرة, which is a terrible hardship, from غمره الماء when the water covers him. In al-Mukhtār: «غمره الماء, i.e. it rose above him; its pattern is نصر. الغمرة is hardship; the plural is غمر, like نوبة and نوب; and غمرات الموت are its severities.» Among the remarkable things in the derivation of these three letters — the ghayn, the mīm and the rāʾ — is that you can tie one meaning to their combinations, uniting those combinations and what is derived from them. These letters have six combinations: غمر, غرم, مرغ, مغر, رغم and رمغ, and one meaning unites them, namely covering, concealing, hiding and removing traces.
In the combination of ghayn and mīm as the first and second radicals there is the meaning of covering. You say سيف مغمود and مغمد, i.e. a sword placed in its sheath (غمده); تغمّده الله برحمته, i.e. Allah covered him (with His mercy). الغمز is well known; you say ما فيه مغمز ولا غميزة, i.e. (there is in him no) hidden, blameworthy matter; and له جارية غمّازة, i.e. a slave-girl good at massaging the limbs. غمسه في الماء فانغمس واغتمس, i.e. he hid it in it; غمس النجم غموسا, the star disappeared; and from it [Translator's note: the source reads «ومه», evidently for «ومنه»] comes اليمين الغموس (the immersing oath), because of its gravity. غمض الأمر: the matter was obscure; كلام غامض: unclear speech. غمط النعمة: he despised the blessing and was not grateful for it. And غمّ الشيء when he covered it.
(الْهُونِ): with ḍamma on the hāʾ; its maṣdars are هوان and هون, i.e. humiliation. When the Arabs intend by الهون the meaning of humiliation they put ḍamma on the hāʾ, and when they intend gentleness, ease and lightness of burden they put fatḥa on the hāʾ, saying: هو قليل هون المئونة (he is of light burden).

* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً) The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to mention some of those who falsely claimed prophethood in their error. (من) is an interrogative noun conveying the meaning of negation, i.e. "no one", in the position of the nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أظلم) is its khabar (predicate). (ممّن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أظلم); the clause (افترى) is the ṣila (relative clause); (على الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (افترى). (كذبا) may be the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb (افترى); or a maṣdar according to the meaning, i.e. "a fabrication", and thus a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (أَوْ قالَ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ) (أو) is a conjunction; (قال) is conjoined to (افترى); (أوحي) is a passive past verb; (إليّ), the preposition and its genitive noun, are in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (أوحي). The wāw is circumstantial, and the clause (لم يوح) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in «قال», or from the yāʾ in «إليّ»; (شيء) is the deputy agent of «يوح». (وَمَنْ قالَ: سَأُنْزِلُ مِثْلَ ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ) (أو) is a conjunction [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the verse is the wāw]. (من) is a relative noun conjoined to the noun in the genitive by «من», i.e. "than one who fabricated". The clause (سأنزل) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (مثل) may be accusative as the direct object, with (ما) a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation and the clause (أنزل الله) its ṣila; or it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being "I will send down a sending-down like what Allah sent down", in which case «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the clause (أنزل الله) has no grammatical position because it occurs after a particle-relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī). (وَلَوْ تَرى إِذِ الظَّالِمُونَ فِي غَمَراتِ الْمَوْتِ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ باسِطُوا أَيْدِيهِمْ) The wāw is resumptive; (لو) is conditional; (ترى) is an imperfect verb, the protasis of (لو), and the apodosis of (لو) is omitted, i.e.:
"you would have seen a tremendous thing." Parallels to this have been given before. The seeing is visual, and its object is omitted, i.e. "if you could see the wrongdoers when they are in the throes of death." (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to (ترى) [Translator's note: the source prints «بتري»]; (الظالمون) is a mubtadaʾ; (في غمرات الموت) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of «الظالمون»; the nominal clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. (والملائكة): the wāw is circumstantial; (الملائكة) is a mubtadaʾ and (باسطو) the khabar; (أيديهم) is muḍāf ilayhi, and it is a direct object in meaning. The clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the khabar, which is (في غمرات الموت). (أَخْرِجُوا أَنْفُسَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الْهُونِ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ) The clause (أخرجوا أنفسكم) is accusative by an implied speech, i.e. "they say to them in reproach and rebuke"; this speech is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the active participle, which is (باسطو). (أنفسكم) is the direct object; (اليوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (أخرجوا) or to (تجزون). The clause (تجزون) is resumptive; it is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent; (عذاب الهون) is the second direct object. (بما): the bāʾ is a preposition, and (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar in the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تجزون), i.e. "because of it". (كان) and its noun, and the clause (تقولون) is the khabar of (كنتم); (غير الحق) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "you say a saying other than the truth." (وَكُنْتُمْ عَنْ آياتِهِ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ) Conjoined to the first (كنتم), falling within the scope of the ṣila of the relative, which is (ما). (عن آياته) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تستكبرون), and the clause (تستكبرون) is the khabar of (كنتم).

* Rhetoric:
In His words «غمرات الموت» there is an explicit representational metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tamthīliyya): He borrowed the overwhelming of water for extreme hardship.

dervis-irab:94-94.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فُرادى): The scholars of language disagree about فرادى: is it a plural or not? Those who say it is a plural disagree about its singular. Al-Farrāʾ said: فرادى is the plural of فرد, فريد and فردان. Ibn Qutayba said: it is the plural of فردان, like سكران and سكارى, عجلان and عجالى. Some said: it is the plural of فريد, like رديف and ردافى, أسير and أسارى — al-Rāghib said this. It was also said: it is a quasi-plural noun (ism jamʿ), because فرد does not form the plural فرادى, and whoever said it is its plural means so only in meaning. The meaning of فرادى is "one by one".

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونا فُرادى كَما خَلَقْناكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ) The wāw is resumptive, and the lām is in answer to an omitted oath. (جئتمونا) is a verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is for lengthening the ḍamma of the mīm, which is the sign of the masculine plural. (فرادى) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the tāʾ, i.e. the agent of (جاء). In (كما خلقناكم), the kāf and its genitive — which is the interpreted maṣdar from maṣdariyya (ما) and the verb — may be in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a coming like your coming on the day We created you the first time"; or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of (جئتمونا). (أول مرة) is accusative as an adverb of time, governed by (خلقناكم). (مرة) is originally the maṣdar of مرّ يمرّ مرّة, and then its use was widened so that it became (an expression of) time. (وَتَرَكْتُمْ ما خَوَّلْناكُمْ وَراءَ ظُهُورِكُمْ) The wāw may be resumptive or circumstantial, so the clause is either resumptive with no grammatical position, or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of (جئتمونا), with (قد) implied. (تركتم) is a verb and its agent. (ترك) here may take a single object, being in the sense of leaving behind rather than making into; or it may be in the sense of making into, taking two objects, the first being relative «ما» and the second the adverb, which is then attached to an omitted element, i.e. "and by leaving, you made what We had bestowed on you to be behind your backs." On the first view the adverb is attached to (تركتم). (وَما نَرى مَعَكُمْ شُفَعاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّهُمْ فِيكُمْ شُرَكاءُ) The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (نرى) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (معكم) is an adverb of place attached to (نرى); (شفعاءكم) is the direct object, and (الذين) an adjective; the clause (زعمتم) is the ṣila (relative clause). (أن) with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of (زعم). (أن) and its noun; (فيكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (شركاء) and was placed before it; and (شركاء) is the khabar (predicate) of (أن). (لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْكُمْ ما كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ) The lām is in answer to an omitted oath, and (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). (تقطع) is a past verb whose agent is an implied pronoun referring to the connection indicated by the word «شركاء», since connection — i.e. linkage and attachment — is understood from it; the meaning is: "the connection between you has been cut." It was also read with the nominative (بينُكم), (بينكم) then being the agent, because it is a noun and not an adverb; it is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-aḍdād), used for union and for separation, i.e. "your union has been cut." (وضل): the wāw is a conjunction; (ضل) is a past verb; (عنكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ضل); (ما) is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila, and the clause (تزعمون) is the khabar of (كنتم). The two objects of (تزعمون) are omitted, the implied form being "you claimed them to be intercessors"; they were omitted because there is indication of them, in the manner of the words of al-Kumayt:
بأي كتاب أم بأية سنّة ... ترى حبهم عارا عليّ وتحسب
(By what Book, or by what Sunna, do you see love of them as a shame upon me, and reckon [it so]?)
i.e. "and reckon it a shame."

dervis-irab:40-41.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ): the statement is resumptive, brought to ask to be informed about their strange state. (أرأيتكم) is an expression that became widespread in their speech, and the views of the scholars and the parsers about it are many; you will see a useful summary under Benefits of what has been said about it. Briefly, it is as follows: the hamza is for interrogation; (رأى) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); and the kāf is a particle of address indicating the variation of the one addressed, while the tāʾ always has fatḥa in all its cases. The meaning of the statement is: "Tell me about your strange state." This has proceeded by way of figurative usage (majāz): since knowledge of a thing is a cause for reporting about it, and seeing it is a way to encompass it in knowledge and to the soundness of reporting about it, the form which is for seeking knowledge or seeking sight was used to seek a report, because they share in seeking. So there are two figurative usages in it: (رأى) in the sense of "knew" or "saw" [used] for reporting; and the use of the hamza, which is for seeking sight, to seek a report. Moreover, it does not follow from «أرأيت» being in the sense of «أخبرني» (tell me) that it is made transitive as that is, because (أخبرني) is made transitive with «عن», whereas (أرأيت) is made transitive to an explicit mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and to an interrogative clause in the place of the second object. The first object in this verse is omitted, its implied form being: «أرأيتم إياه» ("have you considered it"), i.e. the punishment; and the second is the interrogative clause, which is: «أغير الله تدعون».
(إِنْ أَتاكُمْ عَذابُ اللَّهِ أَوْ أَتَتْكُمُ السَّاعَةُ): (إن) is conditional; (أتاكم) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi; (عذاب الله) is the fāʿil; (أو) is a conjunction; and (أتتكم الساعة) is conjoined to (أتاكم). The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: «فمن تدعون» ("then whom would you call upon?"); and it has been said its implied form is: «فأخبروني عنه أتدعون غير الله لكشفه» ("then tell me about it: would you call upon other than Allah to remove it?").
(أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): the clause is resumptive; the hamza is for interrogation; (غير الله) is the fronted mafʿūl bihi of (تدعون); (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and (صادقين) is its khabar (predicate); and the apodosis of (إن) is omitted, i.e. "if you are truthful in that the idols benefit you, then call upon them".
