(بَلْ إِيَّاهُ تَدْعُونَ فَيَكْشِفُ ما تَدْعُونَ إِلَيْهِ إِنْ شاءَ وَتَنْسَوْنَ ما تُشْرِكُونَ): (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; (إياه) is a detached pronoun in the position of the accusative as the fronted mafʿūl bihi of (تدعون); (فيكشف) is conjoined to (تدعون); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the object of (يكشف); and the clause (تدعون إليه) is the ṣila (relative clause). The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (شاء) is the protasis; and the apodosis is omitted because the meaning is understood and what precedes indicates it. What is meant by it [Translator's note: i.e. «ما» in «ما تشركون»] is whatever is worshipped besides Allah in general, whether rational beings or others; and «غير الله» was made to predominate, as a further denunciation of them. (تنسون) is conjoined to (تدعون); (ما) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi; and the clause (تشركون) is the ṣila of «ما».

* Benefits:
(أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ): this tāʾ is among the strange matters in our language. That is, when «أرأيت» is meant in the sense of «أخبرني», the kāf of address may be attached to it [Translator's note: the source prints «تاء الخطاب» (the tāʾ of address), evidently for the kāf of address]. If it is not attached to it, the tāʾ must have what it must have with all other verbs — masculine and feminine, dual and plural — [but when it is attached, the variation passes to the kāf] away from what attaches to the tāʾ, the tāʾ keeping the form it has in addressing a single male. So if the address were to two it would be said: أرأيتكما; or to a plural: أرأيتكم; or to females: أرأيتكن. Thus the tāʾ keeps the fatḥa and is stripped of [indicating] the address, and the kāf in this is a particle of address having no place in i'rab. Sībawayh adduced as proof of that the saying of the Arabs: «أرأيتك فلانا ما حاله؟» (Tell me about so-and-so: what is his state?). But when «أرأيت» is not meant in the sense of "tell me", the tāʾ and the kāf together must have what each must have separately; so one says: أرأيتك قادرا, أرأيتكما قادرين, أرأيتكم قادرين, أرأيتكنّ قادرات, just as you say: أعلمتك قادرا.
Summary of the schools of thought on this expression:
Having established this, we say: the scholars disagreed on this verse in three views:

The first view:
The first object and the clause standing in place of the second object are both omitted because the meaning is understood; the implied form is: "Have you considered your worship of the idols — does it benefit you?" or "your taking other than Allah as a god — does it remove the punishment from you?" and the like. So "your worship" and "your taking" are the first object, the interrogative clause stands in place of the second, the tāʾ is the fāʿil, and the kāf is a particle of address.

The second view:
The condition and its apodosis stand in place of the two objects, because they have produced the intended meaning, so this verb did not need an object.

The third view:
The first object is omitted, and the question belongs to the topic of al-tanāzuʿ (two governors contending for one governed word) between (أرأيتكم) and (أتاكم), the word contended for being (العذاب).

dervis-irab:42-43.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا إِلى أُمَمٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): the oath clause is a resumptive statement brought to console him ﷺ. The wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (أرسلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (إلى أمم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا); (من قبلك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of (أمم); and the clause (قد أرسلنا) has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the omitted oath.
(فَأَخَذْناهُمْ بِالْبَأْساءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَضَرَّعُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أخذناهم) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is conjoined to an omitted element, its implied form being: "and they denied, so We seized them". (بالبأساء) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخذناهم); (الضراء) is conjoined to His words (بالبأساء); (لعل) and its noun; the clause (يتضرعون) is its khabar (predicate); and the clause of hope is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(فَلَوْلا إِذْ جاءَهُمْ بَأْسُنا تَضَرَّعُوا): the fāʾ is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to rebuke them and urge them to remorse, to frighten them of the outcome, and [to urge] seeking refuge in humble supplication to Him, Exalted is He. (ولولا) [Translator's note: the source names (لولا) here without parsing it; see Benefits, third use: a particle of rebuke] and (إذ) is an adverb for past time, attached to (تضرعوا); the clause (جاءهم) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; and (بأسنا) is the fāʿil of (تضرعوا) [Translator's note: so in the source; (بأسنا) is the fāʿil of (جاءهم), while the fāʿil of (تضرعوا) is the wāw].
(وَلكِنْ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (لكن) is lightened from the heavy form and inoperative, so it is merely for correction (istidrāk); (قست قلوبهم) is a past verb and its fāʿil; and the clause is a ḥāl, i.e. "the situation being that they persisted in their state of hardness and coarseness of nature". (زين) is a past verb; (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (زين); (الشيطان) is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined; (ما) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); the wāw is the noun of (كان) and the clause (يعملون) its khabar.

* Benefits:
(لولا) occurs in three ways:
1- A particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence: the condition is prevented due to the existence of the apodosis [Translator's note: so in the source; the usual formulation is that the apodosis is prevented due to the existence of the condition]. The noun after it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is obligatorily omitted, and the khabar must be general existence. But if it is restricted, like standing and sitting, it must be mentioned; for that reason they charged Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī with a grammatical error in his saying describing the sword:
يذيب الرّعب منه كلّ عضب ... فلولا الغمد يمسكه لسالا
(The dread of it melts every blade; were it not for the scabbard holding it, it would have flowed.)
It was answered on his behalf that the clause (يمسكه) is not a khabar but a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) of (الغمد), or a ḥāl. If a pronoun follows it, it should properly be a nominative pronoun, as in His words: «لولا أنتم لكنّا مؤمنين». It has been heard rarely: لولاي, لولاك and لولاه; it is then a preposition and is not attached to anything.
2- A particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) and of polite request (ʿarḍ); it is then specific to the imperfect or what is interpreted as it, as in: «لولا تستغفرون الله» and «لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب».
3- A particle of rebuke and of inducing regret; it is then specific to the past, as in this verse, and it is often accompanied by the adverbial (إذ) or (إذا), as in His words, Exalted is He: «فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم».
Further discussion of it will come in its places.

dervis-irab:44-45.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُبْلِسُونَ): silent with grief, bewildered, despairing.
(دابِرُ): al-dābir is the one who follows from behind, i.e. the last of them.

* I'rab:
(فَلَمَّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (لما) is adverbial; (نسوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause (نسوا) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (ذكروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ذكروا); (فتحنا) is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فتحنا); (أبواب) is a mafʿūl bihi; and (كل شيء) is muḍāf ilayhi.
(حَتَّى إِذا فَرِحُوا بِما أُوتُوا أَخَذْناهُمْ بَغْتَةً فَإِذا هُمْ مُبْلِسُونَ): (حتى) is inceptive or of limit; (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the sense of condition, attached to (أخذناهم); the clause (فرحوا) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فرحوا); the clause (أوتوا) is the ṣila of the relative noun, (أوتوا) being a passive past verb and the wāw its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause (أخذناهم), of verb, fāʿil and object, has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (بغتة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (فإذا): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (إذا) is the one of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya), and it is a particle according to what we have chosen; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (مبلسون) is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is resumptive.
(فَقُطِعَ دابِرُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (قطع) is a passive past verb; (دابر) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (القوم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of (القوم); and the clause (ظلموا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila. (والحمد): the wāw is resumptive; (الحمد) is a mubtadaʾ; (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; (رب) is a naʿt or badal (substitute); and (العالمين) is muḍāf ilayhi.

* Benefits:
(إذا of surprise) — there are three views about it:
1- The view of Sībawayh: that it is an adverb of place or of time.
2- The view of another group of the Basrans: that it is an adverb of time.
In both cases it is attached to the khabar, namely His words (مبلسون), i.e. they were struck silent with despair at the time or the place of their staying.
3- The view of the Kufans: that it is a particle, so it is not attached to anything. This is what we have chosen. Details about it will come in their places.

dervis-irab:95-96.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فالِقُ): active participle of فلق, i.e. he split the thing. Al-Rāghib restricted it [Translator's note: the source reads «وفيده», evidently «وقيّده»] to separating one part of it from another, i.e. He splits the grain for the plant: He splits the grain [Translator's note: the source reads «الجبة», evidently «الحبة»] and green leaves come out of it, and He splits the dry date-stone and a tree comes out of it rising into the air. The difference between الحب and النوى is well known: the first is like wheat and barley, the second like (the stones of) peaches and apricots.
(تُؤْفَكُونَ): you are turned away, i.e. how are you turned away from faith?
(الْإِصْباحِ) with kasra on the hamza: a maṣdar by which the morning is named. It was also read with fatḥa on the hamza (أَصباح), as the plural of صبح. The poet said:
أفنى رياحا وبني رياح ... تناسخ الإمساء والإصباح
(Riyāḥ and the sons of Riyāḥ were annihilated by the succession of evening and morning.)
More on the meaning of both will come in the section on rhetoric.
(حُسْباناً): with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, the maṣdar of حسب الحساب; its hāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently the ḥāʾ is meant] may also take kasra. الحساب is counting.
(سَكَناً): السكن is that in which one finds rest, such as family, wealth and so on. It is the maṣdar of سكنت إلى الشيء, of the pattern طلب. Abū al-Ṭayyib (al-Mutanabbī) said:
بم التّعلّل لا أهل ولا وطن ... ولا نديم ولا كأس ولا سكن
(With what shall I console myself — no family, no homeland, no boon companion, no cup, no one to rest in?)

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ فالِقُ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوى يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَمُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتِ مِنَ الْحَيِّ) Resumptive speech, brought to mention the proofs of the perfection of His power, Exalted is He, and that He is the Originator of things; and whoever is of this standing is the one deserving worship. (إن), its noun and its khabar (predicate). (الحب) is annexed to (فالق), and the annexation is not genuine (ghayr maḥḍa), on the basis that it has the sense of the present or the future, so (الحب) is genitive in form and accusative in position. The annexation may also be genuine (maḥḍa), on the basis that it is an active participle in the sense of the past, because that has already happened. (النوى) is conjoined to (الحب). The clause (يخرج الحي) may be resumptive, having no grammatical position, or it may be in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of (إن). (من الميت) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يخرج). (مخرج) is conjoined to (فالق), i.e. "Allah is the Splitter and the Bringer-forth"; it may also be conjoined to (يخرج), because the parts of the speech accord with one another, in which case the verb must be interpreted as a noun so that conjoining a noun to it is sound, or vice versa. (من الحي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (مخرج). (ذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ) The speech is resumptive, brought to show that Allah is the doer of all that. The fāʾ is resumptive [Translator's note: so in the source, though this phrase has no fāʾ before ذلكم]; the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الله) its khabar. The fāʾ is resumptive; (أنى) is an interrogative noun in the sense of (كيف), in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (تؤفكون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (فالِقُ الْإِصْباحِ وَجَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ سَكَناً) (فالق الإصباح) is an adjective of (الله), and (الإصباح) is muḍāf ilayhi. (وجعل): the wāw is a conjunction; (جعل) is a past verb; (الليل) is its first object and (سكنا) its second object. In a reading that they attribute to the majority:
«جاعل», with (الليل) in the genitive by annexation, in harmony with His words «فالق الإصباح». You may also make (سكنا) accusative as a ḥāl. (وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ حُسْباناً) The wāw is a conjunction; (الشمس) is conjoined to (الليل), and (حسبانا) is conjoined to (سكنا). You may also make (حسبانا) accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "they run by a reckoning" — the verse of (Sūrat) al-Raḥmān indicates this, as will come. (ذلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ) The speech is resumptive; the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ and (تقدير) its khabar; (العزيز) is muḍāf ilayhi and (العليم) an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains splendid devices of eloquence:

1- The device of departing from the expected (mukhālafat al-ẓāhir):
«يخرج الحي من الميت» came with the verb, whereas the expected form would have been the active participle, in keeping with the like attributes mentioned in His words «فالق الإصباح» and «مخرج الميت من الحي». But He turned from the active participle to the imperfect verb in this description alone, namely His words:
«يخرج الحي من الميت», intending to depict the bringing forth of the living from the dead — such as man and bird from the sperm-drop and the egg — and to make it present in the hearer's mind as if he were witnessing it with his own eyes. This device has already been illustrated with His words: «ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فتصبح الأرض مخضرة», where He turned away from the past tense matching His word «أنزل» for this very meaning. There is no doubt that bringing the living out of the dead is more renowned as a display of power and more indicative of it than its reverse, and consideration begins first with it [Translator's note: the source then adds «كإخراج النطفة والبيضة من الحيوان», "such as bringing the sperm-drop and the egg out of the animal", which appears to illustrate the reverse case].

2- The device of the problem (al-ishkāl):
It was pointed to earlier in «Āl ʿImrān». The problem here is that «مخرج» came contrary to the way its like came: it did not come as it came in Āl ʿImrān, «وتخرج», nor as it came in «Yūnus» and in «al-Rūm». Upon this the following question arises: what is the subtle point that required this place to come as it did, differing from its like? The answer by which this problem becomes clear is to say: it came only out of regard for good neighbourliness in the composition, because He said: «فالق الحب والنوى» and «فالق الإصباح». The verse was brought only for praise of Himself through absolute power, which is an essential attribute of Allah the Exalted; and praising with it while using the form of the active participle is more eloquent than using the form of the verb, because of what the active participle indicates of absolute past-ness, which indicates pre-eternity. For its coming as it came conveys the pre-eternity of the power, and the pre-eternity of the power entails the pre-eternity of the One described by it. And since He, Glorified is He, knew that praising Himself merely by the splitting of grain and date-stone in the belly of the earth is incomplete — because it brings no benefit until its plant comes out to the surface of the earth and people witness the power of the One who brings it out and originates it — His words:
«ومخرج الميت من الحي» became a complement, and in this clause He brought the active participle. This is among the miracles before which necks are cut short.

3- The device of the representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya):
That is in His words «فالق الإصباح». Its gist is that He, Exalted is He, likened the splitting of the pillar of dawn and the breaking forth of daybreak to the splitting of the morning. Poets have gazed up at the sky of this eloquence: Abū Tammām said, playing with this meaning:
وأزرق الفجر يبدو قبل أبيضه ... وأول الغيث قطر ثم ينسكب
(The blue of dawn appears before its white, and the first of the rain is drops, then it pours.)
He says: the beginnings of things appear small, then they grow, so one should take care from the beginning of the matter before it reaches its end. And he followed it with a verse that is a marvel of beauty, saying:
ومثل ذلك وجد العاشقين هوى ... بالمزح يبدو وبالإدمان ينتهب
(Like that is the passion of lovers: an inclination that begins in jest and, by persistence, plunders [the heart].)
Some critics attribute these two verses to Ibn al-Rūmī. He means that passion at its beginning is inclination and at its end is fire.

4- The likening of the night to (سكن) (rest):
In likening the night to (سكن) there is an inimitability in which human incapacity is embodied. The Qur'anic word, in expressing the intended meaning, excels all its lexical synonyms by a more complete correspondence to the intended meaning; whatever you substitute for it does not take its place, does not do its work, and does not convey the image it conveyed.
Look at the nature of the letters of which the word «سكنا» is composed and the succession of fatḥas on its letters: all of that makes you feel that calm which brings tranquility and spreads rest in the soul.

dervis-irab:97-98.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَفْقَهُونَ): imperfect of فقه الشيء, with kasra on the qāf, when one understands it, even with the slightest understanding. Al-Harawī said this in the course of arguing that «فقه» is lower than «علم». In the ḥadīth of Salmān, he said, when a woman who came to him had asked him (something): فقهت؟
i.e. "Have you understood?" — as one amazed at the woman's understanding of him. When it is said "لا يفقه فلان شيئا" (so-and-so understands nothing), it goes further in blame, in common usage, than your saying "لا يعلم شيئا" (he knows nothing). It is as though the meaning of "he understands nothing" is that he does not have the capacity for understanding, even if he understands; whereas the most that "he knows nothing" conveys is the negation of knowledge having come to him, and he may have the capacity for understanding and knowledge if he were to learn. The secret of using (يفقهون) here will come in the section on rhetoric.
(مستقر) with fatḥa on the qāf, because it is a noun of place or a mīmī maṣdar in the sense of الاستقرار (settling).
(مُسْتَوْدَعٌ) with fatḥa on the dāl, because it is a noun of place from استودع. More on the meaning of both will come in the section on i'rab.

* I'rab:
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ النُّجُومَ لِتَهْتَدُوا بِها فِي ظُلُماتِ الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) its khabar (predicate). (جعل) here is in the sense of "created", so it takes a single object. (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (جعل); (النجوم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (لتهتدوا): the lām is for giving the reason (taʿlīl) and governs the genitive; (تهتدوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of reason; the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to (جعل), by way of an inclusive substitution (badal ishtimāl) with repetition of the governor, the implied form being "He made the stars for you for your being guided." (في ظلمات البر والبحر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "while you are travelling by night in the darknesses of the night on land and sea." (قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ) The clause is resumptive, brought to stress the obligation of expending effort in the path of learning and guidance. (الآيات) is the direct object; (لقوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (فصلنا), and the clause (يعلمون) is an adjective of (قوم). (وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ) The wāw conjoins to what precedes; (هو) is the mubtadaʾ and the relative noun its khabar; the clause (أنشأكم) is the ṣila (relative clause); (من نفس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنشأكم), and (واحدة) is an adjective. (فمستقر): the fāʾ occurs in the answer to the relative because of the scent of condition in it. (مستقر) was read with fatḥa on the qāf, in which case it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "so for you there is a place of settling", because it is a noun of place or a mīmī maṣdar. Whoever read it with kasra on the qāf and on the dāl, both are active participles, the implied form being:
"so among you is one who settles and one who is deposited." (قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَفْقَهُونَ) Its i'rab has been given, and more on it will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
Oblique allusion (taʿrīḍ) to whoever does not ponder the signs of Allah and does not take lesson from what He created. It is known that ignorance has two different states. The first is an ignorance that does not go beyond the self of the one who considers and does not pass it. The second is an ignorance of what is outside the selves of those who consider, i.e. the stars and considering them, and the knowledge of the divine wisdom. Once that is established, it becomes easy for you to know that a person's ignorance of himself and of his states, and his failure to consider them and reflect upon their phases, is uglier than his ignorance of matters external to him, such as the stars, the celestial spheres and the measures of their courses. So since فقه is the lowest degree of knowledge, it was assigned to the worse of the two parties; and consequently the specification of negating the highest of them, by «علم», went with the party worse in state. [Translator's note: so in the source; the argument as stated seems to require that «يعلمون» (the higher term) go with the lesser fault, i.e. ignorance of the stars, and «يفقهون» with the worse one.]
This is one of the subtleties of our Arabic language, so be keen on it.

* Benefits:
Al-Shawkānī has a passage on «المستقر والمستودع» that quenches the thirst. He said:
«Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĪsā, al-Aʿraj and al-Nakhaʿī read it with kasra on the qāf, and the rest with fatḥa. Both are nominative as two mubtadaʾs whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "so among you is one who settles" or "so for you there is a place of settling" — the first implied form on the first reading and the second on the second, i.e.:
"so among you is one who settles on the surface of the earth" or "so for you there is a settling-place on its surface", "and among you is one deposited in the womb, or in the belly of the earth, or in the loins." It was also said: the مستقر is what is in the womb and the مستودع is what is in the loins. And it was said: the مستقر is whoever has been created, and the مستودع is whoever has not been created; and the depositing is an allusion to their being in the graves until the resurrection.»

dervis-irab:1-2.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جَعَلَ): it may be in the sense of "to originate, to bring about" (أنشأ وأحدث), in which case it takes one object in the accusative, and it may be in the sense of "to make into" (صيّر), in which case it takes two objects. Ibn Jinnī said in «al-Khaṣāʾiṣ»: "The Arabs may extend usage and put one of two verbs in the place of the other, to signal that this verb is in the sense of that other." The difference between jaʿl (making) and khalq (creating) is subtle, caught by a refined mind: khalq contains the meaning of measuring out (taqdīr), while jaʿl contains the meaning of inclusion (taḍmīn), such as originating one thing from another, or turning one thing into another, or moving it from one place to another.
(يمترون): they doubt. Al-imtirāʾ is doubt; its verb: مرى في الأمر, امترى and تمارى; ما فيه مرية, i.e. there is no doubt in it. مريت الناقة and أمريتها: I milked the she-camel, and she gave milk. Among figurative usages is قرع مروته ("he knocked his flint-stone"). Abū Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī said:
حتى كأني للحوادث مروة ... بصفا المشقّر كل يوم تقرع
(Until it is as though I were, for misfortunes, a flint-stone on the rocks of al-Mushaqqar, knocked every day.)
ماريته مماراة: I disputed with him and wrangled with him; تماروا, whose meaning is milking each other,
as though each were milking what the other has.

* I'rab:
(الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ الظُّلُماتِ وَالنُّورَ): resumptive speech urging reflection and contemplation and turning away from dispute and wrangling.
الحمد is a mubtadaʾ (subject); لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to its omitted khabar (predicate); الذي is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective); the clause خلق السموات والأرض is the ṣila (relative clause); السموات is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause وجعل الظلمات والنور is conjoined to the first clause. (ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay, and the conjunction is to His words الحمد لله [Translator's note: the text has the misprint «الحمد الله».] and what follows, in the sense that Allah is worthy of praise for what He created, because He created what He created as a blessing for mankind; then those who disbelieve in Him deviate, and so are ungrateful for His blessing. الذين is a mubtadaʾ; كفروا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila; بربهم is attached to كفروا, in which case يعدلون is in the sense of "they turn away from Him", from al-ʿudūl (turning aside). They may also be attached to يعدلون, the preposition and its genitive noun having been fronted for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila); يعدلون is then from al-ʿadl, which is making two things equal, i.e. "then those who disbelieve make others among created beings equal to their Lord", so the object is omitted. (هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ طِينٍ ثُمَّ قَضى أَجَلًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ)
Resumptive speech brought to establish the proof against their doubting. هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي the khabar; the clause خلقكم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; من طين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلقكم; ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; قضى أجلا is a past verb and its direct object, and the clause is conjoined to the clause خلقكم; وأجل: the wāw is resumptive, and أجل is a mubtadaʾ — beginning with it, though it is indefinite, is permissible because it is described by His word «مسمى»; عنده is an adverb of place attached to its omitted khabar; ثم is a conjunction [here] expressing deeming-unlikely, because of the distance between the two ranks; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause تمترون is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the two verses there are numerous arts of rhetoric, which we summarize as follows:
1- The affirmation of the permanence that He, glory be to Him, deserves, namely the permanence of praise to Him because He is the Bestower of blessings; the speech is declarative, with a command intended by it.
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq) between the heavens and the earth, and the darknesses and the light; when antithesis is multiplied it is called muqābala (correspondence).
3- Divergence in singular and plural: He made light singular and darknesses plural, because darknesses are among dense bodies and have many causes, and because light is of a single genus, namely fire.
4- Using the overt noun in place of the pronoun: He used the overt [noun], saying:
«ربهم», although mention of Allah had preceded, to magnify His majesty. This is one of the customs of the Arabs in their speech: they repeat the noun overtly even though it has preceded, without expressing it by a pronoun, to indicate complete attention. This discussion has preceded, together with citing as evidence the opening of al-Buḥturī's ode rhyming in sīn.
5- Indefiniteness: He began with an indefinite noun, namely «أجل», whereas the apparent [norm] would be to delay the mubtadaʾ: you say عندي كتاب ("I have a book"), and you do not say كتاب عندي.
But what necessitated fronting the indefinite noun is magnifying the significance of the term appointed with Him, glory be to Him — meaning the Hour — and emphasizing the awesomeness of its matter.
6- Omission of the direct object because it is evident, i.e. يعدلون به, i.e.
they make equal to their Lord others who have no power over anything of what He has power over. This is the utmost of folly and the extreme of stupidity.
7- Conjoining with ثمّ to express how unlikely it is that doubt should come from them, despite the existence of what requires its absence.

dervis-irab:3-5.t:
* I'rab:
(وَهُوَ اللَّهُ فِي السَّماواتِ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّكُمْ وَجَهْرَكُمْ وَيَعْلَمُ ما تَكْسِبُونَ)
The speech is resumptive, brought to draw attention to the attributes of divinity which none other than He deserves. هو is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), or it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); الله is the khabar (predicate); في السموات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to the meaning of the name Allah, i.e. "the One worshipped in them"; and في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun likewise attached to the meaning of the name Allah. More on the attachment of this preposition and its genitive noun will come in the section on benefits.
The clause يعلم is a second khabar or a ḥāl (circumstantial); سركم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); جهركم is conjoined to سركم; the clause ويعلم is conjoined to the clause يعلم; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; and the clause تكسبون is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. (وَما تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ مِنْ آياتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كانُوا عَنْها مُعْرِضِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, to show their persistence in disbelief and their turning away from the dazzling signs indicating the divine oneness. ما is negating; تأتيهم is an imperfect verb and a fronted direct object; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; آية is genitive in form and nominative in position, as the fāʿil (agent) of تأتيهم; من آيات ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of آية; إلا is a particle of restriction; كان and its noun; عنها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar «معرضين»; and the clause كانوا is circumstantial. (فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا بِالْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَهُمْ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa ("disclosing") fāʾ; قد is a particle of realization; كذبوا is a verb and its agent; بالحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كذبوا, i.e. "if they turn away from them, then they have denied what is greater than them, namely the truth". The clause in any case has no grammatical position. لما is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking: on the first view it is attached, and the clause جاءهم is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); on the second it has no grammatical position. (فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِيهِمْ أَنْباءُ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; سوف is a particle of the future; يأتيهم is an imperfect verb and a fronted direct object; أنباء is a delayed agent; ما is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause كانوا is the ṣila; the wāw is the noun of كان; the clause يستهزئون is its khabar; and به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يستهزئون.

* Benefits:
What we chose for the attachment of His words, the Exalted, «في السموات» is one view out of twelve that the exegetes and parsers have set forth in the i'rab of this expression. It was chosen by al-Zajjāj, al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Suʿūd, as if it were said:
"And He is the One worshipped in them." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In my view it is the best of the views and the most comprehensive, because of the eloquence of the wording and the grandeur of the meaning." The following are some of the acceptable views:
1- في السموات is attached to an omitted adjective of Allah the Exalted, omitted because the meaning is understood; the implied sense is: "And He is Allah, the One worshipped" or "the Disposer".
2- The speech is complete at His words «وهو الله», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the object of يعلم, namely: "your secret and your open [speech] in them".
3- They are attached to يعلم, and the clause يعلم on this view is resumptive.
We pass over the remaining views because they did not seem sound to us.

dervis-irab:46-47.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَصْدِفُونَ): in al-Mukhtār: "ṣadafa ʿanhu: he turned away; its pattern-classes are ḍaraba and jalasa. Aṣdafahu ʿanhu kadhā: such-and-such turned him away from it." Ṣādafahu: he met him, intentionally or without it. So what the common people say, ṣudfa (chance), is a mistake and a solecism. The author of al-Munjid claimed that al-ṣidfa, with kasra on the ṣād, is a post-classical (muwallad) word meaning chance encounter and coincidence.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ سَمْعَكُمْ وَأَبْصارَكُمْ وَخَتَمَ عَلى قُلُوبِكُمْ): a resumptive statement brought to establish the proof against them and cut off the way to their stubborn arrogance. (قل) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you, O Muḥammad". The hamza is for affirmative interrogation. The first object of (رأيتم) is omitted, its implied form being: "Have you considered your hearing and your sight, if Allah took them?" And the coming interrogative clause, which is «من إله», is in the place of the second object. (إن) is conditional; (أخذ) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); and the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted. The parsing of a parallel to it in «أرأيتكم» has preceded. The kāf of address was not brought here as it was brought there, because of the terror of the threat in the first. Hearing was made singular and sights plural for a secret mentioned before in Sūrat al-Baqara. It has been said: the hāʾ [in (به)] may refer to the hearing, and so be singular because it is singular; and it may be singular because «من» is singular, i.e. "what god other than Allah would bring you what was taken from you of hearing, sight and hearts?" (سمعكم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (أبصاركم) is conjoined; the clause (ختم) is conjoined; and (على قلوبكم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ختم).
(مَنْ إِلهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ): (من) is an interrogative noun for rebuke, and it is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (إله) is its khabar (predicate); (غير الله) is an adjective; the clause (يأتيكم) is a second adjective; and (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتيكم).
(انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآياتِ ثُمَّ هُمْ يَصْدِفُونَ): the clause is resumptive. (انظر) is an imperative verb; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it has suspended (انظر) from governing; the clause (نصرف الآيات) is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; (الآيات) is a mafʿūl bihi; (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause (يصدفون) is the khabar.
(قُلْ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ إِنْ أَتاكُمْ عَذابُ اللَّهِ بَغْتَةً أَوْ جَهْرَةً): the discussion of (أرأيتكم) preceded a little earlier, as did the parsing of (بغتة أو جهرة).
(هَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الظَّالِمُونَ): (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (القوم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (الظالمون) is an adjective.

dervis-irab:48-49.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما نُرْسِلُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to explain the tasks of the message and the precision of the charge with which the messengers are exercised. (نرسل المرسلين) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (مبشرين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and (منذرين) is conjoined to (مبشرين).
(فَمَنْ آمَنَ وَأَصْلَحَ فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (آمن) is a past verb, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (أصلح) is conjoined to it; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لا) is negative and inoperative; (خوف) is a mubtadaʾ and (عليهم) the khabar (predicate); (ولا هم يحزنون): the clause is conjoined to the first clause; the clause «لا خوف عليهم» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». «من» may also be a relative noun, in keeping with what follows it, so that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the clause «لا خوف عليهم» is the khabar of the relative noun, the fāʾ being brought because of the scent of condition in the relative noun.
(وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا يَمَسُّهُمُ الْعَذابُ بِما كانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كذبوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (بآياتنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كذبوا); the clause (يمسهم العذاب) is the khabar of the relative noun. (بما): the bāʾ is a preposition and (ما) is maṣdariyya, the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) being genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يمسهم), i.e. "because of their transgression"; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يفسقون) is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «يمسهم العذاب» there is a dependent explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya), as though the punishment were a living being doing to them whatever pains it wishes. Its like has preceded many times.

dervis-irab:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ: لا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي خَزائِنُ اللَّهِ): the statement is resumptive, brought to declare himself free of what they propose to him. (قل) is an imperative verb; (لا) is negative; (أقول) is an imperfect verb; (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أقول); the clause (لا أقول) is the object of the first speech; (لكم) is attached to (أقول); (عندي) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (خزائن الله) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the second speech.
(وَلا أَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ وَلا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ): the clause (ولا أعلم الغيب) is conjoined to the clause (عندي خزائن الله), because it is part of the object of the speech; and the clause (لا أقول لكم إني ملك) is conjoined to the first clause (لا أقول لكم). (إني ملك): (إن) with its noun and khabar is likewise the object of the speech.
(إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا ما يُوحى إِلَيَّ): the clause falls within the scope of the speech, which has not yet ended. (إن) is negative; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; «ما» is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يوحى) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir); and (إليّ) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يوحى).
(قُلْ: هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ أَفَلا تَتَفَكَّرُونَ): a resumptive statement completing the injunctions. (هل) is an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation, i.e. "they are not equal"; (يستوي) is an imperfect verb; (الأعمى) is its fāʿil (agent); (البصير) is conjoined to (الأعمى); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (أفلا): the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; and (تتفكرون) is conjoined to an omitted, implied element, its implied form being: "i.e. do they not listen to this speech that is recited to you, and so you do not reflect on it and discern its consequences?"

* Rhetoric:
Ṭibāq (antithesis) between (الأعمى) and (البصير); they are two concise similes (tashbīh balīgh) for the one who strays and the one who is guided. They may also be considered as belonging to explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), because the thing likened is not mentioned while the thing it is likened to is mentioned.

dervis-irab:6-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مكّن له في الأرض): He gave him a place; مكّنته: I established him firmly.
(المدرار): abundant. Mifʿāl is an intensive form indicating abundance, like مذكار for a woman who bears many male children, and مئناث for one who bears females.
(قَرْناً): qarn is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like قوم and رهط. People differed about qarn when it is applied to time: the majority of lexicographers hold that it is a hundred years. It is also applied to a group of people who are the inhabitants of one time, as in the verse. Its plural is قرون.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ): the speech is resumptive, brought to begin rebuking those who do not believe, because they were ungrateful for their Lord's blessing and denied the truth when it came to them. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr) and rebuke at the same time; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [of tense] and jussive; يروا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لم; the seeing is visual or cognitive; كم is predicative (khabariyya) or interrogative, in the position of the accusative as a fronted object of أهلكنا; the clause أهلكنا stands in place of the object, or the two objects, of [the verb of] seeing; من قبلهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and من with its genitive noun is in the position of the accusative as the tamyīz (specification) [Translator's note: the text has the misprint «تميز».] of كم. (مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ ما لَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَكُمْ): the clause is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of قرن; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مكناهم; مكناهم is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مكناهم [Translator's note: this statement is repeated in the source.]. «ما» may be a complete indefinite noun in the sense of "something", in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "something of establishment that We did not establish for you", so the clause after it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective. It may also be maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (temporal-maṣdar), i.e. "the duration of their establishment was longer than the duration of your establishment", and the clause is likewise an adjective. It was also said: «ما» is a relative noun in the sense of الذي, the implied sense being:
"the establishment which We did not establish for you"; the thing described was omitted and the adjective was put in its place; the clause after it is the ṣila (relative clause), and the pronoun referring back to «ما» is omitted, i.e. "which We did not establish for you". The first is the simplest of them. لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; نكن [Translator's note: so in the text, a misprint for «نمكن».] is an imperfect verb in the jussive by لم; and لكم is attached to نمكن. (وَأَرْسَلْنَا السَّماءَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِدْراراً): the wāw is conjunctive; أرسلنا السماء is a verb, its agent and its direct object; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسلنا; and مدرارا is a ḥāl. (وَجَعَلْنَا الْأَنْهارَ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْناهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ): likewise conjoined to what precedes; the clause تجري من تحتهم is in the position of the accusative as the second direct object of جعلنا; فأهلكناهم: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and أهلكناهم is a verb, its agent and its direct object; and بذنوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أهلكناهم. (وَأَنْشَأْنا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْناً آخَرِينَ): likewise conjoined; أنشأنا is a verb and its agent; من بعدهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنشأنا; قرنا is the direct object; and آخرين is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (shift of address) in His words «ما لم نمكن لكم», whereas the context would require:
"what We did not establish for them" — in order to single out for direct address those to whom the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ was sent, besides refreshing the listener's attention.
2- Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) in His words «وأرسلنا السماء عليهم مدرارا», the relationship being that of place (maḥalliyya): He means abundant rain, and expressed it by "the sky" because it comes down from it. The poet glanced at this trope in his words:
إذا نزل السماء بأرض قوم ... رعيناه وإن كانوا غضابا
(When the sky [i.e. rain] comes down on a people's land, we graze it, even if they are angry.)

dervis-irab:7-8.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قِرْطاسٍ): al-qirṭās is that on which one writes; kasra on the qāf is better known than ḍamma. القرطس, on the pattern of «جعفر», is a dialectal variant of it. In al-Qāmūs:
"With the qāf vowelled in three ways, and like جعفر and درهم: paper (al-kāghad); al-kāghad is well known, with fatḥa on the ghayn and an undotted dāl, and sometimes it is said with a dotted dhāl; it is arabicized." This is what is meant here. It has other meanings, among them a target, an Egyptian cloak, a fair-skinned slave girl of tall stature, and a young she-camel. The plural is قراطيس.

* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنا عَلَيْكَ كِتاباً فِي قِرْطاسٍ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ): resumptive speech brought to show the excess of their obstinacy and their persistence in arrogance and wrangling.
لو is conditional; نزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); عليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to نزلنا; كتابا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في قرطاس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كتابا»; فلمسوه: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and لمسوه is a verb, its agent and its direct object, conjoined to نزلنا; and بأيديهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to لمسوه. (لَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ): the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; قال الذين is a verb and its agent, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; the clause كفروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); إن is negating; هذا is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction; سحر is the khabar (predicate) of هذا; مبين is an adjective; and the negative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَقالُوا: لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ): the clause is resumptive, brought to emphasize their wrangling and their persistence in obstinacy and arrogance. قالوا is a verb and its agent; لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) that needs no apodosis; أنزل is a passive past verb; عليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل; ملك is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause of urging is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying. (وَلَوْ أَنْزَلْنا مَلَكاً لَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ ثُمَّ لا يُنْظَرُونَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to reply to them with two answers to their obstinacy and arrogance. لو is conditional; أنزلنا ملكا is a verb, its agent and its object; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; the clause قضي الأمر has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay, because of the distance between the two matters:
the matter being decided and the absence of respite, i.e. after the matter is decided there is a severity — how far what they saw falls short of it! [Translator's note: the text repeats «منها منها».] Being taken by surprise by severity is harder than the severity itself. لا is negating; ينظرون is a passive imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), conjoined to قضي الأمر; and the wāw is the deputy agent.

* Rhetoric:
Iṭnāb (amplification) in His words «فلمسوه بأيديهم»: He mentioned the hands, although touching is only by them, so that the perception of both senses would be combined for them: the sense of sight and the sense of touch.

dervis-irab:99-99.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خَضِراً) with kasra on the ḍād: a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle). One says أخضر and خضر, like أعور and عور.
(مُتَراكِباً): parts of it mounting one another, like ears of wheat and the like.
(قِنْوانٌ): a broken plural whose singular is قنو, like صنو and صنوان. This plural is confused with the dual in pause, and it is distinguished by the vowel of the nūn: the nūn of the dual always has kasra, while the nūn of this plural takes all three vowels in turn according to the i'rab. The two are also distinguished in the relative adjective (nisba): when you form the nisba of the dual you return it to the singular and say قنويّ; when you form the nisba of the plural you leave it as it is, because it is a broken plural, and we say قنوانيّ. They are also distinguished in annexation: the nūn of the dual drops for it, unlike the nūn of the broken plural; so you say of the dual هذان قنواك ("these are your two clusters"), and of the plural هذه قنوانك ("these are your clusters"). The like is said of صنوان, as dual and as plural. القنو, with kasra on the qāf — and it is also said with ḍamma — is the العذق (date-cluster), which is to the palm as the bunch is to the grape.
(دانِيَةٌ): easy to gather, near to the one who picks.
(يَنْعِهِ): the maṣdar of ينع with kasra on the nūn; it has kasra in the past and fatḥa in the imperfect, i.e. it ripened and matured. Abū ʿUbayda said in his book Majāz al-Qurʾān: when its yāʾ has fatḥa it is the plural of يانع, as التجر is the plural of تاجر and الصّحب the plural of صاحب. Its maṣdar may also be ينوع, and it is heard from the Arabs: أينعت الثمرة تونع إيناعا. From the usage of those who said ينع are the words of the poet Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya about a Christian woman who became a nun in a ruined monastery near al-Māṭirūn, a place in Syria. He said:
آب هذا الهمّ فاكتنفا ... وأترّ النوم فامتنعا
راعيا للنجم أرقبه ... فإذا ما كوكب طلعا
في قباب عند سكرة ... حولها الزيتون قد ينعا
(This care has returned and enveloped me, and sleep has fled and refused [to come]; watching the stars I keep vigil, whenever a star rises — in domes by a [monastery], around which the olives have ripened.)
to the end of this delightful ode.

* I'rab:
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأَخْرَجْنا بِهِ نَباتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what precedes it, because of the harmony of the beginning of the speech with its end and the mention of what people need for their livelihood. (هو) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) its khabar (predicate); the clause (أنزل من السماء) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (ماء) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أخرجنا) is a verb and its agent; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أخرجنا); and (نبات كل شيء) is the direct object. (فَأَخْرَجْنا مِنْهُ خَضِراً نُخْرِجُ مِنْهُ حَبًّا مُتَراكِباً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أخرجنا) is a verb and its agent; (منه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أخرجنا); (خضرا) is the direct object, and the clause (نخرج) is an adjective of «خضرا». He expressed it with the imperfect, though the context calls for the past, in order to make the near image present; its parallels have been given in the sections on rhetoric. (منه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نخرج); (حبا) is the direct object, and (متراكبا) an adjective. (وَمِنَ النَّخْلِ مِنْ طَلْعِها قِنْوانٌ دانِيَةٌ) The wāw is parenthetical; (من النخل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (من طلعها) is a badal (substitute) from the preposition and genitive noun before it, with repetition of the preposition, and the badal here is a substitution of part for whole, because the spathe (الطلع) is the first of it to appear to the eyes. (قنوان) is the delayed mubtadaʾ, and (دانية) is an adjective of (قنوان). The clause is parenthetical, brought to recall the favour, because (the date) is among the greatest staple foods of the Arabs, and because it combines delight and nourishment. (وَجَنَّاتٍ مِنْ أَعْنابٍ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ مُشْتَبِهاً وَغَيْرَ مُتَشابِهٍ) The wāw is a conjunction, and (جنات) is conjoined to (نبات), so it is accusative, i.e. "and We brought out by the water the plants, and gardens"; it is thus a conjoining of the specific to the general. (من أعناب) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective; and likewise (الزيتون) and (الرمان) [Translator's note: i.e. are conjoined]. Al-Zamakhsharī chose to make (الزيتون) and (الرمان) accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), to extol these two kinds and distinguish them. (مشتبها) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), what is meant being the resemblance of their leaves, and (غير متشابه) is conjoined to it. Some read «وجناتٌ» in the nominative, and Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī judged it weak. The nominative is by conjoining it to (قنوان), or as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e.:
"and there are gardens of grapes"; Abū al-Baqāʾ supplied it as "and of the vine there are gardens." (انْظُرُوا إِلى ثَمَرِهِ إِذا أَثْمَرَ وَيَنْعِهِ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the fronted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. (انظروا) is an imperative verb and the wāw is the agent; (إلى ثمره) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (انظروا); (إذا) is an adverb of the future [Translator's note: the source prints «مستقل», evidently for «مستقبل»] containing the sense of condition, attached to the apodosis, which is (انظروا); the clause (أثمر) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; and (ينعه) is conjoined to (ثمره). (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكُمْ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) The speech is resumptive, brought to give the reason for worshipping Him, Glorified is He, and to show His surpassing power. (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of (إن); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (آيات) is the noun of (إن); (لقوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of (آيات); and the clause (يؤمنون) is an adjective of (قوم). The demonstrative refers to everything mentioned from His words «إن الله فالق الحب والنوى» up to here.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is an eloquent shift of person (iltifāt) in His words «فأخرجنا»; its secret is concern for the importance of this bringing-forth and drawing attention to the surpassing greatness and power.

dervis-irab:100-101.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَخَرَقُوا): they fabricated. One says خلق الإفك and خرقه, اختلقه, افتراه and افتعله, all in the sense of lying. It is of the pattern ضرب.
(بَدِيعُ): The word بديع occurs in the Qur'an twice: first in al-Baqara, in His words «بديع السموات والأرض وإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون», and second in this verse. The meaning of بديع in both verses is their Originator and Inventor without any previous model. This root has many meanings that come down to two things:
1- Newness, which is indicated by bringing a thing into being from the start and without previous model.
2- Excellence and strangeness, which is indicated by the wondrous. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
فأتتها فأخبرتها بعذري ... ثم قالت: أتيت أمرا بديعا
(She came to her and told her of my excuse; then she said: you have done a strange thing.)

* I'rab:
(وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ الْجِنَّ) Resumptive speech, brought to show their stance towards their Creator after He had shown the favours lavished upon them, and how they went against what sound reason requires. (جعلوا) is a verb and its agent; (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (شركاء), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it; (شركاء) is the second object of (جعلوا), placed first to show the enormity of taking a partner for Allah; and (الجن) is the first object. (وَخَلَقَهُمْ وَخَرَقُوا لَهُ بَنِينَ وَبَناتٍ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) The wāw is circumstantial, and (قد) must be supplied after it. (وخرقوا): the wāw is a conjunction; (خرقوا) is a verb and its agent; (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خرقوا); (بنين) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (بنات) is conjoined to (بنين); (بغير علم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of (خرقوا), i.e. "they fabricated the lie, accompanied by ignorance", which is the absence of knowledge. The clause is conjoined to the clause (وخلقهم). (سُبْحانَهُ وَتَعالى عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ) (سبحانه): a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "He is exalted far above with an exalting"; (تعالى) is conjoined to the implied verb governing (سبحانه); (عما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تعالى); the clause (يصفون) is the ṣila (relative clause); and the clause of glorification is resumptive. (بَدِيعُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ) The clause is resumptive, brought to show the impossibility of what they attribute [Translator's note: the source prints «ينسونه», evidently for «ينسبونه»] to Him and to affirm His transcendence above it. (بديع السموات والأرض) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is the Originator". (أنى) is an interrogative noun in the sense of "how" or "whence", in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; (يكون) is a defective imperfect verb; (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of (يكون), and (ولد) is its delayed noun. The clause (أنى يكون له ولد) is resumptive. (وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ صاحِبَةٌ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive; (تكن) [Translator's note: the source prints «ولكن», evidently for «وتكن»] is a defective imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم); (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of (تكن), and (صاحبة) is its delayed noun. (خلق كل شيء): this clause is either resumptive or a ḥāl. On the latter parsing the meaning is: "How, and from where, could He have a child, when He created all things, including what they called a child of His? So how could it cross anyone's mind that the begotten is the child of his Creator?"
(وهو): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (بكل شيء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عليم), and (عليم) is the khabar of «هو».

dervis-irab:9-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَلْبِسُونَ): one says لبس عليه الأمر يلبسه, with ḍamma on the bāʾ in the imperfect [Translator's note: so in the text; the vowelling of the verse, «يَلْبِسُونَ», has kasra on the bāʾ.], labsan: he made his affair confused for him, obscured it and made it problematic for him. Its origin is covering with a garment.

* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ مَلَكاً لَجَعَلْناهُ رَجُلًا وَلَلَبَسْنا عَلَيْهِمْ ما يَلْبِسُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to reply to them with the second answer. لو is conditional; جعلناه is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ملكا is a second direct object; the pronoun refers back to the warner they proposed. The meaning is: had We made that warner an angel, We would have represented that angel as a man, since individual people are unable to see an angel in its own form and frame. The lām links the apodosis of لو; the clause جعلناه رجلا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; للبسنا is conjoined to «لجعلنا»; عليهم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to لبسنا; «ما» may be a relative noun in the sense of الذي, i.e. "We would have confused for them what they confuse for themselves or for others", in which case it is a direct object; or it may be maṣdariyya, i.e. "We would have confused for them with a confusion like that with which they confuse others", in which case it is fused into a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause يلبسون has no grammatical position in both cases. (وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): resumptive speech brought to console the Prophet ﷺ. The lām is [the lām of] the answer to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of realization; استهزئ is a passive past verb; برسل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استهزئ, and they stand in place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and من قبلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective). (فَحاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; حاق is a past verb conjoined to استهزئ; بالذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حاق; the clause سخروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to سخروا; ما is the agent of حاق, and it is either a relative noun or maṣdariyya; كان and its noun; the clause يستهزئون is its khabar (predicate); and به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يستهزئون. The pronoun in به refers back to the messenger — the meaning being that the consequence of their mocking the messenger, who is strung on the thread of the messengers, encompassed them — or to the word ما, whether maṣdariyya or relative. (قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ انْظُرُوا): resumptive speech brought to urge reflection and travel in the land to contemplate the consequences [Translator's note: the text reads «مغاب», apparently for «مغابّ» / «مغبّات» ("consequences").] of the former nations and their fates. The clause سيروا is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ثم was used to point to the distance latent in the travel that leads to insight and contemplation, and because the obligation of travel was only for reaching this lofty rank, which is the utmost that high aspirations aspire to. في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to سيروا; ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; and انظروا is an imperative verb and its agent. (كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of انظروا; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar of كان; عاقبة is its noun — كان was not made feminine because العاقبة is figuratively (not really) feminine; it [كيف] has suspended the verb of looking from operating in form; and المكذبين is muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) in His words «عاقبة المكذبين», the relationship being the outcome and end to which the fate and end of the deniers lead.
2- In His words from «ولقد استهزئ» to His words «ما كانوا به يستهزئون» there is an art called radd al-aʿjāz ʿalā al-ṣudūr (returning the ends upon the beginnings). It consists of any speech between whose beginning and end there is a bond — usually verbal, rarely semantic — by which harmony and cohesion are achieved between the two parts of the speech. It has three divisions:
1- Where the last word of the speech agrees with the last word of its first part, or is cognate with it, as in His words, the Exalted, in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: «أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون وكفى بالله شهيدا».
2- Where the last word of the speech agrees with its first word, as in His words, the Exalted, in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: «وهب لنا من لدنك رحمة إنك أنت الوهّاب».
3- Where the last word of the speech agrees with one of the words of its first part, wherever it may be, as in the verse we are dealing with. These bonds are all verbal; they may also be semantic, as in His words, the Exalted: «يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضرّكم من ضلّ إذا اهتديتم».

Poetic examples:
Among examples of this art in poetry are the words of al-Buḥturī:
ضرائب أبدعتها في السماح ... فلسنا نرى لك فيها ضريبا
(Traits of generosity you originated, so we see no peer to you in them.)
And the words of Abū Tammām:
ولم يحفظ مضاع المجد شيء ... من الأشياء كالمال المضاع
(Nothing preserves lost glory like wealth that is spent away.)
And the famous, splendid verses of the Ḥamāsa:
تمتع من شميم عرار نجد ... فما بعد العشية من عرار
شهور ينقضين وما شعرنا ... بأنصاف لهنّ ولا سرار
(Enjoy the scent of the ʿarār flowers of Najd, for after this evening there will be no ʿarār. Months pass away, and we perceived neither their middles nor their moonless ends.)
Al-Thaʿālibī showed his wit by combining this art with the art of tajnīs (paronomasia), saying — and it would almost be delightful were it not for a touch of affectation:
وإذا البلابل أفصحت بلغاتها ... فانف البلابل باحتساء بلابل
(When the nightingales speak eloquently in their tongues, banish your cares by sipping from wine-jugs.)
The first بلابل is the plural of بلبل, a well-known singing bird; the second:
is the plural of بلبال, which is grief; and the third is the plural of بلبلة, with ḍamma, which is a wine-jug. Another showed his wit by combining this art with the art of tajnīs and the art of tawriya (double entendre), saying: لا كان إنسان تيمّم قاصدا ... صيد المها فاصطاده إنسانها
(May there not be a man who set out intending to hunt the wild cows [i.e. beautiful women], and was then hunted by their pupils.)
The first إنسان is the well-known person, and the second إنسان is the pupil of the eye. The following is a group of examples of this art distributed over its three divisions mentioned above. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said:
لو اختصرتم من الإحسان زرتكم ... والعذب يهجر للإفراط في الخصر
(Had you cut short your kindness, I would have visited you; sweet water is shunned for excessive coldness.)
الخصر, with two fatḥas, is coldness.
And Abū Tammām said:
ومن يك بالبيض الكواعب مغرما ... فما زلت بالبيض القواضب مغريا
(Whoever is enamoured of fair, full-breasted maidens — I have never ceased to be devoted to white, cutting swords.)
And how beautiful are the words of one of them:
فدع الوعيد فما وعيدك ضائري ... أطنين أجنحة الذباب يضير؟
(Leave off threats, for your threat does not harm me; does the buzzing of flies' wings do harm?)
And Abū Tammām said in elegy:
ثوى بالثّرى من كان يحيا به الثّرى ... ويغمر حرف الدهر نائله الغمر
وقد كانت البيض القواضب قبله ... بواتر فهي الآن من بعده بتر
(He who used to bring the earth to life now lies in the earth, he whose abundant bounty used to overwhelm the edge of fortune. The white cutting swords were, before him, sharp; now, after him, they are blunted.)

dervis-irab:51-52.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأَنْذِرْ بِهِ الَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ أَنْ يُحْشَرُوا إِلى رَبِّهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the statement is conjoined to what preceded, turning to directing the warning to those in whom acceptance of admonition and readiness to receive it are discerned, and they are the disobedient believers. (أنذر) is an imperative verb; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنذر); (الذين) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يخافون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and (أن) with what follows it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of (يخافون).
(لَيْسَ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ وَلِيٌّ وَلا شَفِيعٌ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (أن يحشروا), i.e. warn with it these who fear the gathering, in the state that they have, besides Allah, no protector to befriend them, no helper and no intercessor to intercede for them. (ليس) is a defective past verb; (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of (ليس); (من دونه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; (ولي) is the noun of (ليس); (ولا شفيع) is conjoined to (ولي); (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (يتقون) is its khabar; and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.
(وَلا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَداةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تطرد) is an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive (لا), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (الذين) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (يدعون) is the ṣila; (ربهم) is a mafʿūl bihi; (بالغداة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يدعون); and (العشي) is conjoined to (الغداة).
(يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ): the clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun of (يدعون), i.e. "they call upon Him sincerely"; and (وجهه) is a mafʿūl bihi.
(ما عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): (ما) may be the Ḥijāzī mā, governing as (ليس) does, so that «عليك» is in the position of the accusative as its khabar — according to those who permit its governing a fronted khabar when it is an adverb or a preposition with its genitive noun. Under the view that forbids this, the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar, and the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject) is «شيء», to which «من» has been redundantly added. His words (من حسابهم) are a ḥāl, the one to whom the ḥāl refers being «شيء», because had the preposition and its genitive noun come after it, they would have been attached to an omitted adjective of it; and the adjective of an indefinite noun, when fronted, becomes accusative as a ḥāl. The clause (ما عليك …) is also a ḥāl.
(وَما مِنْ حِسابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the parsing of (وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء) has preceded, except that making (من حسابك) a ḥāl is problematic, because it entails fronting the ḥāl before its abstract governor, which is weak. Had the second clause come on the pattern of the first, the construction would have been: "وما عليهم من حسابك من شيء", fronting the word made genitive by (على) as He fronted it in the first; but He fronted it [i.e. (من حسابك)] to honour him ﷺ, so that the address faces him directly. And so you are compelled to make it an adjective placed before the noun it describes.
(فتطردهم): the fāʾ is the causal (sababiyya) one, and it is the answer to the negation; (تطردهم) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن). (فتكون): the fāʾ is also causal, and it is the answer to the prohibition — so consider the subtlety of the difference between the meanings of the two fāʾs. You may also make the second fāʾ a conjunction, so that it is conjoined to (تطردهم) by way of causation, because his being unjust is caused by driving them away. (من الظالمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of (تكون).

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «يريدون وجهه», i.e. His essence and reality, there is majāz mursal (synecdoche), the relation being the mention of the part while intending the whole; it is a figure acceptable in their speech.
2- In His words «وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء» there is the device of radd al-ʿajuz ʿalā al-ṣadr (returning the end to the beginning). It is that the speaker places one of two words that agree in pronunciation and meaning, or resemble each other in pronunciation but not meaning, or are united by derivation or quasi-derivation, at the end of the speech, after placing the other word in its beginning.
From it is the saying of al-Buḥturī:
ضرائب أبدعتها في السّماح ... فلسنا نرى لك فيها ضريبا
(Traits of generosity you originated, so we see no equal to you in them.)
And the saying of Abū Tammām:
ولم يحفظ مضاع المجد شيء ... من الأشياء كالمال المضاع
(Nothing preserves glory that would be lost like wealth that is spent away.)
And the saying of al-Maʿarrī:
لو اختصرتم من الإحسان زرتكم ... والعذب يهجر للإفراط في الخصر
(Had you cut short your kindness I would have visited you; even sweet water is shunned for being excessively cold.)
And the famous line of al-Ḥamāsa:
تمتع من شميم عرار نجد ... فما بعد العشيّة من عرار
(Enjoy the scent of the ʿarār flowers of Najd, for after this evening there will be no ʿarār.)

* Benefits:
It is related that the chiefs of the polytheists said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If you drove away from us these slaves" — meaning the poor Muslims, namely ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, Ṣuhayb and Bilāl, and the smell of their cloaks, for they wore woollen cloaks continually, having no others — "we would sit with you and converse with you." He, upon him be blessing and peace, said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then make them get up from us when we come, and when we leave, seat them with you if you wish." He said: "Yes," hoping for their Islam. They said: "Then write us a document binding you to that." He brought the sheet and called ʿAlī to write, and Jibrīl came down to him with His words: «ولا تطرد..» (the verse). This is among the most splendid examples of Islamic equality.

dervis-irab:53-54.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَتَنَّا): We tested and tried.
(مَنَّ): He bestowed favour. One says: he has upon me a minna and minan (favours); manna ʿalayya bimā ṣanaʿa (he reminded me of his favour in what he did); imtanantu minka bimā faʿalta minnatan jasīma, i.e. I bore a great favour; and "his heart has no munna", i.e. strength. The root of mīm and nūn conveys giving and withholding for the most part; from it: manaḥa, and so-and-so is mannāḥ (a great giver), and so-and-so gives manāʾiḥ and minaḥ (gifts); manaʿa al-shayʾ, manaʿahu and manaʿa ʿanhu, and he is manūʿ and mannāʿ (withholding). This is among the wonders of our language that stop at no limit.

* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ فَتَنَّا بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ): the statement is resumptive, brought to explain that Islam made equality a law and a way, because Allah tried the rich by the poor and the poor by the rich, each being tried by his opposite, so that equality becomes universal: there is no high and no low, no great and no small. The kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); or it is a preposition and the demonstrative is in the position of the genitive, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of an omitted noun described. Its discussion has preceded; Sībawayh prefers parsing it as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (بعضهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (ببعض) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فتنا).
(لِيَقُولُوا: أَهؤُلاءِ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ بَيْنِنا أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَعْلَمَ بِالشَّاكِرِينَ): the lām is for giving the reason, and (يقولوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām; the implied form is: "and with the like of that trial We tried [them] so that they would say this saying, as a trial and test from Us". The lām may also be the lām of becoming (al-ṣayrūra), or of outcome, so that His words «أهؤلاء» issue from them by way of belittling the believers. The interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). The hamza is for affirmative and mocking interrogation; (هؤلاء) is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «منّ الله» is the khabar (predicate); (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «منّ»; and (من بيننا) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. We may also parse «هؤلاء» as accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), by an omitted verb explained by the overt verb that governs its pronoun through «على», the explaining being in terms of meaning, not wording; the implied form is: "Has Allah preferred these, and bestowed favour on them" or "chosen them"; and the clause (منّ الله عليهم) then has no grammatical position because it is explicative. This view became acceptable, and many preferred it, only because it follows the interrogative hamza, which is a particle mostly followed by a verb. His words (أليس): the hamza is for affirmative interrogation; (ليس) is a defective past verb; (الله) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (أعلم) is genitive by the bāʾ in wording and accusative by position as the khabar of (ليس); (بالشاكرين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أعلم); and the interrogative clause is resumptive, brought to be the answer to the affirmative interrogation.
(وَإِذا جاءَكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآياتِنا فَقُلْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to return to mention of the believers whose driving away was forbidden. (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the sense of condition, attached to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e. "say: peace be upon you, at the time of their coming". The clause (جاءك) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; (الذين) is the fāʿil (agent); the clause (يؤمنون) is the ṣila (relative clause). (فقل): the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis; (سلام) is a mubtadaʾ, permitted to begin with though it is indefinite because of the sense of supplication in it; (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; the clause (قل) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and the clause (سلام عليكم) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech.
(كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ): the clause falls within the scope of what is said, because it is part of what he says to them. (كتب ربكم) is a verb and its fāʿil; (على نفسه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كتب); and (الرحمة) is a mafʿūl bihi.
(أَنَّهُ مَنْ عَمِلَ مِنْكُمْ سُوءاً بِجَهالَةٍ ثُمَّ تابَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): it was read with fatḥa on the hamza, so that (أن) and its noun are in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of (الرحمة), and the clause is included in the scope of the speech. In a reading with kasra on the hamza, the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the mercy, and the hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the noun of (إن). (من) is a jussive conditional noun or a relative, and it is a mubtadaʾ in either case; (عمل) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (سوءا) is a mafʿūl bihi; (منكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the fāʿil of (عمل); and (بجهالة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, also from the same fāʿil, i.e. "he did it while ignorant of the reality of the harms and faults and evil outcomes that result from it". (ثم) is a conjunction; (تاب) is conjoined to (تاب) [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for "conjoined to (عمل)"]; and (أصلح) is likewise conjoined to it.
