The fāʾ links the apodosis; and (أن) with fatḥa on the hamza, with what falls within its scope, is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "his affair and his outcome is Allah's forgiveness of him"; and (غفور رحيم) are two khabars of (أن). It was read with kasra on the hamza of (إن) as a new beginning, and Ibn Jarīr preferred it as a new beginning since it occurs after the fāʾ. The clause (من عمل) is the khabar of (إن), and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

dervis-irab:102-103.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ) The speech is resumptive; it and what follows it are a listing that affirms His description, Glorified is He, by these sublime attributes. The demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject); (الله) is a first khabar (predicate), (ربكم) a second khabar, and the clause (لا إله إلا هو) a third khabar. The i'rab of the word of testimony has been given before, so renew your acquaintance with it. (خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَاعْبُدُوهُ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ) (خالق كل شيء) is a fourth khabar. (فاعبدوه): the fāʾ gives the reason (taʿlīliyya); (اعبدوه) is an imperative verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is for showing the cause of worship. (وهو): the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (على كل شيء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (وكيل), and (وكيل) is the khabar of (هو). (لا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصارَ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ) The clause is a fifth khabar. (تدركه الأبصار) is a verb, a fronted direct object and an agent. (وهو يدرك): the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يدرك الأبصار) is its khabar. (وهو): the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (اللطيف) is a first khabar and (الخبير) a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the second verse there are numerous devices of rhetoric, which we summarise as follows:

1- Correspondence (al-munāsaba):
This is when the speaker begins with a meaning and then completes his speech with what corresponds to it in meaning, not in wording. The meaning of denying that eyes perceive a thing corresponds to subtlety (al-luṭf). This speech comes in the manner of a representation (tamthīl), because what is familiar to the one addressed is that sight does not perceive subtle bodies such as air and the other elements, nor single atoms; it only perceives the colour of every coloured thing and the being of every existing thing. So this representation came so that the hearer may imagine it and thereby compare the unseen to the seen. Likewise His words, Exalted is He: «وهو يدرك الأبصار», to which describing the Perceiver as All-Aware (al-khibra) corresponds.

2- The device of guarding (al-iḥtirās):
When He, Glorified is He, affirmed for Himself the perceiving of eyes [Translator's note: so in the source; the context suggests "when He denied that eyes perceive Him"], eloquence required the device of guarding, to avoid anyone supposing that if He is not perceived He does not exist. So it was necessary to say «وهو يدرك الأبصار», to affirm existence for His essence.

3- The device of folding and spreading (al-laff wa-l-nashr):
Some called it "the device of the resemblance of the ends" (tashābuh al-aṭrāf). His word «اللّطيف» goes back to His words «لا تدركه الأبصار», and His word «الخبير» goes back to His words «وهو يدرك الأبصار».

4- The device of turning back (al-taʿaṭṭuf):
which is His words «لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار», because (الأبصار) comes at the beginning and at the end of the speech.

5- The device of antithesis (al-muṭābaqa):
between His words «لا تدركه الأبصار» and His words «وهو يدرك الأبصار».
Thus the verse has completed five full devices of the devices of rhetoric.

* Benefits:
This verse is the strongest of the proofs of the Muʿtazila among the transmitted proofs that Allah the Exalted is not seen, because it is explicit. The answer is that another verse contradicts it, namely His words, Exalted is He: «وجوه يومئذ ناضرة إلى ربها ناظرة». As for their doubt from His words, Exalted is He, «لا تدركه الأبصار», the Ashʿarīs answered it: His words «لا تدركه الأبصار» are the contradictory of His words, Exalted is He, «يدرك الأبصار» [Translator's note: so in the source; the argument requires the contradictory to be the affirmative «تدركه الأبصار», "the eyes perceive Him"], which entails that every single one sees Him [Translator's note: the source reads «لا يبصره», "does not see Him"], because the alif and lām, when they enter a plural, convey all-inclusiveness; and the contradictory of a universal negative is a particular affirmative. So the meaning of His words «لا تدركه الأبصار» is: not all eyes perceive Him — and we accept that, for not all eyes see Him; only the believers see Him. This subtle point is the meaning of their saying: the negation of generality does not convey negation [Translator's note: the usual formula is that the negation of generality (salb al-ʿumūm) does not convey general negation (ʿumūm al-salb)].

dervis-irab:104-107.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَصائِرُ): plural of بصيرة, which is the light of the heart by which one gains insight [Translator's note: the source prints «يستصر», evidently for «يستبصر»], while البصر is the light of the eye by which you see. It is applied to reason, intelligence, lesson, witness and proof. One says: جوارحه بصيرة عليه (his limbs are witness against him), and فراسة ذات بصيرة, i.e. true (insight). In al-Qāmūs: البصر, with vowelled letters, is the sense of the eye; the plural is أبصار, like سبب and أسباب.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ جاءَكُمْ بَصائِرُ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) Resumptive speech, brought on the tongue of the Prophet; what is meant by them (the بصائر) is the verses of the Qur'an. (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (جاءكم بصائر) is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a delayed agent; (من ربكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (جاءكم), or to an omitted adjective of (بصائر). (فَمَنْ أَبْصَرَ فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ عَمِيَ فَعَلَيْها) The fāʾ is resumptive, for detailing; (من) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أبصر) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then the seeing is for his own self"; and likewise (ومن عمي فعليها). The clause joined to the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من». (وَما أَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ بِحَفِيظٍ) The wāw is resumptive, and it may be circumstantial; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating (ما); (أنا) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as its noun; (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (حفيظ); the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and (حفيظ) is a noun genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ليس) [Translator's note: so in the source; the operator here is (ما), which works like (ليس)]. (وَكَذلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآياتِ وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرَسْتَ وَلِنُبَيِّنَهُ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a varying like the way We varied them in what is recited to you"; (الآيات) is the direct object. The wāw is a conjunction, and the lām is the lām of reason (taʿlīl); the verb after it, (يقولوا), is accusative by an implied أن. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ called it the lām of outcome or of becoming (lām al-ʿāqiba / al-ṣayrūra). The clause (ليقولوا) is conjoined to an implied element, i.e. "so that they take lesson and so that they say"; the clause (درست) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (ولنبينه): the wāw conjoins to the first lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (نصرف). The difference between the two lāms will come in the section on rhetoric.
The pronoun in «لنبينه» refers to the Qur'an, though it has not been mentioned, because it is known. (لقوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نبينه), and the clause (يعلمون) is an adjective of (قوم). (اتَّبِعْ ما أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) The clause is resumptive, addressed to the Prophet ﷺ. (اتبع) is an imperative verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت). «ما» may be a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the object of (اتبع), the resumptive pronoun being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (أوحي), and the clause being the ṣila (relative clause); or it may be maṣdariyya, in which case the preposition and its genitive noun are the deputy agent. (من ربك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being from your Lord". The clause (لا إله إلا هو) is parenthetical; the i'rab of the word of testimony has been given many times. (أعرض) is conjoined to (اتبع), and (عن المشركين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أعرض). (وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أَشْرَكُوا) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (لو) is conditional; (شاء ربك) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «شاء الله»] is a verb and its agent; the object of the willing is omitted, the implied form being "their not associating"; and the clause (ما أشركوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَما جَعَلْناكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظاً) The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (جعلناك) is a verb, an agent and a first direct object; (حفيظا) is the second object of (جعلنا); and (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «حفيظا». (وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِوَكِيلٍ) Conjoined to what precedes; its i'rab was given shortly before.

* Rhetoric:
Al-Zamakhsharī said — and it is among the choicest of the subtle points he brought: «If you ask: what difference is there between the two lāms in (ليقولوا) and (لنبينه)? I say: the difference between them is that the first is figurative and the second literal. That is because the verses were varied for making clear, and were not varied so that they would say "you have studied"; but because this saying came about through the varying of the verses, just as the making-clear came about through it, it was likened to it and brought in the same way.»

* Benefits:
In His word «درست» there are thirteen readings: three of them mutawātir and ten shādhdh (irregular). We have included them briefly:

The three mutawātir readings:
1- دَرَسْتَ on the pattern ضربت, active, the tāʾ being the agent, i.e.:
"you have studied, O Muḥammad."
2- دَرَسَتْ, the tāʾ being the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; its meaning is "they have become worn out and repeated in the ears."
3- دارَسْتَ on the pattern قاتلت, i.e. "you have studied together with others, O Muḥammad."

The ten shādhdh readings:
1- درّست: with doubling and in the second person, i.e. "you have studied the ancient books."
2- درّست: doubled, passive, in the second person.
3- دورست: without doubling, with a wāw, passive.
4- دورست: passive, predicated of the pronoun of the verses.
5- دارست: with the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine attached to the end of the verb.
6- درست: with fatḥa on the dāl and ḍamma on the rāʾ (دَرُسَتْ), predicated of the pronoun of the verses.
7- درس: its agent is the Prophet.
8- درسن: predicated of the feminine nūn, which is the pronoun of the verses.
9- درّسن: like the one before it, but with doubling, meaning:
their wearing-out became intense.
10- دارسات: plural of دارسة, meaning "ancient", or meaning "having become worn out".

dervis-irab:55-56.t:
* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ): a resumptive statement brought to explain the purpose of setting out the signs in detail. (كذلك) is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (الآيات) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw conjoins to an omitted element, the implied form being: "so that the truth may appear, and so that the way of the criminals may appear". The lām is for giving the reason; (تستبين) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām of reason; and (سبيل) is the fāʿil (agent). (السبيل) is feminine and may be masculine; it has been read «ليستبين», so the verb is feminine because (السبيل) is feminine and masculine because it is masculine.
(قُلْ: إِنِّي نُهِيتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): a resumptive statement brought to return to addressing them, to cut off their empty hopes. (قل) is an imperative verb; (إن) and its noun; the clause (نهيت) is its khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (أن) with what follows it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نهيت); the meaning is: "and I was forbidden from worshipping those whom you call upon". (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (تدعون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and (من دون الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تدعون).
(قُلْ لا أَتَّبِعُ أَهْواءَكُمْ قَدْ ضَلَلْتُ إِذاً وَما أَنَا مِنَ الْمُهْتَدِينَ): the statement is resumptive, brought so that he ﷺ returns to addressing them; He repeated it, despite its recent mention, for further emphasis. The clause (لا أتبع أهواءكم) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech; the clause (قد ضللت) is resumptive, brought from him ﷺ to affirm his desisting from what he was forbidden. (إذن) is a particle of answer and requital containing the sense of condition; the meaning is: "if I followed your desires I would go astray and would not be guided". So it is equivalent to a condition and an apodosis. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the negative Ḥijāzī mā, governing as (ليس) does; (أنا) is its noun; and (من المهتدين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar. He turned from the verbal to the nominal [clause] only to indicate permanence and continuity.

dervis-irab:57-58.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ: إِنِّي عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّي): a resumptive statement to explain the truth that the Prophet ﷺ follows and to crush the falsehood that they follow. (قل) is an imperative verb; the clause (إني على بينة) is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); (إن) and its noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate); and (من ربي) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of (بينة).
(وَكَذَّبْتُمْ بِهِ ما عِنْدِي ما تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِهِ): the wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to declare their denial abhorrent. It may also be circumstantial, so that the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «قد» must then be implied. (كذبتم) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and (به) is attached to (تستعجلون) [Translator's note: so in the source; the first (به) evidently belongs to (كذبتم)]. (ما) is negative; (عندي) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (تستعجلون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تستعجلون); and the clause (ما عندي) is resumptive.
(إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ يَقُصُّ الْحَقَّ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْفاصِلِينَ): a resumptive statement brought to explain that judgement belongs to Allah, Glorified is He. (إن) is negative; (الحكم) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of (الحكم); the clause (يقص الحق) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; and (الحق) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). In a reading: «يقضي الحق» with ḍād, from al-qaḍāʾ in the sense of judging and deciding by judgement. Ibn Jarīr preferred it, saying: "Because deciding between those who differ is only by judgement, not by narrating." (الحق) is then an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He judges with the true judgement". The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (خير الفاصلين) is the khabar.
(قُلْ: لَوْ أَنَّ عِنْدِي ما تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِهِ لَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ): the clause is resumptive, to explain that the matter goes back to Allah, Exalted is He. (لو) is conditional. (أن) with what falls within its scope is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "it were established"; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech. The adverb is attached to the omitted, fronted khabar of (أن); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the delayed noun of (أن); the clause (تستعجلون) is the ṣila; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تستعجلون); the lām occurs in the apodosis of (لو); (قضي) is a passive past verb; (الأمر) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (بيني) is an adverb of place attached to (قضي), and (بينكم) is likewise an adverb conjoined to the preceding adverb.
(وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِالظَّالِمِينَ): a resumptive statement. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ, (أعلم) the khabar, and (بالظالمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أعلم).

dervis-irab:59-59.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المفاتح): the plural of miftaḥ, with kasra on the mīm, which is the key (miftāḥ); it has also been read mafātīḥ. It has been said: mafātīḥ is the plural of miftāḥ, which is that by which one reaches what is in storehouses secured by locking. And it has been said: it is the plural of maftaḥ, with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the tāʾ, which is the storehouse (makhzan), in pattern and meaning.

* I'rab:
(وَعِنْدَهُ مَفاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لا يَعْلَمُها إِلَّا هُوَ): the statement is resumptive, brought to explain that matters of the unseen belong exclusively to Him, Glorified is He. The adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (مفاتح الغيب) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (لا يعلمها) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (مفاتح), its governor being the [notion of] being-settled to which the adverb is attached; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (هو) is the fāʿil (agent), or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) fāʿil — and perhaps this is preferable.
(وَيَعْلَمُ ما فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ وَما تَسْقُطُ مِنْ وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعْلَمُها): the wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negative [Translator's note: so in the source; no negative (ما) precedes (يعلم) here]; (يعلم) is an imperfect verb; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (في البر) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; and (البحر) is conjoined to (البر). The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (تسقط) is a nominative imperfect verb; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (ورقة) is genitive by (من) in wording and nominative by position as the fāʿil of (تسقط); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and the clause (يعلمها) is a ḥāl from (ورقة). The ḥāl came from an indefinite noun because it rests upon a negation.
(وَلا حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُماتِ الْأَرْضِ وَلا رَطْبٍ وَلا يابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (حبة) is conjoined to (ورقة), genitive in wording; had «حبة» been read in the nominative, by conjunction to the sense, it would have been permissible. (ولا رطب ولا يابس) are likewise conjoined to (ورقة). (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (في كتاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, and it is a repetition of His words (إلا يعلمها), as a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute); so it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains kinds of rhetoric that we summarize as follows:
1- The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya) in His words «مفاتح الغيب», as though the unseen had keys in His hand, Exalted is He, with which He uncovers what is hidden from people.
2- The explicit metaphor in His words «ظلمات» for the hardships and terrors of land and sea that disable the senses and bewilder the minds, because darkness disables the sense of sight. Hence a severe, hard day is called "a dark day" and "a day with stars", because the stars appear only in darkness — by way of explicit metaphor.
3- Ṭibāq (antithesis) between land and sea, and the moist and the dry; so it is a contrast (muqābala).
4- Repetition in His words «إلا يعلمها» and in His words «إلا في كتاب مبين», because the latter is equivalent to «إلا يعلمها». The benefit of this repetition is refreshing what has become distant: since, after negation was turned into the affirmation of knowledge intended in His words «إلا يعلمها», He conjoined [further items] to «ورقة», and these conjoined items were included in the affirmation of knowledge — which is the intent — and the end of them had become distant from its connection to the preceding affirmation, it was fitting to renew the connection with the intent. Then what befitted the eloquence customary in the Qur'an was to renew it in another expression, so that the hearer receives it fresh and new, not wearied by repetition.
5- Exhausting the particular and attaching it to the universal (ḥaṣr al-juzʾī wa-ilḥāquhu bi-l-kullī): this is that the speaker comes to some species and, to magnify it, makes it a genus, after exhausting the divisions of its species and genera. For He, Glorified is He, after reporting that with Him are the keys of every unseen thing — since the lām here is for the genus — in general terms, praised Himself in that He knows what is in land and sea of the kinds of animals, plants and minerals, exhausting the universal "generated things" (al-muwalladāt). He, Glorified is He, saw that confining Himself to that would not complete [Translator's note: the source prints «لا بكمل», evidently «لا يكمل»] the meaning of self-praise, because a weak person might think that He knows the universals but not the particulars; for the three generated things — even if they are particulars relative to the world — are each universal relative to what lies under it of intermediate genera, species and their kinds. So for the perfection of self-praise He said: «وما تسقط من ورقة إلا يعلمها». And He knew that some of His creatures might share knowledge of that with Him — everyone for whom He created perception and whom He guided to the way of that — and so share in it; so He praised Himself with what none shares in by His words: «ولا حبة في ظلمات الأرض». Then He attached these particulars, after exhausting them, to the universals when He said: «ولا رطب ولا يابس», because all generated things and the elements from which they were generated — whatever is in the interior of the earth and whatever has come out to its surface — do not go beyond these two divisions. He omitted mention of the temperate, for it is a mixture of these two divisions, and so He sufficed with mentioning the root instead of the branch. Then He said: «إلا في كتاب مبين», indicating that His knowledge of that is a knowledge, of what He knows, recorded [Translator's note: the source prints «مفيد» (beneficial), evidently for «مقيد» (recorded)] in a clear Book; so it is safe from error and forgetting.

Poetic examples:
Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī said, glancing at this lofty heaven of eloquence:
هي الغرض الأقصى ورؤيتك المنى ... ومنزلك الدنيا وأنت الخلائق
(It is the furthest goal; seeing you is the wish; your dwelling is the world, and you are all creatures.)
He intended to magnify the one he praised, so he made his dwelling, which is particular, universal, namely the world; and he made his person, which is particular, universal, namely all creatures. So he made the particular universal. As for exhausting the divisions of the particular, it is because the world is either an animal with its body and accident [Translator's note: so in the source; the sentence appears incomplete], and the dwelling comprises both. Similar is the saying of Abū al-Faraj al-Babbaghāʾ:
ما بأرض لم تبد فيها صباح ... ما بدار حللت فيها ظلام
وإذا ما أقمت في بلد فه ... ي جميع الدّنيا وأنت الأنام
(There is no morning in a land where you do not appear; there is no darkness in a house where you alight. And when you stay in a town, it is the whole world, and you are mankind.)
He exhausted all the divisions of the particular in the way we mentioned and attached it to the universal. And Abū al-Ḥasan al-Salāmī said:
إليك طوى عرض البسيطة جاعل ... قصارى المطايا أن يلوح لها القصر
فكنت وعزمي والظّلام وصارمي ... ثلاثة أشباه كما اجتمع النسر
فسرت بآمالي لملك هو الورى ... ودار هي الدّنيا ويوم هو الدهر
(To you folded up the breadth of the earth one who made the utmost aim of the mounts that the palace should gleam before them. I, my resolve, the darkness and my sword were three alike, as the [stars of the] Eagle gather. So I journeyed with my hopes to a king who is all mankind, a house that is the world, and a day that is all time.)
The last line is the one intended. The poet wished to magnify the one he praised, to exalt the house in which he visited him, and to honour the day on which he met him; so he made the one praised all mankind, made the house in which he visited him the whole world, and made the day on which he met him the whole of time. So he made the particular universal after exhausting the divisions of the particular. As for making the particular universal: the one praised is part of mankind, his house is part of the world, and the day of meeting him is part of time. As for exhausting the divisions of the particular: the world consists of bodies, adverbs of time and adverbs of place, and he exhausted all of that in mentioning the one praised, his house and the day of meeting him. As for attaching the particular to the universal: it is because he attached the one praised to all mankind in that he made him the weight of all mankind, in the manner of the saying of Abū Nuwās:
ليس على الله بمستنكر ... أن يجمع العالم في واحد
(It is not deemed impossible for Allah to gather the whole world in a single man.)

dervis-irab:108-109.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عَدْواً): wrongfully and aggressively.
(جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ): الجهد with fatḥa on the jīm is hardship, and with ḍamma (الجُهد) is capacity.
(يُشْعِرُكُمْ): makes you aware and informs you.

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَسُبُّوا الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) Resumptive speech, brought to forbid something which is obligatory in itself but which leads to the reviling of Allah the Exalted; for that reason the prohibition of it was issued — and many an act of obedience has drawn on to an act of disobedience. (لا) is prohibitive; (تسبوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by it, and the wāw is the agent; (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يدعون) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (من دون الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ عَدْواً بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) The fāʾ is the causal fāʾ (al-sababiyya); (يسبوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after it, because it is preceded by a prohibition, i.e. "do not revile their gods, for there may follow from that what you hate, the reviling of Allah." The fāʾ may also be a conjunction, with (يسبوا) conjoined to (تسبوا). The Divine Name is the direct object. (عدوا) is accusative as a maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq), because it is synonymous with it [Translator's note: i.e. with the reviling]; it may correctly be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of aggression"; and it may be a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, because reviling is never anything but aggression. (بغير علم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted emphasising ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida). (كَذلِكَ زَيَّنَّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمْ) (كذلك): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "We made their deeds seem fair to these with a making-fair like Our making-fair to every community their deeds." (زينا) is a verb and its agent; (لكل أمة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (زينا); (عملهم) is the direct object; and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (ثُمَّ إِلى رَبِّهِمْ مَرْجِعُهُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay, conjoining to an omitted element whose implied form is "so they come to Him". (إلى ربهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and (مرجعهم) is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). (فينبئهم): the fāʾ is a conjunction for sequence with immediacy, to affirm that rebuke and reproach follow upon the return swiftly and without respite. (ينبئهم) is an imperfect verb, and the hāʾ is the first direct object; (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun in the place of the second object of (ينبئهم); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila, and the clause (يعملون) is the khabar of (كانوا). (وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ) The wāw is resumptive; (أقسموا) is a verb and its agent; (بالله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أقسموا). (جهد أيمانهم) is accusative as a maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq), i.e. "they swore the utmost of their swearings", (الأيمان) being in the sense of swearings, as you say: "I struck him the hardest of blows." It was also said:
it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "they swore, striving hard in their oaths." Al-Mubarrad said: it is accusative by a verb from its own root. (أيمانهم) is muḍāf ilayhi, a case of annexing the maṣdar to its object. (لَئِنْ جاءَتْهُمْ آيَةٌ لَيُؤْمِنُنَّ بِها قُلْ إِنَّمَا الْآياتُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) The lām is the one preparing for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) is conditional; (جاءتهم) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its object; (آية) is the agent. (ليؤمنن): the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, since the oath precedes the condition. (يؤمنن) is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, is the agent; and the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis. (بها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يؤمنن). (قل) is an imperative verb, and the clause is resumptive. (إنما) is the restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (الآيات) is a mubtadaʾ, and (عند الله) is an adverb attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (وَما يُشْعِرُكُمْ أَنَّها إِذا جاءَتْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to show the wisdom that called for the answer to take this form. (ما) is an interrogative noun of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يشعركم) is its khabar; the kāf is the first object of (يشعركم), and (أنّ) with what falls in its scope is in the place of the second object. (إذا) is an adverb attached to (يؤمنون), and the clause (لا يؤمنون) is the khabar of (أنها). More will be said on this inimitable construction.

* Benefits:
The scholars disagreed much about this inimitable construction, and we shall choose what is most in keeping with logic and taste. Some illustrated this construction with an example: if someone says to you, "Honour so-and-so, for he will repay you", while you know of him that he will not, you say in reply, "And what makes you know that if I honour him he will repay me?" — so you disapprove of his affirming the repayment. If the matter is reversed and he says to you, "Do not honour him, for he will not repay you", while you know of him that he will repay, and you disapprove of the one advising you to deny him, you say:
"And what makes you know that he will not repay me?", meaning: "while I know of him that he will repay." So what disapproval of the believers — who thought well of the obstinate and believed they would believe when the requested sign came down — would require is to say: "And what makes you know that, when it comes, they will believe?", dropping «لا». Since the verse came in this form, the scholars disagreed. Some took «لا» to be redundant (zāʾida); some interpreted «أنّ» as «لعل» (perhaps), from the Arabs' saying: "Go to the market; perhaps (أنك) you will buy meat"; and they cited as evidence the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
عوجا على الطّلل المحيل لأننا ... نبكي الديار كما بلى ابن حزام
(Turn aside to the time-worn ruin — perhaps we may weep over the abodes as Ibn Ḥizām wept.) [Translator's note: the source prints «بلى», evidently for «بكى».]
i.e. "لعلنا" (perhaps we). Others made the speech the answer to an omitted oath — the hamza of (أن) may take fatḥa after an oath — and said: the implied form is "By Allah, when it comes they will not believe." The soundest view is that the verse remains on its apparent sense and that all of this is mere strain. To make this clear it is said: if you have denied Zayd (your generosity) because you know that he will not repay, and someone advises you to honour him, on the basis that the adviser supposes repayment, you have two possible stances with him: a stance in which you disapprove of his claiming knowledge of what you know to be otherwise, and a stance in which you excuse him for not knowing what you have encompassed in knowledge. If you disapprove of him, you say: "And what makes you know that he will repay?" And if you excuse him for not knowing that he will not repay, you say: "And what makes you know that he will not repay?", meaning: "And how could you know what I know of his not repaying, when you have not tested his affair as I have tested it, nor sounded his depths as I have sounded them?" So too the verse: the speech in it came only to establish an excuse for the believers in their not knowing what is hidden in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, namely the non-belief of these people. Thus the entry of «لا» is sound, and it becomes clear that the cause of the confusion was mistaking disapproval for the establishing of excuses. This is among the loftiest proofs of inimitability.

dervis-irab:110-110.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَعْمَهُونَ): imperfect of «عمه» في طغيانه, with the maṣdar عمه, of the pattern تعب:
when one wavers in bewilderment. It is taken from their saying أرض عمهاء, when there are no signs of safe passage in it. So he is عمه and أعمه.

* I'rab:
(وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصارَهُمْ كَما لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ) The wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; (نقلب) is an imperfect verb; (أفئدتهم) is its object, and (أبصارهم) is conjoined to (أفئدتهم). (كما): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element whose implied form is "so they do not believe, just as they were when the signs came down at their first request", because their hearts are sealed; it is thus a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (ما) is maṣdariyya; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive; (يؤمنوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم); (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يؤمنوا); and (أول مرة) is an adverb of time attached to (يؤمنوا). (وَنَذَرُهُمْ فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (نذرهم) is conjoined to (لا يؤمنون), falling within the domain of the disapproval and restricted by what it is restricted by. (في طغيانهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يعمهون), and the clause (يعمهون) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "bewildered".

dervis-irab:111-111.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قُبُلًا): with two ḍammas, plural of قبيل; its parallels are رغيف and رغف, قضيب and قضب. Or it is the plural of قبيل in the sense of كفيل (guarantor).

* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ أَنَّنا نَزَّلْنا إِلَيْهِمُ الْمَلائِكَةَ وَكَلَّمَهُمُ الْمَوْتى) The wāw is resumptive; (لو) is conditional; (أن) with what falls in its scope is the agent of an omitted verb, i.e. "were it established (that)".
The clause (نزلنا إليهم الملائكة) is the khabar (predicate) of (أن), and (كلّمهم) is conjoined to (نزلنا). That is what they requested when they said: "Why are the angels not sent down to us?" (الموتى) is the fāʿil (agent). (وَحَشَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلًا) The wāw is also a conjunction; (حشرنا) is a verb and its agent, conjoined to (نزلنا), i.e. as they also said. (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (حشرنا); (كل شيء) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (قبلا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.:
"group after group", or "as guarantors", as was given in the section on vocabulary. (ما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. (ما) is negating; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); (يؤمنوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an أن necessarily implied after the lām of denial [Translator's note: the source repeats this sentence twice]; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element, which is the khabar, i.e.:
"they were not fit for belief." (إلا) is a particle of exception from the most general of states, so it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), the meaning being: "they would not believe in any state at all except in the state of Allah's willing"; so (أن) and what follows it is a maṣdar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. Or it is an exception from the most general of times, so the maṣdar is in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time: "except at the time of Allah's willing". Or it is an exception from a general cause, i.e.:
"they would not believe for any reason at all except for Allah's willing (their) belief", so it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The exception may also be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), with (أن) and what it governs interpreted as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "but Allah's will comes about"; the argument of those who hold this is that Allah's will is not of the same kind as their wishes. (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَجْهَلُونَ) The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (لكن) and its noun, and the clause (يجهلون) is its khabar.

dervis-irab:112-113.t:
* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ جَعَلْنا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا شَياطِينَ الْإِنْسِ وَالْجِنِّ) Resumptive speech, brought to console the Prophet ﷺ for the hostility of Quraysh that he witnessed against him and the conspiracies they were plotting by night. The kāf is in the position of the accusative, being, together with what it governs, an adjective of an omitted maṣdar emphasising what follows it. (جعلنا) is a verb and its agent, and it takes two objects. (لكل نبي) is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of «عدوا»; (عدوا) is the second object of (جعلنا), and (شياطين الإنس والجن) is the first object of (جعلنا). (يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلى بَعْضٍ زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ غُرُوراً) The clause may be resumptive, to show the state of the enemy. It was called "inspiration" (وحي) because it takes place only secretly among them, and their deceptive embellishment was made "gilded speech" because they adorn it. It may also be a ḥāl from it [Translator's note: i.e. from the enemy]. (يوحي) is an imperfect verb; (بعضهم) is the fāʿil (agent); (إلى بعض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يوحي); (زخرف القول) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (غرورا) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "in order to deceive them"; or a maṣdar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "deceiving"; or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because the meaning of "some of them inspire others" is "they deceive them by that with a deceiving". (وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ ما فَعَلُوهُ فَذَرْهُمْ وَما يَفْتَرُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; (لو) is conditional; (شاء ربك) is a verb and its agent, and it is the protasis of (لو); its object is omitted — its discussion has been given before. The clause (ما فعلوه) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ of eloquence, implying an omitted clause); (ذرهم) is an imperative verb with a latent agent, and the hāʾ is the direct object. The wāw is a conjunction, and (ما) is a relative noun conjoined to the hāʾ in (فذرهم), i.e. "leave them and leave what they fabricate". The wāw may also be in the sense of "with", and (ما) a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); and (ما) may be maṣdariyya, i.e.:
"leave them and leave their fabrication." This verse was revealed before the command to fight. (وَلِتَصْغى إِلَيْهِ أَفْئِدَةُ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ) The wāw is a conjunction and the lām is for giving the reason (taʿlīl); (تصغى) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to «غرورا». It was not made accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi only because the agent differs — the agent of (تصغى) is the deceived, while the agent of the first is the deceivers [Translator's note: the source prints «الفارّون», "those who flee", evidently for «الغارّون», "the deceivers"] — and because it is not an explicit maṣdar; so two of the conditions for making the mafʿūl li-ajlihi accusative are missing. The meaning of (تصغى) is "inclines". (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تصغى); (أفئدة) is the agent of (تصغى); (الذين) is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause (لا يؤمنون) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (بالآخرة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يؤمنون). (وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْتَرِفُوا ما هُمْ مُقْتَرِفُونَ) Also conjoined to «غرورا», i.e. the lām is for giving the reason and has kasra, and «أن» is optionally implied after it in all three verbs. Their order is extremely fine and at the summit of eloquence, because first comes the deception, then the inclining, then the being pleased, then the committing (of sin): each one is caused by what precedes it. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to call these lāms the lām of becoming or of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra / al-ʿāqiba), and that is not far-fetched.

dervis-irab:114-115.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَكَماً): a judge who judges only with justice. It is more intensive than حاكم, because the حكم judges only with justice, while the حاكم may overstep and act unjustly; or because judging is repeated from the حكم, unlike the حاكم, which is true of (one who judged) a single time. Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī gazed up at the sky of this word in his words:
يا أعدل الناس إلّا في معاملتي ... فيك الخصام وأنت الخصم والحكم
(O most just of people, except in your dealings with me: the dispute is about you, and you are both the adversary and the judge.)

* I'rab:
(أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْتَغِي حَكَماً) The clause is conjoined to an implied element required by the context of the speech, i.e. "say to them: shall I incline to the ornaments of this world and so seek a judge?" The hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); it is the object of an omitted speech, and the clause of speech is resumptive. (غير الله) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (أبتغي), and (حكما) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a tamyīz (specification). «حكما» may also be the direct object, with «غير» a ḥāl from «حكما», because it was originally an adjective of it. (وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكِتابَ مُفَصَّلًا) The wāw is circumstantial, and the clause is a ḥāl emphasising the disapproval. (هو) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) the khabar (predicate); the clause (أنزل) is the ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position; (إليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنزل); (الكتاب) is the direct object; and (مفصلا) is a ḥāl from (الكتاب). (وَالَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ مُنَزَّلٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ بِالْحَقِّ فَلا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought from Allah the Exalted to affirm that the Book is a reality sent down from Him, Exalted is He. (الذين) is a relative noun, the mubtadaʾ; the clause (آتيناهم) is the ṣila; (الكتاب) is the second direct object; and the clause (يعلمون) is the khabar of the relative noun. (أنّ), its noun and its khabar stand in place of the two objects of (يعلمون). (من ربك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (منزل); (بالحق) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the nominative pronoun in «منزل», which is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The fāʾ in «فلا» is the faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you know this and are certain of it, then do not be". (لا) is prohibitive; (تكونن) is a defective imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn, and it is in the position of the jussive by the prohibitive (لا); its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); and (من الممترين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar. The address, though on the surface of the speech directed to the Prophet ﷺ, is in reality directed to his community. (وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقاً وَعَدْلًا) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to begin showing the perfection of the Book. (كلمة ربك) is the agent of (تمت), and (صدقا) and (عدلا) are a ḥāl. Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Ṭabarī parsed them as a tamyīz, and al-Jalāl followed them; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected this view and said: «It is not correct.» Perhaps what he meant is that truth and justice belong to the very nature of the words of Allah, and a tamyīz only explains what is vague, and there is no vagueness in that. Al-Kawāshī parsed them as a ḥāl from «ربك», or as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). If we parse them as two ḥāls, they must be interpreted in the sense of a derived word, i.e. "truthful and just". Al-Zamakhsharī confined himself to the ḥāl.
I say: I do not consider it far-fetched that they be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with truth and justice", to avoid the interpretation; or that they be adjectives of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a completion of truth and justice" [Translator's note: the source prints «نمام», evidently for «تمام»]. (لا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِماتِهِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) The clause is a ḥāl from the agent of (تمت), or resumptive. (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (مبدل) is its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa; and (لكلماته) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of «لا».
(وهو السميع العليم): the wāw is resumptive; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (السميع) is a first khabar and (العليم) a second khabar.

dervis-irab:60-60.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جَرَحْتُمْ): you earned. In al-Miṣbāḥ: jaraḥa, of the pattern-class nafaḥa, and ijtaraḥa: he worked with his hand and earned; from this, birds of prey and beasts of prey that hunt are called jawāriḥ, because they earn with their hands.

* I'rab:
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ): a resumptive statement brought to address the disbelievers. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) its khabar (predicate); the clause (يتوفاكم) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and (بالليل) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتوفاكم).
(وَيَعْلَمُ ما جَرَحْتُمْ بِالنَّهارِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يعلم) is conjoined to (يتوفاكم); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the object of (يعلم); and the clause (جرحتم) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. «ما» may also be maṣdariyya, the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) being the object of (جرحتم) [Translator's note: so in the source; on this view the interpreted maṣdar would be the object of (يعلم)].
(ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُكُمْ فِيهِ لِيُقْضى أَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى): (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (يبعثكم) is conjoined to (يتوفاكم); (فيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يبعثكم); the lām is for giving the reason; (يقضى) is a passive imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām of reason, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (يبعثكم); (أجل) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and (مسمى) an adjective.
(ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): conjoined to the preceding clause. (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (مرجعكم) is a delayed mubtadaʾ; (ثم ينبئكم) is likewise conjoined; (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ينبئكم); the clause (كنتم تعملون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; and the clause (تعملون) is the khabar of (كنتم).

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is "al-tanzīl al-manẓūm" (versified revelation), which is what occurs in the Qur'an in metre without the intention of poetry. That is in His words «ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار», which is a hemistich of a line in the wāfir metre. There is found in the Qur'an what is a complete line or a hemistich; yet it does not acquire the name of poetry, nor does its author acquire the name of poet.
We will cite for you a group of verses that occurred in metre — and pay no heed to those who say that they are poetry. Among them are His words, Exalted is He, in the ṭawīl metre, a hemistich of a line: «فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر». In the madīd: «واصنع الفلك بأعيننا». In the basīṭ: «فأصبحوا لا يرى إلا مساكنهم». In the khafīf: «لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا». It may be a complete line, as in His words, in the majzūʾ al-ramal: «وجفان كالجوابي وقدور راسيات»:
وجفان كالجوابي ... وقدور راسيات
And His words in the same metre:
لن تنالوا البرّ حتى ... تنفقوا مما تحبّون
And in the majzūʾ al-kāmil:
والله يهدي من يشاء ... إلى صراط مستقيم
And in the mujtathth:
نبّىء عبادي أنّي ... أنا الغفور الرحيم
Poets have played with this subject and included in their lines verses that occurred in metre without intention, and some of it turned out curious and sweet. It is reported of Abū Nuwās that he included this in his saying:
وفتية في مجلس وجوههم ... ريحانهم قد عدموا التّثقيلا
دانية عليهم ظلالها ... وذلّلت قطوفها تذليلا
(Youths in a gathering whose faces are their sweet basil, free of all heaviness; its shades close down over them, and its clusters hang low and humbled.)
It is in the rajaz metre, and the mīm in «عليهم» must be lengthened for the metre to be correct. There is no avoiding here a reference to the disagreement that arose among the scholars over the permissibility of quoting the noble verses (iqtibās); what the majority of them hold is that it is permissible on condition that the versifier does not descend to meanings and subjects incompatible with the majesty of the Qur'an. Among the curious things mentioned in this regard is that someone composed a line in which he said:
وما حسن بيت له زخرف ... تراه إذا زلزلت لم يكن
(What is the beauty of a house with ornament (zukhruf)? You see it, when [the earth] is shaken, as though it never was.)
Then he hesitated because he had used these Qur'anic words in poetry, so he came to the Shaykh al-Islām Taqī al-Dīn ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd to ask him about it, and recited the line to him. The shaykh said to him: "Say: «فما حسن كهف» (what is the beauty of a cave)." He said to him: "My master, you have both benefited me and given me a fatwā." [Translator's note: the names Zukhruf, Zalzala and Kahf are all titles of sūras; the shaykh's quip answers in the same playful vein.]

dervis-irab:61-62.t:
* I'rab:
(وَهُوَ الْقاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبادِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ عَلَيْكُمْ حَفَظَةً): a resumptive statement brought to explain that He, Glorified is He, is the Dominant, the Subduer, who disposes of the affairs of His servants. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (القاهر) its khabar (predicate); (فوق) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being exalted". (ويرسل): the wāw is resumptive, and there is no harm in its being a conjunction, as a case of conjoining a verbal clause to a nominal clause. (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يرسل), and (حفظة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The preposition and its genitive noun may also be attached to (حفظة), because it is the plural of ḥāfiẓ, which is an active participle, i.e. "He sends those who preserve your deeds against you".
(حَتَّى إِذا جاءَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنا): (حتى) is inceptive or of limit, and it has preceded many times. (إذا) is an adverb of the future attached to (توفته); the clause (جاء) is in the position of the genitive by annexation; (أحدكم) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and (الموت) a delayed fāʿil (agent); and the clause (توفته رسلنا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(وَهُمْ لا يُفَرِّطُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (لا يفرطون) is in the position of the nominative as the khabar; and the clause is a ḥāl. You may also make the wāw resumptive, the clause being resumptive, brought to explain that they neglect nothing of the affairs of the servants.
(ثُمَّ رُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلاهُمُ الْحَقِّ): (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (ردوا) is a passive past verb and the wāw its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause (ردوا) is conjoined to (توفته); (إلى الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ردوا); (مولاهم) is a badal (substitute) of (الله) or a naʿt (adjective) of it; and (الحق) is a naʿt of (مولاهم).
(أَلا لَهُ الْحُكْمُ وَهُوَ أَسْرَعُ الْحاسِبِينَ): (ألا) is a particle of drawing attention and opening; (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (الحكم) is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (أسرع الحاسبين) its khabar; and the clause is resumptive.

dervis-irab:63-64.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ مَنْ يُنَجِّيكُمْ مِنْ ظُلُماتِ الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ): a resumptive statement to establish the proof against unjust humanity, which appears weak when it falls into hardship, and when the hardship is removed from it, returns to its error, its vehemence and its arrogance. (قل) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (من) is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (ينجيكم) is the khabar (predicate); (من ظلمات) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينجيكم); the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); (البر) is muḍāf ilayhi; and (البحر) is conjoined to (البر).
(تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً): the clause (تدعونه) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in (ينجيكم), i.e. "He saves you while you are calling upon Him". As for what al-Jalāl [al-Maḥallī] inclined to — supplying an adverb and making it [the clause] in the position of the genitive by annexation — it is very far-fetched, because omitting the word annexed to a clause has not been heard in their speech. (تدعونه) is a nominative imperfect verb, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (تضرعا) and (خفية) are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the place of a ḥāl from the wāw, i.e. "you call upon Him while humbly beseeching and in secret". They may also be parsed as two maṣdars from the meaning of the governor, not from its wording, as in their saying: «قعدت جلوسا» (I sat down a sitting).
(لَئِنْ أَنْجانا مِنْ هذِهِ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ): this clause is accusative by an intended speech, the speech being a ḥāl, i.e. "you call upon Him, saying that". It may also have no grammatical position, because it explains the supplication. The lām paves the way for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) is conditional; (أنجانا) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its fāʿil being "He", and (نا) is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; (من هذه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنجانا), the reference being to the darknesses, which are treated as a singular. (لنكونن): the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; the clause (نكونن من الشاكرين) has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, since the oath comes first, according to the rule; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted because it comes later, as in the saying of Ibn Mālik:
واحذف لدى اجتماع شرط وقسم ... جواب ما أخرت فهو ملتزم
(When a condition and an oath come together, omit the answer of whichever you put later; this is binding.)
(من الشاكرين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of (نكونن).
(قُلِ اللَّهُ يُنَجِّيكُمْ مِنْها): the clause is resumptive. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (ينجيكم) is its khabar; (منها) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ينجيكم), i.e. from the darknesses; and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the speech.
(وَمِنْ كُلِّ كَرْبٍ ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ تُشْرِكُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (من كل كرب) is conjoined to the genitive pronoun, with the preposition repeated, as is the rule; (ثم) is a conjunction; (أنتم) is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause (تشركون) is the khabar.

dervis-irab:131-134.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ أَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ رَبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ الْقُرى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُها غافِلُونَ) The clause is resumptive (istīnāfiyya), serving as a justification. The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is what follows it, i.e. "that is established"; or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that"; and the pointing refers to what preceded of the sending of the messengers to them and their warning them. أَنْ is the lightened form of the heavy (أَنَّ), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); together with what follows it, it is in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar, and also attached to an omitted element that is a badal (substitute) for ذلِكَ if it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. لَمْ is a particle of negation, and يَكُنْ is an imperfect verb made jussive by لَمْ; the clause «لم يكن» is the khabar of «أن». رَبُّكَ is the noun of يَكُنْ, and مُهْلِكَ الْقُرى is its khabar. بِظُلْمٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ذلك, i.e. "coupled with wrongdoing", or from the agent of مُهْلِكَ, and the two come to one meaning, or from الْقُرى, i.e. "coupled with their sins". وَأَهْلُها: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); أَهْلُها is a mubtadaʾ and غافِلُونَ a khabar, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl.
(وَلِكُلٍّ دَرَجاتٌ مِمَّا عَمِلُوا وَما رَبُّكَ بِغافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to set out the condition of the believers and the disbelievers. وَلِكُلٍّ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and the tanwīn in كُلٍّ is a substitute for the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement), i.e. "and for every group"; an important discussion of the tanwīn and its kinds will come in the section on Benefits. دَرَجاتٌ is a postponed mubtadaʾ. مِمَّا: مِنْ is a preposition, and مَا is either a maṣdar particle (maṣdariyya) or a relative (mawṣūla); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of دَرَجاتٌ. The clause عَمِلُوا has no grammatical position in either case. وَما رَبُّكَ: the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; مَا is the Hijazi negative that works like لَيْسَ; رَبُّكَ is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and غافِلٍ is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of «ما». عَمَّا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to غافِلٍ, and the clause يَعْمَلُونَ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative مَا.
(وَرَبُّكَ الْغَنِيُّ ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ) A resumptive statement. رَبُّكَ is a mubtadaʾ, الْغَنِيُّ is the first khabar, and ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ is a second khabar.
(إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَسْتَخْلِفْ مِنْ بَعْدِكُمْ ما يَشاءُ) The conditional clause is a third khabar. It is also permissible to parse «الْغَنِيُّ» and «ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ» as two naʿts of «رَبُّكَ», in which case the conditional clause is the khabar of «رَبُّكَ». إِنْ is conditional. يَشَأْ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive; يُذْهِبْكُمْ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). وَيَسْتَخْلِفْ: the wāw is a conjunction, and يَسْتَخْلِفْ is an imperfect verb conjoined to يُذْهِبْكُمْ. مِنْ بَعْدِكُمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. مَا is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as direct object, and the clause يَشاءُ is the ṣila of the relative and has no position.
(كَما أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ) كَما: the preposition and its genitive noun are a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); parallels to it have already been given. أَنْشَأَكُمْ consists of a verb, a latent agent and a direct object. مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أَنْشَأَكُمْ, and قَوْمٍ is a muḍāf ilayhi. آخَرِينَ is a naʿt of قَوْمٍ.
(إِنَّ ما تُوعَدُونَ لَآتٍ وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ) A resumptive statement introduced to confirm what preceded. إِنَّ and its noun; the clause تُوعَدُونَ is the ṣila of the relative, and it is passive, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "that with which (به) you are threatened, of the Hour and the punishment". The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and آتٍ is the khabar of إِنَّ. وَما: the wāw is a conjunction; مَا is the Hijazi negative; أَنْتُمْ is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and مُعْجِزِينَ is genitive in form and accusative in position as its khabar.

* Benefits:
The tanwīn: it is a quiescent nūn that is attached to the end of a word in pronunciation but not in writing, for a purpose other than emphasis. Its well-known kinds are four:

1- Tanwīn al-tamkīn (the tanwīn of firmness):
This is the one attached to declinable nouns. Its benefit is to indicate the firmness of the noun in nounhood, as in: جاء زيد ("Zayd came"), ورأيت زيدا ("and I saw Zayd"), ومررت بزيد ("and I passed by Zayd").

2- Tanwīn al-tankīr (the tanwīn of indefiniteness):
This is the one attached to some indeclinable nouns to distinguish the definite from the indefinite among them. It is regular (qiyāsī) in the case of a proper name ending in -wayhi, as in: مررت بسيبويه وسيبويه آخر ("I passed by Sībawayh and another Sībawayh"), and it is by hearsay (samāʿī) in the case of verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl) when they are made indefinite, as in إيه with kasra on the hamza and kasra on the hāʾ without tanwīn, and as in the words of Ḥāfiẓ Ibrāhīm in his elegy for Saʿd Zaghlūl:
إيه يا ليل هل شهدت المصابا ... كيف ينصبّ في النفوس انصبابا
(Go on, O night! Did you witness the calamity? How it poured down upon the souls in a flood!)
For if you wish to ask for more of some talk, you add tanwīn and say: إيهٍ.

3- Tanwīn al-muqābala (the tanwīn of correspondence):
This is the one attached to the sound feminine plural, as in: رأيت مؤمنات ("I saw believing women"). It is so called because it corresponds to the nūn of the sound masculine plural.

4- Tanwīn al-ʿiwaḍ (the tanwīn of compensation):
This is what is brought as compensation either for a word that is a muḍāf ilayhi after كل and بعض, as in the verse above «ولكلّ», i.e. "for every group"; or as compensation for a letter that analogy requires to be dropped, and this is the one attached to the defective diptote noun, as in: جوار and غواش; or as compensation for a clause, and this is the one attached to the word «إذ» when it occurs as a muḍāf ilayhi, as in: وأنتم حينئذ تنظرون ("and you at that moment are looking on"), where the tanwīn is a compensation for a clause, i.e. "at the time when (the soul) reaches the throat".
These four kinds are the basis of the tanwīn, and a group of scholars, among them Ibn Hishām in Mughnī al-labīb and Ibn al-Khabbāz in Sharḥ al-Jazūliyya, added to these four kinds:

1- Tanwīn al-tarannum (the tanwīn of chanting):
This is the one attached to the free rhymes (al-qawāfī al-muṭlaqa), i.e. those that end in a letter of prolongation, namely alif, wāw and yāʾ generated by the lengthening of the vowel, and they are called the letters of release (aḥruf al-iṭlāq), as in the words of Jarīr:
أقلّى اللوم عاذل والعتابن ... وقولي إن أصبت لقد أصابن
(Lessen the blame, O censurer, and the reproach, and say, "If you are right, you have indeed hit the mark.")
So the tanwīn was attached to the ʿarūḍ and the rhyme-word, namely العتابن and أصابن; the original was العتابا and أصابا, and the tanwīn was brought in place of the alif. The first is a noun and the second a verb. It may also be attached to a particle, as in the words of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
أزف التّرحّل غير أنّ ركابنا ... لمّا تزل برحالنا وكأن قد
(The departure has drawn near, except that our mounts have not yet moved off with our saddles, and it is as if they already had.)
The original is قدي, and the tanwīn was brought in place of the yāʾ.
2- Al-tanwīn al-ghālī (the excessive tanwīn):
This is the one attached to the bound rhymes (al-qawāfī al-muqayyada), i.e. those whose rhyme letter (rawī) is quiescent and not a letter of prolongation, as an addition to the metre; for this reason it is called "excessive" (ghālī), i.e. because it goes beyond the limit of the metre, as in the words of Ruʾba the rajaz poet:
وقاتم الأعماق خاوي المخترقن ... مشتبه الأعلام لمّاع الخفقن
(Many a dusty, deep-reaching waste, empty to cross, its landmarks alike, its mirages flashing...)

3- Tanwīn al-ḍarūra (the tanwīn of necessity):
This is the one attached to what is not fully declinable, as in the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
ويوم دخلت الخدر خدر عنيزة ... فقالت: لك الويلات إنّك مرجلي
(And the day I entered the howdah, the howdah of ʿUnayza, she said, "Woe to you! You are making me go on foot.")
and to the vocative with ḍamma, as in the words of al-Aḥwaṣ:
سلام الله يا مطر عليها ... وليس عليك يا مطر السلام
(The peace of Allah, O Maṭar, be upon her; but upon you, O Maṭar, be no peace.)

4- Al-tanwīn al-shādhdh (the anomalous tanwīn):
As in the saying of some of them, reported by Abū Zayd: هؤلاء قومك.

5- Tanwīn al-ḥikāya (the tanwīn of quotation):
Such as when you name a man ʿĀqila: you quote the word as heard. Thus we arrive at nine kinds. Ibn al-Khabbāz made each of the tanwīn of the vocative with ḍamma and the tanwīn of the diptote a kind in its own right, so that he arrived at ten kinds, which we have set out merely for information and curiosity; otherwise some of them are not acceptable and are not accepted by the linguistic taste, and that is grasped intuitively.

dervis-irab:135-136.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَكانَتِكُمْ): There is disagreement about the mīm of «مكان» and «مكانة». It is said that it is original, and both come from مكن يمكن; and it is said that it is redundant, and both come from الكون. The meaning on the first view is: "according to your capacity in your affair, your utmost ability and your potential", مكانة being a maṣdar. On the second view: "act according to your condition, which you are in".
(ذَرَأَ): He created. ذرأ الله الخلق ("Allah created the creation"), and ذرأنا الأرض وذروناها, i.e. we sowed it with seed. And ذرأة has come over him, which is the whiteness of grey hair when it first appears at the two temples of it; a man is أذرأ and a woman ذرآء. He said:
فمرّ ولمّا تسخن الشمس غدوة ... بذرآء تدري كيف تمشي المنائح
(He passed by, while the sun had not yet warmed in the morning, a grey-haired she-camel that knows how milch camels walk.)
i.e. she has been given as a loan (muniḥat) much and has grown accustomed to it, so she is easygoing in walking and does not refuse.
(الزعم) with fatḥa on the zāy and with ḍamma. In al-Miṣbāḥ: زعم زعما, of the pattern of قتل. There are three dialects for al-zaʿm: fatḥa on the zāy for the people of the Hijaz, ḍamma for Banū Asad, and kasra for some of Qays. Al-zaʿm is used in the sense of "saying", and from it: زعمت الحنفية ("the Ḥanafiyya claimed") and زعم سيبويه ("Sībawayh claimed"), i.e. he said; and on this basis is the saying of the Exalted: «أو تسقط السماء كما زعمت» i.e. "as you said". It is used for "supposition", as one says: في زعمي كذا ("in my supposition, such and such"). And for "belief", and from it the saying of the Exalted: «زعم الذين كفروا أن لن يبعثوا». Al-Azharī said: Most often al-zaʿm is used of what is doubted and not verified. Some of them said: it is a euphemism for lying. In Asās al-balāgha he said: "وزعموا مطيّة الكذب (zaʿamū is the mount of lying), and in his speech there are مزاعم, when it is not trustworthy, and I will do that ولا زعماتك". And this saying, ولا زعماتك, means "and I do not imagine your claims". Dhū l-Rumma said:
لقد خطّ رومي ولا زعماته ... لعتبة خطّا لم تطبّق مفاصله
(Rūmī wrote for ʿUtba a document whose joints were not fitted well, and not [as] his claims [would have it].)
Rūmī: a ʿarīf (steward) in the desert, who ruled in favour of ʿUtba ibn Ṭarthūth, a man who was disputing with him about a well, and wrote him a deed.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: يا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ إِنِّي عامِلٌ) A resumptive statement introduced for threat and warning and for exaggeration in restraining them from what they are upon. يا is a particle of vocative, and قَوْمِ is the one addressed, a muḍāf to the omitted first-person yāʾ, whose discussion has already preceded.
اعْمَلُوا is an imperative verb, the intention of which is threat and restraint; عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; إِنِّي is inna and its noun, and عامِلٌ is its khabar, and the clause serves as a justification for the command.
(فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ تَكُونُ لَهُ عاقِبَةُ الدَّارِ إِنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ) The fāʾ is for justification, and the clause is explanatory-justifying and has no position; it came only to confirm the content and import of the preceding clause. مَنْ is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as direct object of تَعْلَمُونَ, which has the sense of "knowing" (ʿirfān), so it takes a single object. The clause تَكُونُ has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative. It is also permissible for «مَنْ» to be interrogative in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar being the clause تَكُونُ, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of تَعْلَمُونَ. لَهُ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar of تَكُونُ, and عاقِبَةُ الدَّارِ is its postponed noun. إِنَّهُ is inna and its noun, and the clause لا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ is its khabar; this clause is also a justification, as if it were an answer to an implied question, as though it were said: "And what is their end?"
(وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ مِمَّا ذَرَأَ مِنَ الْحَرْثِ وَالْأَنْعامِ نَصِيباً) A resumptive statement introduced to set out a kind or pattern of their corrupt rulings. جَعَلَ here has the meaning of "made" (ṣayyara), so it takes two objects. لِلَّهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element that is the second direct object, and the first object is نَصِيباً. مِمَّا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was an adjective of «نَصِيباً» and was put before it. The clause ذَرَأَ has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative. مِنَ الْحَرْثِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, also from «نَصِيباً», and الْأَنْعامِ is conjoined to الْحَرْثِ.
(فَقالُوا: هذا لِلَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وَهذا لِشُرَكائِنا) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and قالُوا is conjoined to جَعَلُوا. The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, and لِلَّهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative as the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). بِزَعْمِهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to what the "being established" of «لله» is attached to. وَهذا لِشُرَكائِنا is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is conjoined to: هذا لله.
(فَما كانَ لِشُرَكائِهِمْ فَلا يَصِلُ إِلَى اللَّهِ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of consequence (tafrīʿiyya), and the clause has no position because it is in the manner of a resumptive one. مَا is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the clause كان is a ṣila with no position; كان is a past defective verb, its noun latent; لِشُرَكائِهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar. The fāʾ is a connective (rābiṭa) because of the scent of conditionality in the relative; لا is negative, and the clause لا يَصِلُ إِلَى اللَّهِ is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of «ما».
(وَما كانَ لِلَّهِ فَهُوَ يَصِلُ إِلى شُرَكائِهِمْ) The wāw is a conjunction. وما كان لله: its i'rab has already preceded. The fāʾ is a connective, هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يَصِلُ إِلى شُرَكائِهِمْ is its khabar.
(ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ) The clause is resumptive. ساءَ is a past, non-conjugating verb, among the verbs of blame; مَا is a relative noun, the agent. It is also said that «ما» is an indefinite complete noun meaning "something", accusative as tamyīz (specification), the estimate being: "evil as a judgement is their judgement". The detail of this will come in the section on Benefits.

* Benefits:
The grammarians disagreed about the word «ما» after the verbs of praise and blame: نعم, بئس and ساء. Ibn Mālik said in al-Khulāṣa:
و «ما» مميّز، وقيل: فاعل ... في نحو: نعم ما يقول الفاضل
(And «ma» is a specification, and it is said: an agent, in the like of "How excellent is what the virtuous man says".)
The detail is that this «ما» is of three kinds:
1- Single: i.e. not followed by anything.
2- Followed by a single word.
3- Followed by a verbal clause.
The first: as in: دققته دقّا نعمّا ("I pounded it a pounding that is excellent"). There are two views on it: (a) definite: it is a relative noun, an agent. (b) an indefinite complete noun: and on this view the specified one (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted, i.e. "how excellent is the pounding".
The second: as in: فنعمّا هي ("how excellent it is") and بئسما تزويج بلا مهر ("how evil is a marriage without a dowry"). There are three views on it: a definite complete noun, an agent; an indefinite complete noun; and compounded with the verb before it in the manner of the compounding of «ذا» with «حبّ», so it has no position, and what follows it is the agent.
The third, followed by a verbal clause, as in: «نعمّا يعظكم به» and «بئسما اشتروا به أنفسهم». There are views on it, the most important four:
(a) that it is indefinite, in the position of an accusative as tamyīz.
(b) that it is in the position of a nominative as agent.
(c) that it is itself the makhṣūṣ.
(d) that it is a restrainer (kāffa).
As for those who say that it is in the position of an accusative as tamyīz, they differed about it in three views:
(a) that it is an indefinite described by the verb after it, and the makhṣūṣ is omitted.
(b) that it is an indefinite described, and the verb after it is an adjective of an omitted makhṣūṣ.
(c) that it is tamyīz, and the makhṣūṣ is another omitted relative «ما», and the verb is the ṣila of the omitted relative «ما»; and this is what we choose for ease of i'rab.
As for those who say that it is in the position of a nominative as agent, they differed about it in five views:
(a) that it is a complete definite noun, i.e. not needing a ṣila, and the verb after it is an adjective of an omitted noun.
(b) that it is a relative, the verb being its ṣila, and the makhṣūṣ is omitted.
(c) that it is a relative, the verb being its ṣila, and it and its ṣila suffice in place of the omitted.
(d) that it is a maṣdar particle which, with its ṣila (because it contains the musnad and the musnad ilayhi), takes the place of both the agent and the makhṣūṣ noun together.
(e) that it is an indefinite described, and the makhṣūṣ is omitted.
As for those who say that it is itself the makhṣūṣ, they said: it is a relative, the agent is latent, and another «ما», omitted, is the tamyīz. As for those who say that it is a restrainer, it restrained «نعم» from working, as قلّ, طال, كثر and شدّ were restrained from it, so that it became able to enter a verbal clause.

Applying the disagreement to the verse:
If we wish to apply what we have summarised to «ساء ما يحكمون»: if we make «ما» a tamyīz, it is an indefinite described, i.e. "evil as a thing they judge"; and if we make it an agent, it is a defective definite, i.e. "evil is that which they judge"; and on both views the makhṣūṣ of blame is always omitted. We have been long in this quotation because the words of the grammarians in it are extremely confused.

dervis-irab:137-137.t:
* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلادِهِمْ شُرَكاؤُهُمْ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to explain the influence of the sayings of the callers of evil who spread falsehoods. وكذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), like its parallels. لِكَثِيرٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «زَيَّنَ»; مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of كَثِيرٍ. قَتْلَ is a fronted direct object, أَوْلادِهِمْ is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement), and شُرَكاؤُهُمْ is the postponed agent of زَيَّنَ.
(لِيُرْدُوهُمْ وَلِيَلْبِسُوا عَلَيْهِمْ دِينَهُمْ) The lām is for justification. يُرْدُوهُمْ is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أَنْ after the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to زَيَّنَ. وَلِيَلْبِسُوا is conjoined to لِيُرْدُوهُمْ. عَلَيْهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to لِيَلْبِسُوا, and دِينَهُمْ is a direct object. So He gave a reason for the adornment in two things: in destroying them, i.e. bringing them to ruin, and in introducing doubt to them in their religion. The clause is resumptive, on the sounder view, i.e. "and thus he adorned".
(وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما فَعَلُوهُ فَذَرْهُمْ وَما يَفْتَرُونَ) The wāw is resumptive, and لَوْ is conditional. شاءَ اللَّهُ is a verb and an agent, and the direct object is omitted, i.e. "their not doing it". مَا is negative; فَعَلُوهُ is a verb, an agent and a direct object. The nominative pronoun refers to «كَثِيرٍ», and the accusative pronoun refers to the killing (al-qatl), because it is what the discourse was conducted about. فَذَرْهُمْ: the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa); ذَرْهُمْ is an imperative verb with a latent agent and a direct object. The wāw is a conjunction or the wāw of accompaniment; مَا is a relative noun or a maṣdar particle, i.e. "leave them and what they fabricate of lies", or "leave them and their fabrication".

* Benefits:
In this verse there are many readings, which the scope of this book does not allow for. We have followed the practice of not pointing to a reading unless it contains an important discussion, so in the section of I'rab we contented ourselves with the reading of the majority. Ibn ʿĀmir, one of the seven, read:
«وكذلك زيّن لكثير من المشركين قتل أولادهم شركائهم» with ḍamma on «قتل» as deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) of the passive زُيِّنَ, accusative on «أولادهم» and genitive on «شركائهم». So «قتل» in the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir is a maṣdar in a construct, and شركائهم is annexed to «قتل», being the annexation of a maṣdar to its agent, and أَوْلادَهُمْ is its object, and it separates the muḍāf from the muḍāf ilayhi. Three things make that good:
