1- That the separator is a complement (faḍla), for that justifies not reckoning with it.
2- That it is not foreign, because it is connected with the muḍāf.
3- That it is estimated as postponed because the muḍāf ilayhi is estimated as fronted by virtue of its being the agent in meaning.
By that the extent of al-Zamakhsharī's incoherence in his statement becomes clear:

What al-Zamakhsharī said:
"As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, «قتل أولادهم شركائهم», with ḍamma on al-qatl, accusative on al-awlād and genitive on al-shurakāʾ, on the annexation of al-qatl to al-shurakāʾ and the separation between them by other than the adverb, it is a thing which, were it in the place of necessities, namely poetry, would be ugly and rejected, so how is it in prose speech? And how is it in the Qurʾān, which is inimitable by reason of its wording and its robustness?"

Separation between the two parts of a genitive construct:
Many of the grammarians claimed that one does not separate between the two parts of a genitive construct except in poetry specifically, because the muḍāf is placed in relation to the muḍāf ilayhi in the position of a part of it, since it occupies the place of its tanwīn; so just as one does not separate between the parts of a noun, one does not separate between it and what is placed in the position of a part of it. This is the view of the Basrans. According to the Kufans, the cases of separation are seven, three of which are permissible in free usage (al-saʿa), i.e. prose, and they are:
1- That the muḍāf is a maṣdar and the muḍāf ilayhi is its agent, and the separator is either its object, as in the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir mentioned above, and the words of the poet:
عتوا إذ أجبناهم إلى السلم رأفة ... فسقناهم سوق البغاث الأجادل
(They were insolent when out of compassion we answered them to peace, so we drove them as hawks drive the small birds.)
Here سوق is a maṣdar in construct, الأجادل is the muḍāf ilayhi, being the annexation of a maṣdar to its agent, and البغاث is its object, and it separated between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi; the original is: سوق الأجادل البغاث. Or its adverbial, as in the saying of one of them:
«ترك يوما نفسك وهواها موبق لها» ("Abandoning, for a day, yourself and its desire is ruinous for it"). Here ترك is a maṣdar in construct, نفسك is the muḍāf ilayhi, being the annexation of a maṣdar to its agent, its object is omitted, and يوما is an adverb of the maṣdar, meaning that it is attached to it, and it separated between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi.
2- That the muḍāf is a participle and the muḍāf ilayhi is its first object, and the separator is its second object, as in the reading of some of them: «فلا تحسبنّ الله مخلف وعده رسله» with accusative on وعده and genitive on رسله. So مخلف is an active participle that takes two objects, and it is a muḍāf, رسله is the muḍāf ilayhi, being the annexation of the participle to its first object, and وعده is its second object, and it separated between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi.
3- That the separator is an oath, as in their saying: «هذا غلام والله زيد» ("This is, by Allah, Zayd's boy"), where زيد is made genitive by the annexation of غلام to it, and the oath separates between them.
The remaining four of the seven are specific to poetry, and they are:
1- Separation by a foreign element, as in the words of Jarīr:
تسقي امتياحا ندى المسواك ريقتها ... كما تضمّن ماء المزنة الرّصف
(She gives to drink, in eagerness, the dew of her saliva to the toothstick, as the pebbles hold the water of the rain cloud.)
Here تسقي is the imperfect of سقى, which takes two objects, and its agent is a pronoun that refers to the beloved in the verse before it; ندى is its first object and is a muḍāf, ريقتها is the muḍāf ilayhi, and المسواك is its second object, and it separated between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. "she gives to drink the dew of her saliva to the toothstick". المسواك is foreign to «ندى» because it is not governed by it, although the governing element of the two is one.
2- Separation by the agent of the muḍāf, as in his words:
ما إن وجدنا للهوى من طبّ ... ولا عدمنا قهر وجد صبّ
(We have not found any remedy for passion, nor have we lacked the overpowering of a lover's longing.)
He annexed «قهر» to its object, which is «صب», and separated between them by the agent of the maṣdar, which is «وجد».
3- Separation by the naʿt of the muḍāf, as in the words of Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān, when three of the Khawārij agreed that each of them would kill one of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān, so ʿAlī was killed, and ʿAmr and Muʿāwiya were spared:
نجوت وقد بل المرادي سيفه ... من ابن أبي شيخ الأباطح طالب
(You escaped, when al-Murādī had wetted his sword, from the son of the father of the chief of the Abāṭiḥ, Ṭālib.)
So he separated between the two parts of the construct, which are أبي and طالب, by the naʿt of the muḍāf, which is: شيخ الأباطح, i.e. "from the son of Abū Ṭālib, the chief of the Abāṭiḥ". Al-Murādī, with fatḥa on the mīm, is a relative adjective to Murād, a clan of Madhḥij, and he is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muljam, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the jīm, in the form of a passive participle.
4- Separation by the vocative, as in his words:
كأن برذون أبا عصام ... زيد حمار دقّ باللجام
(As though the pony of Zayd, O Abū ʿIṣām, were an ass struck with the bridle.)
So he annexed برذون to زيد, and separated between them by the one addressed whose particle was dropped, and حمار is the khabar of كأن; the original is: كأن برذون زيد حمار يا أبا عصام. To all of this Ibn Mālik pointed in al-Khulāṣa with his words:
فصل مضاف شبه فعل ما نصب ... مفعولا أو ظرفا أجز ولم يعب
فصل يمين واضطرارا وجدا ... بأجنبي أو بنعت أو ندا
(Separating a muḍāf that resembles a verb by what it makes accusative, an object or an adverb, permit it, and it is not faulted; and separation by an oath; and by necessity it has been found with a foreign element, or an adjective, or a vocative.)

Between Abū Ḥayyān and al-Zamakhsharī:
Abū Ḥayyān rebutted al-Zamakhsharī and was harsh in his rebuttal. After quoting the words of al-Zamakhsharī which we quoted at the beginning of this discussion, he said:
"And marvel at a weak non-Arab in grammar who rejects from a pure, genuine Arab a mutawātir reading, and marvel at this man's ill opinion of the leading reciters whom this community chose to transmit the Book of Allah, east and west."

Between Abū Ḥayyān and al-Fārisī:
Abū Ḥayyān went on to rebut Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī. He said: "Nor should attention be paid to the saying of Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī: This is ugly, rare in usage, and had he (meaning Ibn ʿĀmir) turned away from it, it would have been better, because they did not permit separation between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi by the adverb in speech, despite their latitude regarding the adverb, and they permitted it only in poetry."

A glimpse of ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir:
As for ʿUqba, he is the great Companion and the commander-prince who took part in the conquest of Egypt, then ruled it as deputy and in his own right. He was an enlightened, intelligent man who enjoyed clear intellectual qualities, and the Prophet ﷺ charged him to judge between two disputants who brought their dispute to him, and he was a poet, a reciter and a scribe. «[Translator's note: the source passes here from the reciter Ibn ʿĀmir to ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir the Companion without explanation; the reciter of the seven is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir al-Yaḥṣubī. The text is translated as written.]»

Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī separated between the two parts of a genitive construct:
Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī used separation between the two parts of a construct, and separated between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi by the object, saying, in a poem in which he praises Abū l-Qāsim Ṭāhir ibn al-Ḥusayn:
حملت إليه من لساني حديقة ... سقاها الحجا سقي الرياض السحائب
(I carried to him from my tongue a garden that reason watered as the clouds water meadows.)
Here he separated by the object. The meaning of the verse is that he made the poem a garden because of the meanings in it, as in a meadow there are flowers and plants, and he made the intellect its waterer, because the meanings in it are made beautiful only by the intellect, so he made the intellect its waterer, as the clouds water the meadows, سحاب being the plural of سحابة.

The word of Ibn Jinnī:
Abū l-Fatḥ Ibn Jinnī said: "When something of that happens, one looks at the condition of the Arab and what he brought; if he is eloquent and what he cited is accepted by analogy, the better course is to think well of him, because it is possible that this reached him from an ancient dialect whose time has grown long and whose traces have faded."

The word of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ:
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "Of what the Arabs said, only the least of it has reached you; had it come to you in full, much knowledge and poetry would have come to you."

A report from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb:
Ibn Sīrīn reported from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he preserved the least of that and most of it was lost to them, meaning poetry, in a story of some length.

dervis-irab:138-139.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حِجْرٌ): The pattern is فِعْل (with kasra on the first letter) in the sense of مفعول, like الذبح and الطحن; the masculine and feminine, the singular and plural are alike in describing with it, because its ruling is that of nouns that are not adjectives, and for that reason it occurred as an adjective of أنعام and حرث. Its meaning is al-ḥajr, i.e. prevention. When they designated things from their crops and their cattle for their gods, they said: only those whom we wish may eat them. So they made the share of the gods three kinds: the first is what He mentioned in His words: حِجْرٌ, i.e. prohibited, forbidden; the second is what He mentioned in His words: «وأنعام حرمت ظهورها»; and the third is His words: «لا يذكرون اسم الله عليها». So they made them categories by their own whim and ascribed that categorisation to Allah.
(خالِصَةٌ): The tāʾ in خالصة is for intensification, like that in راوية, علامة, نسّابة, الخاصة and العامة; or it is a maṣdar on the pattern fāʿila, like العافية and العاقبة.

* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا: هذِهِ أَنْعامٌ وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ لا يَطْعَمُها إِلَّا مَنْ نَشاءُ بِزَعْمِهِمْ) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to relate another kind of their kinds of disbelief. هذِهِ is a demonstrative in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), أَنْعامٌ is a khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the content of the saying. حَرْثٌ is conjoined to أَنْعامٌ, and حِجْرٌ is a description of both, i.e. forbidden, prevented, prohibited. The clause لا يَطْعَمُها is a second adjective of أَنْعامٌ; يَطْعَمُها is an imperfect verb and a direct object, إِلَّا is a particle of restriction, and مَنْ is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as agent of يَطْعَمُها; the clause نَشاءُ has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative. بِزَعْمِهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of قالُوا, i.e. they said that, coupled with their false claim.
(وَأَنْعامٌ حُرِّمَتْ ظُهُورُها) The wāw is a conjunction; أَنْعامٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "these", and the clause is conjoined to His words «هذه أنعام», i.e. they said, pointing to another group of their cattle, and by them they mean the baḥāʾir, the sawāʾib and the ḥawāmī, which have preceded in al-Māʾida. The clause حُرِّمَتْ ظُهُورُها is an adjective, i.e. they are not ridden, and ظُهُورُها is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) of حُرِّمَتْ.
(وَأَنْعامٌ لا يَذْكُرُونَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا افْتِراءً عَلَيْهِ) The wāw is a conjunction, and أَنْعامٌ is also the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause is conjoined to what preceded, so the sayings are three. The clause لا يَذْكُرُونَ is an adjective of أَنْعامٌ, اسْمَ اللَّهِ is a direct object, and عَلَيْهَا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يَذْكُرُونَ. In افْتِراءً it is permissible that it be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. they did all that for the sake of fabrication; it is permissible that it be a ḥāl, i.e. fabricating; and it is permissible that it be an emphatic maṣdar, because their saying that is in the sense of fabrication, so it is parallel to your saying: رجع القهقرى ("he went back backwards") and قعد القرفصاء ("he sat squatting"). عَلَيْهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to افْتِراءً, or to an omitted adjective of it.
(سَيَجْزِيهِمْ بِما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to affirm their recompense. بِما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يَجْزِيهِمْ; in «ما» it is permissible that it be a maṣdar particle or a relative, and the bāʾ is of causation, i.e. because of their fabrication or because of what they used to fabricate against Allah.
(وَقالُوا: ما فِي بُطُونِ هذِهِ الْأَنْعامِ خالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا وَمُحَرَّمٌ عَلى أَزْواجِنا) A resumptive statement introduced to begin another saying among their fabrications and falsehoods; for they used to say about the foetuses of the baḥāʾir and the sawāʾib: whatever is born of them alive is exclusively for the males and the females do not eat of it, and whatever is born of them dead, the males and females share in it. مَا is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; فِي بُطُونِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative; هذِهِ is a demonstrative in the position of a genitive by annexation; الْأَنْعامِ is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; خالِصَةٌ is a khabar of «ما»; لِذُكُورِنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالِصَةٌ; مُحَرَّمٌ is conjoined to خالِصَةٌ; and عَلى أَزْواجِنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مُحَرَّمٌ.
(وَإِنْ يَكُنْ مَيْتَةً فَهُمْ فِيهِ شُرَكاءُ) The wāw is a conjunction, and إِنْ is conditional. يَكُنْ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its noun latent, its implied form being: "and if what is in their bellies is", and مَيْتَةً is a khabar. The fāʾ is a connective for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). هُمْ is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ and شُرَكاءُ a khabar. فِيهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because in origin it was an adjective of شُرَكاءُ; and you may attach it to شُرَكاءُ.
(سَيَجْزِيهِمْ وَصْفَهُمْ إِنَّهُ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ) A resumptive statement in the manner of a justification, introduced to explain their playing with the rulings of prohibition and permission, in a way that His wisdom requires and His knowledge demands. The sīn is a particle of futurity; يَجْزِيهِمْ is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent and referring to Allah the Exalted; the hāʾ is a first direct object, and وَصْفَهُمْ is a second direct object of يَجْزِيهِمْ. The clause إِنَّهُ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ is a justification and has no position. A muḍāf must be supposed, the estimate being: "He will recompense them with the recompense of their describing falsehood against Allah in permitting and prohibiting".

dervis-irab:116-117.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَخْرُصُونَ): they lie, from al-kharṣ, which is estimating and guessing. Lying was called kharṣ because of the false conjectures that enter into it. One says kharaṣa yakhruṣu (its pattern being naṣara), and ikhtaraṣa the saying and takharraṣahu: he fabricated it.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يُضِلُّوكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction. إن is conditional, and تطع is the protasis; أكثر is the mafʿūl bihi; من is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi; and في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative. ويضلوك is the apodosis, jussive; the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; and عن سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يضلوك.
(إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ) The sentence is resumptive, with no grammatical position. إن is negative; ويتّبعون is an imperfect verb, nominative, the wāw being its fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction; and الظن is the mafʿūl bihi. The wāw is a conjunction; إن is negative; هم is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; and the sentence يخرصون is their khabar.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مَنْ يَضِلُّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ) The sentence is resumptive, to confirm the content of the conditional sentence. إن and its ism; هو is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم a khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of «إن»; or «هو» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and أعلم is the khabar of «إن». من is a relative noun accusative through an implied verb and not through أعلم itself, because the elative does not govern an overt object in such a case; more of this i'rab will come in the section on Benefits. The implied form is: "He knows who goes astray" (يعلم من يضل). The sentence يضل is the ṣila of the relative; وعن سبيله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يضل; وهو is a mubtadaʾ; أعلم is a khabar; and بالمهتدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعلم.

* Benefits:
This verse has occupied the grammarians and the exegetes, and we shall summarise for you what has been said on the matter. Some said: «أعلم» in both places has the sense of "knows" (يعلم). Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī said:
فحالفت طيء من دوننا حلفا ... والله أعلم ما كنا لهم خولا
(So Ṭayyiʾ made an alliance apart from us, and Allah knows that we were never servants to them.)
It was said: the elative is in its proper sense, and the accusative is through an implied verb, as we chose in the section on i'rab. It was said: it is accusative through the elative, according to the school of the Kufans. This is problematic, because the annexation would imply that Allah is one of the misguided, exalted is He above that. It was said: it is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "of the one who goes astray" (بمن يضل). It was said: in the position of the genitive by annexation of the elative to it. It was said: «من» is in the position of the nominative, and it is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being the sentence يضل, and the sentence is in the position of the accusative or is suspended from governing by «أعلم» (muʿallaqa), that is: "He knows best which of the people goes astray" (أعلم أي الناس يضل), as in His saying the Exalted: «لنعلم أي الحزبين»? So reflect, and Allah protect you.

dervis-irab:118-119.t:
* I'rab:
(فَكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ بِآياتِهِ مُؤْمِنِينَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent one (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), because it discloses an implied condition, the implied form being: "if you are firm in faith, then eat" (إذا كنتم متحقفين بالإيمان فكلوا) [Translator's note: the source reads «متحقفين», apparently a misprint for «متحققين» ("firmly established"); translated accordingly]. This command is built upon the prohibition of following the misleaders who forbid the lawful and make lawful the forbidden. ومما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كلوا; the sentence ذكر اسم الله عليه is the ṣila of the relative; اسم الله is the nāʾib fāʿil of ذكر; and عليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ذكر. إن is conditional; وكنتم is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, the tāʾ being its ism and مؤمنين its khabar; وبآياته is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مؤمنين; and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, that is: "then eat" (فكلوا).
(وَما لَكُمْ أَلَّا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to stress the permissibility of what is slaughtered in the name of Allah. ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; ولكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of «ما»; and أن لا تأكلوا is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, that is: في أن لا تأكلوا; and since the preposition was omitted it is in the position of the accusative; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to whatever «لكم», which occurs as the khabar of the interrogative «ما», is attached to. ومما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تأكلوا; and the sentence ذكر اسم الله عليه is the ṣila of the relative.
(وَقَدْ فَصَّلَ لَكُمْ ما حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِلَّا مَا اضْطُرِرْتُمْ إِلَيْهِ) The wāw is a ḥāl wāw; قد is a particle of confirmation; فصل is a past verb with a latent fāʿil; ولكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فصّل; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the sentence حرم عليكم has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative; إلا is a particle of exception; and ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception; the sentence اضطررتم إليه is the ṣila of the relative. You may also take it as an exception from the pronoun in «حرّم», with ما as a maṣdar particle in the sense of duration, that is: "the things that were forbidden to you, except when compelled to them", as He detailed in the verse «حرمت عليكم الميتة»; then the exception is connected (muttaṣil), and this is perhaps preferable, because the exception is from the same genus. The sentence اضطررتم has no grammatical position in either case; وإليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the passive اضطررتم; the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil; and the whole sentence is accusative as a ḥāl.
(وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً لَيُضِلُّونَ بِأَهْوائِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction or a ḥāl wāw; إن and its ism; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the sentence يضلون is the khabar of إن; وبأهوائهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يضلون; and بغير علم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is: "clad in ignorance" (متلبسين بالجهل).
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُعْتَدِينَ) The sentence gives a reason, with no grammatical position. إن and its ism; هو is a mubtadaʾ, or a separating pronoun, and أعلم is the khabar of هو or the khabar of إن; and بالمعتدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعلم.

dervis-irab:140-140.t:
* I'rab:
(قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ قَتَلُوا أَوْلادَهُمْ سَفَهاً بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) A resumptive statement introduced to explain another pattern of their ignorance, for some of the Arabs of Rabīʿa and Muḍar used to bury their daughters alive for fear of captivity and poverty. قَدْ is a particle of affirmation; خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ is a verb and an agent; the clause قَتَلُوا أَوْلادَهُمْ has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative. سَفَهاً is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. because of the lightness of their minds and their ignorance. بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of قَتَلُوا, i.e. ignorant that Allah is the Provider for them and for their children.
(وَحَرَّمُوا ما رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ افْتِراءً عَلَى اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; حَرَّمُوا is a verb and an agent; مَا is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ is the ṣila; افْتِراءً is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi or a ḥāl; عَلَى اللَّهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to افْتِراءً.
(قَدْ ضَلُّوا وَما كانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ) The clause is an emphasis (tawkīd) of His words: «قد خسر الذين». The wāw is a conjunction, مَا is negative, and كانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ is kāna with its noun and khabar (predicate).

dervis-irab:141-141.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَعْرُوشاتٍ): عرش يعرش and يعرش (of the two patterns taʿiba and naṣara): he built a structure of wood. عرش البيت: he built it. عرش العرش: he made it. Al-ʿarsh is the king's throne and the corner (support) of a thing. The original of al-ʿarsh in the language is a roofed thing on which the vine is placed, its plural being عروش. استوى على عرشه when he became king. وثلّ عرشه: when he perished. Zuhayr said:
تداركتما عبسا وقد ثلّ عرشها ... وذبيان إذ زلّت بأقدامها النّعل
(You two rescued ʿAbs when its throne had been toppled, and Dhubyān when the sandal slipped from their feet.)
And al-ʿurūsh: houses. Al-Quṭāmī said:
وما لمثابات العروش بقيّة ... إذا استلّ من تحت العروش الدّعائم
(There is nothing left of the gathering places of the houses once the supports are pulled from beneath the roofs.)
And «ومكتنسات في العرائش» i.e. the howdahs. They disagreed about its meaning. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Al-maʿrūshāt is what spreads out and extends over the ground, like the vine, the gourd, the melon and the like; and ghayr maʿrūshāt is what stands on a stalk, like the palm, the crops and the rest of the trees." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "Both apply to the vine specifically, because of it there is that which is trellised and that which is not trellised but remains on the surface of the ground, spread out." And he said in al-Kashshāf: "Maʿrūshāt: raised up. Ghayr maʿrūshāt: left on the surface of the ground, not trellised. It is also said: al-maʿrūshāt is what is in the countryside and the inhabited places, of what people planted and cared for, so they trellised it; and ghayr maʿrūshāt is what Allah caused to grow wild in the wilderness and the mountains, so it is not trellised."

* I'rab:
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَ جَنَّاتٍ مَعْرُوشاتٍ وَغَيْرَ مَعْرُوشاتٍ) The wāw is resumptive; هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ and الَّذِي its khabar; the clause أَنْشَأَ has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; جَنَّاتٍ is a direct object; مَعْرُوشاتٍ is an adjective; and غَيْرَ مَعْرُوشاتٍ is conjoined to مَعْرُوشاتٍ.
(وَالنَّخْلَ وَالزَّرْعَ مُخْتَلِفاً أُكُلُهُ) وَالنَّخْلَ وَالزَّرْعَ are conjoined to جَنَّاتٍ. مُخْتَلِفاً is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because the palm and the crops, at the time of their coming forth, have no fruit that could be varied or uniform; and أُكُلُهُ is the agent of «مُخْتَلِفاً», because it is an active participle.
(وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ مُتَشابِهاً وَغَيْرَ مُتَشابِهٍ) It is also conjoined to what preceded. He singled out these kinds because of the excellence in them over the rest of what grows in the gardens. مُتَشابِهاً is a ḥāl and غَيْرَ مُتَشابِهٍ is conjoined to it.
(كُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ إِذا أَثْمَرَ وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصادِهِ) A resumptive statement introduced to explain that it is permitted. كُلُوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the agent; مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كُلُوا; إِذا is a future adverb containing the sense of a condition; آتُوا is an imperative verb conjoined to كُلُوا; حَقَّهُ is a direct object; يَوْمَ is an adverb of time attached to آتُوا; and حَصادِهِ is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement). By "the due" here is meant the zakāt, and it is not problematic that the sūra is Makkan while the zakāt was made obligatory in Madīna, because this verse is Madīnan; it is also meant what was given in charity to the poor at the time of harvest, and that was well known.
(وَلا تُسْرِفُوا إِنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تُسْرِفُوا is an imperfect verb made jussive by لا, i.e. do not exceed the limit. Al-Zajjāj said: on this basis, if a person gave all his property and delivered nothing to his dependants, he has been extravagant. إِنَّ and its noun, and the clause لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ is its khabar, and the clause of إِنَّ and what is in its scope is a justification for what preceded.

dervis-irab:120-121.t:
* I'rab:
(وَذَرُوا ظاهِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَباطِنَهُ) The wāw is a conjunction on what has preceded; وذروا is an imperative verb, the wāw being the fāʿil; ظاهر الإثم is the mafʿūl bihi; and باطنه is conjoined to ظاهر.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْسِبُونَ الْإِثْمَ سَيُجْزَوْنَ بِما كانُوا يَقْتَرِفُونَ) The sentence gives a reason, with no grammatical position. إن and its ism; the sentence يكسبون is the ṣila of the relative; الإثم is the mafʿūl bihi; the sentence سيجزون is the khabar of إن; وبما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يجزون; the sentence كانوا is the ṣila of the relative; the wāw is the ism of كان; and the sentence يقترفون is its khabar. The returning pronoun is omitted, that is: يقترفونه ("they commit it").
(وَلا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; وتأكلوا is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لا, the wāw being the fāʿil; ومما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تأكلوا; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion; ويذكر is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لم; اسم الله is the nāʾib fāʿil of يذكر; and عليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يذكر. وإنه: the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; إن and its ism; the shifted lām; and فسق is the khabar of إن. The pronoun in «إنه» refers to the maṣdar of the verb that the particle of prohibition entered, that is, "the eating"; or to «ما», that is, to what is left without the naming. More will be said on this question.
(وَإِنَّ الشَّياطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلى أَوْلِيائِهِمْ لِيُجادِلُوكُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction on «وإنه لفسق», or resumptive; إن and its ism; the shifted lām; the sentence يوحون is the khabar of «إن»; وإلى أوليائهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يوحون; the lām is for giving a reason; and ويجادلوكم is an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied أن after the lām; and the preposition and its genitive noun are likewise attached to «يوحون».
(وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; وأطعتموهم is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi, in the position of the jussive as the protasis, the tāʾ being the fāʿil and the wāw being for the fullness of the ḍamma (ishbāʿ); إن and its ism; the shifted lām; and مشركون is its khabar. The apodosis is not joined to the fāʾ for two reasons:
The first is that the lām that prepares for an oath (lām al-tawṭiʾa li-l-qasam) is implied before the conditional إن; for this reason the implied oath is answered by His saying «إنكم لمشركون», and the apodosis is omitted because the answer to the oath fills its place. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: the omission of the fāʾ from the apodosis is good when the condition is in the form of a past verb. More discussion on this will come in the section on Benefits. [Translator's note: the source announces two reasons but states only the first.]

* Benefits:
1- The wāw in His saying the Exalted «وانه لفسق» has occupied the exegetes, the grammarians and the jurists to a degree for which the breadth of this book has no room. We chose what we saw as nearest to understanding, and we think it useful to allude to their disagreement briefly; whoever wants full coverage should consult the large works.
The wording of al-Samīn:
Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī, known as al-Samīn, said: "His saying: «وإنه لفسق». This sentence has several aspects:
1- That it is resumptive. They said it cannot be a coordinate (nasaq) on what precedes it, because the first is a request (ṭalabiyya) and this is declarative (khabariyya); and this wāw is called the wāw of resumption.
2- That it is coordinated to what precedes, with no concern for [Translator's note: the source reads «ولا يبالي نتجا لفهمها», which is garbled and cannot be construed with certainty; rendered as closely as possible], and this is the view of Sībawayh.
3- That it is a ḥāl: "Do not eat it, the circumstance being that it is an act of disobedience (fisq)."
On the basis of these aspects the jurists disagreed on the permissibility of eating what Allah's name was not mentioned over:
1- A group held it forbidden whether he left it deliberately or by forgetfulness. This is the view of Ibn Sīrīn, al-Shaʿbī and Mālik ibn Anas, and it is reported from ʿAṭāʾ that he said: Everything over which Allah's name was not mentioned, of food or drink, is forbidden. They argued for this from the apparent sense of this verse.
2- Al-Thawrī and Abū Ḥanīfa said: if he leaves the naming deliberately it is not lawful, and if he leaves it forgetfully it is lawful.
3- Al-Shāfiʿī said: the slaughtered animal is lawful whether he left the naming deliberately or forgetfully. Ibn al-Jawzī reported it from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal.
What al-Rāzī reported from al-Shāfiʿī:
Al-Rāzī mentioned in his book Manāqib al-Shāfiʿī that a gathering brought him together with a group of Hanafis, and that they claimed al-Shāfiʿī's opinion that eating what was left without the naming is lawful is refuted by His saying the Exalted: «ولا تأكلوا مما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه وإنه لفسق». He said: "I said to them: There is no proof in it; rather it is an argument for al-Shāfiʿī. That is because the wāw is not for coordination, owing to the difference between the nominal and the verbal sentence, nor for resumption, because the basis of the wāw is to link what follows it to what precedes it. It remains, then, that it is for ḥāl, so the ḥāl sentence restricts the prohibition, and the meaning is: Do not eat of it in the state of its being fisq, and its implication is that eating is permitted when it is not fisq."

What al-Zamakhsharī says:
Al-Zamakhsharī said in his Kashshāf: "If you say: A group of the mujtahids held that eating what Allah's name was not mentioned over, by forgetfulness or deliberately, is permitted, I say: These interpreted it as carrion and what had a name other than Allah's mentioned over it, as in His saying: «أو فسقا أهل لغير الله به»." It is clear that al-Zamakhsharī is a Hanafi, so he is championing his school. It would take us long to cite the arguments of both parties, which does not fall within the scope of our book, and what has preceded suffices us.
2- Every answer that cannot be made a condition requires the fāʾ, because its meaning is immediate succession without separation, just as the consequence follows the protasis. This is in the following places:
1- The nominal sentence, like His saying the Exalted: «وإن يمسسك بخير فهو على كل شيء قدير».
2- The request sentence, like His saying the Exalted: «إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني».
3- The sentence whose verb is past in form and meaning; then it must be joined with an overt «قد», like His saying the Exalted: «إن يسرق فقد سرق», or an implied one, like His saying the Exalted: «إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت», that is: فقد صدقت.
4- The sentence whose verb is a non-conjugating (jāmid) verb, like His saying the Exalted: «إن ترني أنا أقلّ منك مالا وولدا فعسى ربي أن يؤتين خيرا من جنّتك».
5- The sentence whose verb is joined to «قد», like His saying the Exalted: «إن يسرق فقد سرق».
6- The sentence whose verb is joined to the negative «ما», like His saying the Exalted: «فإن توليتم فما سألتكم من أجر».
7- The sentence whose verb is joined to «لن», like His saying the Exalted: «وما يفعلوا من خير فلن يكفروه».
8- The sentence whose verb is joined to the sīn, like His saying the Exalted: «ومن يستنكف عن عبادته ويستكبر فسيحشرهم إليه جميعا».
9- The sentence whose verb is joined to sawfa, like His saying the Exalted: «وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله».
10- The sentence whose verb is headed by «ربّ», like: «إن تجيء فربما أجيء» ("If you come, then perhaps I will come").
11- The sentence whose verb is headed by kaannamā, like His saying the Exalted: «أنه من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا».
12- The sentence whose verb is headed by a conditional particle, like His saying the Exalted: «وإن كان كبر عليك إعراضهم فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقا في الأرض أو سلما في السماء فتأتيهم بآية».
The fāʾ is occasionally omitted, rarely, as in the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb when he asked him about the lost property (luqaṭa): «فإن جاء بها صاحبها وإلا استمتع بها» ("If its owner comes for it, well; otherwise, make use of it"); or out of poetic necessity, as in the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها ... والشرّ بالشرّ عند الله مثلان
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah thanks him for them; and evil for evil, in Allah's sight, are two equals.)
He meant: فالله يشكرها.
The fāʾ of the consequence may also be replaced by the iḏā of surprise (idhā al-fujāʾiyya) if the particle is «إن», as in His saying the Exalted: «وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم إذا هم يقنطون».

dervis-irab:122-122.t:
* I'rab:
(أَوَمَنْ كانَ مَيْتاً فَأَحْيَيْناهُ وَجَعَلْنا لَهُ نُوراً يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي النَّاسِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to draw a parallel for the state of the disbeliever and the believer. The hamza is for rhetorical (inkārī) questioning, and the wāw is a conjunction on a sentence extracted from His saying «وإن أطعتموهم», the implied form being: "Are you like them?" (أأنتم مثلهم), so that the two sentences are alike in being nominal.
من is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the sentence كان is the ṣila of the relative; and ميتا is the khabar of كان. فأحييناه: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أحييناه is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi. وجعلنا is conjoined to His saying فأحييناه; وله is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as the first object of جعلنا; and نورا is the second mafʿūl bihi; or جعلنا is in the sense of "We created" (خلقنا), in which case the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, because they were originally a naʿt of it, and نورا is a mafʿūl bihi if جعلنا means خلقنا, and a second object if it stays as it is. The sentence يمشي is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of «نورا»; وبه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يمشي; and في الناس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is: "being among them" (كائنا بينهم).
(كَمَنْ مَثَلُهُ فِي الظُّلُماتِ لَيْسَ بِخارِجٍ مِنْها) كمن: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of «من»; ومثله is a mubtadaʾ; وفي الظلمات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; and the nominal sentence is the ṣila of the relative. The sentence ليس بخارج منها is accusative as a ḥāl: ليس is a defective past verb with a latent ism; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and خارج is genitive in form by the bāʾ but accusative in position as the khabar of ليس; and منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خارج.
(كَذلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْكافِرِينَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) كذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar; its like has often been given. وزين is in the passive; وللكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to زين; ما is a relative noun, the nāʾib fāʿil; the sentence كانوا is the ṣila of the relative; and the sentence يعملون is the khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is the representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī), which has often been pointed out. The point of resemblance in it is an image abstracted from several things. This is a parable that Allah the Exalted struck for the state of the believer and the disbeliever. He made clear that the guided believer is in the position of one who was dead, whom He gave life and gave a light by which he is guided in his affairs, and that the disbeliever is in the position of one who is in the darkness, plunged into it. These different kinds were not brought together for the parable, and these disparate things did not meet in the ruling of the thing likened, except because He did not regard what presents itself to the eye, but what presents itself to the intellect, and was not concerned with what sight attains but with what reflection holds to. We believe that the parables that occur in the Qur'an are general, applying to every human being in his various circumstances and states, and this is the correct view, which suits the meaning of the guidance that the Qur'an brought. But the exegetes, may Allah have mercy on them, expand on this, assigning to every verse an occasion connected with it, and there is nothing to prevent that as long as people's states are alike and similar across the different circumstances of time and place. More than one of them mentioned that two men are meant in the verse: the first is Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, and the second is Abū Jahl ibn Hishām. They cite a curious story that it is no harm to cite; its gist is that Abū Jahl threw dung at the Prophet ﷺ, and Ḥamza was told what Abū Jahl had done (Ḥamza had returned from hunting with a bow in his hand, and had not yet believed). Ḥamza came in anger until he stood over Abū Jahl and began to strike him with the bow, while Abū Jahl began to plead with Ḥamza and say: "O Abū Yaʿlā! Do you not see what he has brought? He has called our minds foolish, reviled our gods and opposed our forefathers!" Ḥamza said: "And who is more foolish in mind than you? You worship stones instead of Allah! I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." So Ḥamza accepted Islam that day.

dervis-irab:142-144.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَمُولَةً): Al-ḥamūla, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ: those of the camels that are able to bear a load.
(فَرْشاً): And al-farsh: their young ones. This is the well-known sense in the language. He said in al-Asās: "And the ḥamūla passed by: they are the camels that are loaded, «ومن الأنعام حمولة وفرشا»". ʿAntara said:
ما راعني إلّا حمولة أهلها ... وسط الديار تسفّ حبّ الخمخم
(Nothing startled me but the pack-camels of her people in the midst of the dwellings, gobbling the seeds of the khamkham.)
Its commentator al-Zawzanī said: "Al-ḥamūla: the camels that are able to be loaded." It is also said: "Al-ḥamūla: the large livestock, I mean camels, cattle and sheep/goats, and al-farsh their young." Al-Zajjāj said: "The people of the language are unanimous that al-farsh is the young camels." Abū Zayd said: "It is possible that it was named with the maṣdar, because al-farsh in origin is a maṣdar; and al-farsh is a word shared among many meanings, among them: household goods, the wide open space, the slight broadening of the camel's foot, smooth ground, and a plant that clings to the ground." It is also said: al-ḥamūla is everything that is loaded among camels, cattle, mules and donkeys; and al-farsh is what is taken from their wool, fur and hair to be spread out." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. He brought into being of the livestock those that carry heavy loads, and those that are spread out for slaughter, or whose fur, wool and hair is woven into spreads. It is also said: al-ḥamūla are those fit for carrying, and al-farsh the young, like weaned camels, calves and lambs, because they are close to the ground by the smallness of their bodies, like the spread that is laid on it."
(الضَّأْنِ): It is said: it is the plural of ḍāʾin for the male and ḍāʾina for the female; and it is said: a collective noun (ism jamʿ); and the same is said of al-maʿz, whether its ʿayn has sukūn or fatḥa. In al-Qāmūs: أضئن ضأنك: separate them from the goats. Al-ḍaʾn is a generic noun, as opposed to the māʿiz of the flock; and al-ḍāʾin: the woolly one, as opposed to the māʿiz of the flock, and its plural is ضأن, ضأن, ضئين and ضئين. In al-Asās: ماله الضّأن والمعز والضّئين والمعز, and he has a flock of ḍaʾina of sheep, and the meat and hide of ḍāʾin and māʿiz; and أضأن فلان وأمعز means that his sheep and goats became many; and the Arabs say: اضأن ضأنك وامعز معزك, i.e. separate them. «[Translator's note: the source has "جعمه" in "وجعمه ضأن …", evidently for "وجمعه"; translated accordingly.]»
(الْمَعْزِ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: al-maʿz is a generic noun with no singular from its own wording; they are the hairy ones of the flock, the singular being shāh, which is feminine; the ʿayn takes fatḥa or sukūn, and the plural of the one with sukūn is amʿuz and maʿīz, like ʿabd: aʿbud and ʿabīd. The alif of al-maʿzā is for linking (ilḥāq) and not for the feminine, and for this it takes tanwīn when indefinite and its diminutive is maʿīz; and if the alif were for the feminine it would not be dropped. The male is māʿiz and the female māʿiza.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنَ الْأَنْعامِ حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً) The wāw is a conjunction; مِنَ الْأَنْعامِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because in origin it was an adjective of «حمولة وفرشا» and was put before them; حَمُولَةً is conjoined to جَنَّاتٍ, i.e. "and He brought into being of the livestock beasts of burden and small ones to be spread".
(كُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ) A resumptive statement introduced to explain what they confused and in which their sayings were disordered, namely that they forbade the males of the livestock at one time and the females at another, so He denounced that to them. كُلُوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; مِمَّا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كُلُوا; the clause رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; لا is prohibitive; تَتَّبِعُوا is an imperfect verb made jussive by لا, and the wāw is the agent; خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ is a direct object; and the clause is conjoined to the clause كُلُوا. إِنَّ and its noun; لَكُمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; عَدُوٌّ is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ and مُبِينٌ an adjective; and the clause is a justification with no position.
(ثَمانِيَةَ أَزْواجٍ مِنَ الضَّأْنِ اثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ الْمَعْزِ اثْنَيْنِ) ثَمانِيَةَ أَزْواجٍ is a badal (substitute) of حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً; and it is said it is accusative by كُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ, or by an implied «أنشأ», and to this al-Kisāʾī inclined. Al-zawj is that with which there is another of its kind that pairs with it, and from the two offspring result; and what is meant is four males of each of camels, cattle and sheep/goats, and four females likewise. مِنَ الضَّأْنِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an implied verb أَنْشَأَ; اثْنَيْنِ is a badal of ثَمانِيَةَ أَزْواجٍ, and the rest of the eight were conjoined to it.
(قُلْ آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ) قُلْ is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) and has no position; the hamza is for denunciatory interrogation; آلذَّكَرَيْنِ is a direct object fronted before حَرَّمَ; أَمْ is a conjunction; الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ is conjoined to الذَّكَرَيْنِ; and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the content of the saying.
(أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحامُ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ) The second أَمْ is a conjunction; it conjoined the relative «ما» after it to الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ, so it is in the position of an accusative. When a quiescent mīm met what follows it, assimilation (idghām) became obligatory; further explanation of that will come in the section on Benefits.
(نَبِّئُونِي بِعِلْمٍ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) The clause is also parenthetical, introduced to show their incapacity. These two parenthetical clauses occurred among the enumerated items to stress the falsity of their sayings. نَبِّئُونِي is an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; بِعِلْمٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نَبِّئُونِي; إِنْ is conditional; كان and its noun, which is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and صادِقِينَ is its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes indicates it.
(وَمِنَ الْإِبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ اثْنَيْنِ قُلْ آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحامُ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ) The i'rab of its parallel has been given exactly.
(أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَداءَ إِذْ وَصَّاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهذا) أَمْ is the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa), estimated as «بل» and the hamza, the estimate being: "rather, were you witnesses?". إِذْ is an adverb attached to شُهَداءَ, and the clause وَصَّاكُمُ اللَّهُ is in the position of a genitive by annexation; بِهذا is attached to وَصَّاكُمُ.
(فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً لِيُضِلَّ النَّاسَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) The fāʾ is the eloquent one (faṣīḥa), i.e. "when you have known this and it has taken root in your minds"; مَنْ is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ and أَظْلَمُ is the khabar, and the clause has no position; the interrogation has the sense of negation, i.e. "no one is more wrongful". مِمَّنِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أَظْلَمُ; the clause افْتَرى has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; عَلَى اللَّهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to افْتَرى; كَذِباً is a direct object or an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), and the i'rab of its parallel has preceded. The lām is for justification; يُضِلَّ is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أَنْ after the lām of justification; النَّاسَ is a direct object; the lām of justification and what follows it are attached to افْتَرى; بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of افْتَرى, i.e. he fabricated against Him the Exalted.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ) إِنَّ and its noun; the clause لا يَهْدِي is its khabar; الْقَوْمَ is a direct object and الظَّالِمِينَ a naʿt (adjective) of الْقَوْمَ; and the nominal clause is a justification with no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
Idghām (assimilation): It is the entering of one letter into another letter of its kind, such that the two become a single doubled letter. It has three states:

1- Obligatory assimilation:
That is when the two are homogeneous in a single word. As for the words of the poet:
الحمد لله العليّ الأجلل ... الواسع الفضل الوهوب المجزل
(Praise be to Allah, the Most High, the Most Exalted, the Vast in bounty, the Bestower, the Generous.)
it is among the poetic necessities. Assimilation of two identical adjoining letters, the first of which has a vowel, is obligatory when they are in two words, as when they are in one word, such as: سكتّ, سكّنا, عنّي and عليّ, and اكتب بالقلم, and استغفر ربك, and like the verse we are dealing with, «أمّا اشتملت عليه». Some words are irregular and not to be taken as a model, such as: ألل السّقاء والأسنان (when their smell changes and spoils), دبب الإنسان (when hair grows on his forehead), ضببت الأرض (when its lizards become many), قطط الشعر (when it is short and curly; and one says قطّ with assimilation), لححت العين (when its eyelids stick together with rheum), and الخخت (when its tears are many and its eyelids thick).

2- Permissibility of assimilation and of leaving it:
This occurs in four places:
(a) That the first letter of the two identical ones is vowelled and the second is quiescent with an incidental sukūn, for the jussive or for the construction (binā') in the singular imperative; so you say: لم يمدّ and مدّ with assimilation, and لم يمدد and امدد; and the unassimilated is better, and the Qurʾān speaks with it. The Exalted said: «يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار». And He said: «واشدد على قلوبهم». The vowel of the second of the two assimilated letters in the jussive imperfect and the imperative, to which nothing has been attached, follows the vowel of its first letter, and this is the more frequent; and we hold that it should be vowelled with fatḥa for lightness.
(b) That the ʿayn of the word and its lām are two yāʾs, the second of which necessarily takes a vowel, such as: عيي and حيي. So you say: عيّ and حيّ; and if the vowel of the second is incidental, for the sake of case-ending, such as لن يحيي, its assimilation is prevented.
(c) That at the beginning of the past verb there are two tāʾs, such as: تتابع and تتبّع; assimilation is then permitted with the addition of a hamzat waṣl at its beginning, to avert beginning with a quiescent letter, such as: اتّابع and اتّبع. If it is imperfect, assimilation is not permitted, but lightening it is permitted by dropping one of the two tāʾs, so you say for تتلظّى: تلظّى, and for تتجلّى: تجلّى. The Exalted said: «تنزّل الملائكة والرّوح», and He said: «نارا تلظّى»; and Abū Tammām said, describing spring:
أضحت تصوغ بطونها لظهورها ... نورا تكاد له القلوب تنوّر
(They (the clouds/the plants) have come to fashion, from their insides for their backs, a light at which hearts almost become illumined.)
(d) That two identical vowelled letters adjoin in two words, such as: جعل لي, and كتب بالقلم. Assimilation is then permitted by making the first identical letter quiescent, so you say: جعل لي and كتب بالقلم «[Translator's note: the source prints these two examples exactly as in the previous sentence, without showing the assimilated pronunciation; they are given as written. The word printed "تقل" is evidently "تقول", "you say".]», except that assimilation is permitted here in pronunciation and not in writing.

3- Prevention of assimilation:
That is in seven places:
(a) That the two identical letters stand at the beginning, like ددن, i.e. play.
(b) That they are in a noun on the pattern فُعَل (ḍamma then fatḥa) like دُرَر, or فُعُل (two ḍammas) like سُرُر, or فِعَل (kasra then fatḥa) like لِمَم, or فَعَل (two fatḥas) like طَلَل.
(c) That the two identical letters are in a pattern augmented for linking (ilḥāq), like جلبب and هيلل.
(d) That something already assimilated is attached to the beginning of the two identical letters, like هلّل. That is because the second assimilation would be like a repetition of assimilation, which is prohibited.
(e) That the two identical letters are on the pattern «افْعِلْ» in the exclamation of wonder, as in: أحبب بالعلم.
«[Translator's note: the source gives no letter "و" for the next item; it is translated as it appears, unlettered.]» And that the sukūn of one of the two identical letters occurs incidentally, because of its attachment to a vowelled nominative pronoun, like مددت.
(ز) That it is among what the Arabs irregularly left unassimilated by choice, and these are memorised words, mentioned at the beginning of the discussion.

dervis-irab:151-151.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تعال): one of the specific usages that became general; originally it was said by one who was in a high place to one below him, then it became frequent and widened until it became general. It is an imperative verb that always has a fatḥa at its end, and for this reason they accused Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī of a grammatical error in his saying:
أيا جارتا ما أنصف الدهر بيننا ... تعالي أقاسمك الهموم تعالي
(O my neighbour, Time has not been fair between us; come, let me share my sorrows with you, come.)

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: تَعالَوْا أَتْلُ ما حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ): a new sentence, uttered to command him ﷺ to recite to them what their Lord has forbidden them, as a reality and not a conjecture, as certainty and not guesswork. The clause تعالوا is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying; it is an imperative verb indeclinable through the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; أتل is an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the answer to a request, though Ibn Hishām prefers to say that it is the answer of an implied condition; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a direct object; the clause حرم عليكم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e.
"that which He has forbidden". It is also permissible that "ما" be a maṣdar particle, i.e. "recite the forbidding of your Lord"; but a prohibition is not recited; rather it is a maṣdar standing in the place of the direct object.
ربكم is the agent of حرم; and عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حرم or to أتل, on the basis that the matter belongs to the chapter of conflict (tanāzuʿ). (أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئاً وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً): there are many views on "أن", of which two are preferred. The first is that it is explicative, because what has the meaning of saying, without its letters, precedes it; لا is prohibitive; تشركوا is an imperfect verb jussive by it, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative. The second view is that it is a maṣdar particle, and it and what is within its scope are a badal of «ما حرم»; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تشركوا; شيئا is a direct object, or in the sense of a maṣdar, in which case it is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); and a like of it has been indicated before. بالوالدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the verb of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "show kindness to the parents"; and إحسانا is an absolute object of the omitted verb. An important discussion by Ibn Hishām on the i'rab of this verse will come in the section on Benefits. (وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تقتلوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; أولادكم is a direct object; من إملاق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقتلوا, i.e. "for the sake of poverty", so من is causal (sababiyya); the object of purpose was not put in the accusative because its condition fails, since الإملاق is a maṣdar that is not of the heart; further discussion of it will come in the section on Rhetoric. نحن is a mubtadaʾ and the clause نرزقكم is the khabar; the clause نحن نرزقكم is resumptive, giving the reason for the prohibition before it; إياهم is conjoined to the pronoun in نرزقكم; and He put those addressed before the pronoun of the children, the reverse of the verse in al-Isrāʾ, for a rhetorical secret that will come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَلا تَقْرَبُوا الْفَواحِشَ ما ظَهَرَ مِنْها وَما بَطَنَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تقربوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and the wāw is the agent; الفواحش is a direct object; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a badal of الفواحش, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl); the clause ظهر has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ظهر; and ما بطن is conjoined to ما ظهر. (وَلا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ): conjoined to what precedes and included within its scope, to complete the list of prohibitions, which are ten things.
لا is prohibitive; تقتلوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; النفس is a direct object; التي is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as an adjective; the clause حرم الله has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; إلا is a particle of restriction; and the exception is an emptied one from the most general of circumstances, i.e. "do not kill it in any circumstance except the circumstance of your being linked with the truth", so the باء is the باء of accompaniment, and it with its genitive noun is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the wāw in «تقتلوا». It is also permissible that the emptied exception be from the verb itself, in which case the preposition and its genitive noun are an absolute object, i.e. "except the killing that is linked with the truth", such as retaliation (qawad), the ḥadd for apostasy, and the stoning of a muḥṣan. (ذلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause is resumptive, uttered to point to what precedes; the clause وصاكم is the khabar of ذلكم; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to وصاكم; and لعلكم تعقلون is لعل with its noun and khabar; the clause of hope is a ḥāl clause, i.e. "that you may use your intellects, which restrain your selves and hold them back from committing these prohibited things".

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains marvellous varieties of rhetoric that require length, but it is a length that does not weary, for talk of beauty is long, and the longer it is, the more it improves, like beauty itself: the more you look closely at it, the more the marks of its loveliness increase:
يزيدك وجهه حسنا ... إذا ما زدته نظرا
(His face increases you in beauty whenever you increase your gazing.)

1- Tawhīm (creating a false impression):
The first art in this verse is the art of tawhīm, which was indicated in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, and we renew our acquaintance with it here and say: it is that the speaker brings a word such that what follows it of speech gives the impression that the speaker intended a corruption of it (taṣḥīf), whereas he intends something else; and that is in His saying: «أن لا تشركوا به شيئا».
For the apparent speech indicates the prohibition of the negation of polytheism, and its entailment is the permitting of polytheism, which is impossible and contrary to the intended meaning. The interpretation that resolves the difficulty is that, among the commands mentioned in the context of the verse and what follows, there are things forbidden to them and things they are commanded to do. Polytheism towards Allah, the killing of the inviolable soul, and the consuming of the orphan's property are among what is forbidden outwardly and inwardly, while giving full measure and weight with equity, justice in speech let alone in deed, fulfilling the covenant, and following the straight path are among the deeds commanded with an obligatory command. Were the speech to come without «لا», it would be cut off, disordered and corrupted in meaning, for the meaning would become: "He has forbidden you polytheism and kindness to parents", which is the opposite of the intended meaning. For this reason the addition came, whose outward appearance gave the impression of corruption of meaning, so that one would resort to the interpretation by which the conjoining of the remaining commands to what precedes is made sound.

2- Taghāyur (variation):
The second art in it is taghāyur, and that is in His saying: «ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق». Its definition is the variation of two approaches, whether in a single meaning, such that a person praises a thing or blames it, or blames what another has praised, and the reverse, and prefers one thing over another, then returns and makes the less-preferred one the preferred. Among the forms of taghāyur is the variation of meaning through the variation of wording, as in His saying: «ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق نحن نرزقكم وإياهم», which differs from His saying on this very same subject in (Sūrat) Banī Isrāʾīl: «ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقهم وإياكم». In the verse of al-Anʿām He put (the parents) first because it is addressed to the poor, as His saying «من إملاق» shows; so rhetoric required that the promise to them, I mean the impoverished fathers, of provision that would enrich them come first, and rhetoric required completing the meaning with a promise for the sons after the promise for the fathers, so that the souls might be completely at rest. In Banī Isrāʾīl the address is to the rich, as His saying «خشية إملاق» shows, for none fears poverty but the rich, while the poor man's poverty is already present. So rhetoric required putting first the promise of provision to the sons, so that this precedence might point to the fact that He, glory be to Him, is the One who provides for the sons, in order to remove what the rich imagined, that by spending on the sons they would come to poverty after wealth; then this reassurance was completed by their promise of provision after the promise for their sons. Glory be to the One who spoke this speech!

Taghāyur in Arabic poetry:
The poets have excelled in this meaning, played with it and taken every path with it, and we shall present to you below a selection of what has been completed by taghāyur, where poets praised what is commonly blamed and blamed what deserves praise. The first to allude to this was ʿAntara ibn Shaddād, the ʿAbsī poet and the famous horseman, when he desired to kiss swords because they gleamed like the flash of the mouth of the one who loves them, and he said his two famous verses:
ولقد ذكرتك والرماح نواهل ... منّي وبيض الهند تقطر من دمي
(I remembered you while the spears were drinking from me and the white swords of India were dripping with my blood,)
فوددت تقبيل السيوف لأنها ... لمعت كبارق ثغرك المتبسّم
(and I longed to kiss the swords because they gleamed like the flash of your smiling mouth.)
How lovely is the saying of Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī, who took another path and said:
مسيء محسن طورا وطورا ... فما أدري عدّوي أم حبيبي
(At one time wrongdoer and at another benefactor; I do not know whether he is my enemy or my beloved.)
يقلّب مقلة ويدير طرفا ... به عرف البريء من المريب
(He turns an eye and rolls a glance by which the innocent is known from the suspect.)
وبعض الظالمين وإن تناهى ... شهيّ الظلم مغتفر الذنوب
(And some wrongdoers, even if they go to extremes, are pleasing in their wrong and their sins are forgiven.)
Al-Buḥturī was fond of this art, and said:
عيّرتني بالشيب من بدآته ... في عذاري بالهجر والاجتناب
(She reproached me for grey hair, from its beginnings at my cheek, with shunning and avoidance.)
لا تريه عارا فما هو بالشيب ولكنه جلاء الشباب
(Do not see it as a disgrace; it is not grey hair, but rather the brightening of youth.) [Translator's note: the source prints this verse as a single run without the hemistich separator]
وبياض البازيّ أصدق حسنا ... إن تأمّلت من سواد الغراب
(And the whiteness of the falcon is truer in beauty, if you ponder, than the blackness of the raven.)
And he said on the same meaning, and did well:
عذلتنا في عشقها أمّ عمرو ... هل سمعتم بالعاذل المعشوق؟
(Umm ʿAmr blamed us for loving her; have you ever heard of a blamer who is beloved?)
ورأت لمّة ألمّ بها الشّيب فريعت من ظلمة في شروق
(She saw a lock of hair that grey had touched, and was alarmed at a darkness amid a dawn.)
ولعمري لولا الأقاحي لأبصر ... ت أنيق الرياض غير أنيق
(By my life, were it not for the white camomile flowers, you would see the lovely meadows as not lovely.)
ومزاج الصهباء بالماء أولى ... بصبوح مستحسن وغبوق
(And mixing the red wine with water is better suited to a morning or evening draught that is deemed good.)
وسواد العيون لو لم يكمّل ... ببياض ما كان بالموموق
(And the blackness of the eyes, were it not completed by whiteness, would not be admired.)
أيّ ليل يبهى بغير نجوم؟ ... وسماء تندى بغير بروق؟
(What night is splendid without stars? And what sky is moist without lightning?)
Al-Buḥturī described the day of parting as short, though people have agreed on its length, where he said:
ولقد تأمّلت الفراق فلم أجد ... يوم الفراق على امرئ بطويل
(I have pondered parting and found the day of parting not long for anyone.)
قصرت مسافته على متزوّر ... منه لدهر هن صبابة وغليل
(Its span is short for one who visits from it, for a time of longing and thirst.) [Translator's note: the second verse is textually obscure in the source]
As for Ibn al-Rūmī, he rose above the earlier and later poets in blaming what people have agreed to praise, and said, satirising the full moon:
لو أراد الأديب أن يهجو البد ... ر رماه بالخطة الشنعاء
(If the man of letters wished to satirise the full moon, he would pelt it with the ugly charge.)
قال: يا بدر أنت تغدر بالسا ... ري وتغري بزائر الحسناء
(He would say: O full moon, you betray the night traveller and expose the visitor of the beauty.)
يعتريك المحاق في كل شهر ... فترى كالقلامة الحجناء
(The waning befalls you every month, and you appear like a curved nail-paring.)
نمش في بياض وجهك يحكي ... كلفا فوق وجنة برصاء
(Freckles in the whiteness of your face resemble blotches on the cheek of a leper.)
لا لأجل المديح بل خيفة الهجر أخذنا جوائز الخلفاء
(Not for the sake of praise but for fear of abandonment have we taken the caliphs' rewards.) [Translator's note: this line, appended in the source without a hemistich separator, appears to be a separate fragment]
And al-Sharīf al-Raḍī satirised the sun, saying:
في خلقة الشمس وأخلاقها ... شتى عيوب ستة تذكر
(In the sun's creation and character are various faults, six of which may be mentioned.)
رمداء عمشاء إذا أصبحت ... عمياء عند الليل لا تبصر
(She is bleary and dim-eyed by morning, and blind at night, unable to see.)
ويغتدي البدر لها كاسفا ... وجرمه من جرمها أصغر
(The full moon becomes dimmed beside her, though its body is smaller than hers.)
حرورها في القيظ لا يتّقى ... ودفؤها في القر مستحقر
(Her scorching heat in summer cannot be warded off, and her warmth in the cold is despised.)
وخلقها خلق الملول الذي ... ينكث للعهد ولا يبصر
(Her nature is the nature of the weary one who breaks the covenant and does not see.)
ليست بحسناء وما حسن من ... يحسر منه الطرف إذ ينظر
(She is not beautiful, and what beauty is it from which the eye recoils when it looks?)
Were we to expand, we would fill the whole book with this delightful, unique poetry, but it suffices us of the necklace to take what encircles the neck.

3- Al-majāz al-mursal (the unrestricted figurative use):
In His saying, the Exalted: «من إملاق», which runs the course of a metonymy (kināya), because when his wealth leaves his hand poverty rides him, so the word of the cause is used in the place of the effect. It is said in Asās al-Balāgha: "Among the figurative usages: أملق الدهر ماله, 'Time took his wealth away and removed it from his hand'; and أملق الرجل means 'the man spent his wealth until he became poor', and he is a مملق. A Bedouin said: 'May Allah fight women, how they draw out excuses, as if they came out from beneath their feet', i.e. they extract them."

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām has a lengthy discussion of this verse. He said: "As for His saying, the Exalted:
«قل تعالوا أتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم أن لا تشركوا به شيئا», it was said that لا is negative, it was said prohibitive, and it was said redundant, and all are possible. The sum of the matter in the verse is that «ما» is declarative, in the sense of "that which", in the accusative by «أتل», and «حرم ربكم» is the ṣila, and «عليكم» is attached to حرم. This is the apparent view. Al-Zajjāj allowed «ما» to be interrogative, in the accusative by حرم, with the clause quoted by «أتل», because it has the sense of "I say"; and it is permissible that «عليكم» be attached to «أتل», and whoever prefers giving effect to the first of the two conflicting words, namely the Kufans, prefers it over its being attached to حرّم. Concerning «أن» and what follows it there are several views: first, that the two are in the position of the accusative as a badal of «ما», on the basis that it is relative and not interrogative, since the badal is not accompanied by the interrogative hamza. Second, that the two are in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted «هو»; some of the grammarians allowed these two. On these two, «لا» is redundant; Ibn al-Shajarī said: the correct view is that it is negative on the first and redundant on the second.
Third, that the original is: 'He made that clear to you so that you not associate partners (with Him)'; this is because when their leaders forbid them what Allah, glory be to Him, the Exalted, has made lawful, and they obey them, they commit polytheism, because they have set up other than Allah in His position. Fourth, that the original is: 'I enjoin you not to associate partners', by the proof that «وبالوالدين إحسانا» means 'and I enjoin you regarding the parents', and that at the end of the verse is «ذلكم وصّاكم به'; on these two views the clause and the preposition are omitted. Fifth, that the implied form is: «أتل عليكم أن لا تشركوا», indicated by what precedes. Al-Zajjāj allowed these three views. Sixth, that the speech is complete at «حرم ربكم», then begins «عليكم أن لا تشركوا وأن تحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا وأن لا تقتلوا ولا تقربوا»; in that case «عليكم» is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning 'hold fast to'. «أن» in the six views is a maṣdar particle, and «لا» in the last four views is negative. Seventh, that «أن» is explicative, with the meaning of 'أي', and «لا» is prohibitive, and the verb is jussive, not accusative, as if it had been said: 'I say to you: do not associate anything with Him, and show kindness to the parents.' These two views were allowed by Ibn al-Shajarī." Ibn Hishām also said in another place in al-Mughnī:
"As for the saying of some of them regarding «قل تعالوا أتل ما حرم عليكم ربكم أن لا تشركوا به شيئا» that the pause is before «عليكم», and that «عليكم» is an incitement (ighrāʾ), it is good, and it escapes an apparent difficulty in the verse that requires interpretation."
We have lengthened the quotation only because much has been said about the verse. So reflect, and Allah protect you.

dervis-irab:123-124.t:
* Vocabulary:
(صَغارٌ): al-ṣaghār (with fatḥa on the ṣād) is abasement and humiliation. One says ṣaghira (like karuma), ṣaghran (with kasra on the ṣād and fatḥa on the ghayn), and ṣaghran (with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the ghayn), and ṣaghār (with fatḥa on the ṣād and the ghayn), and ṣaghāra and ṣughrān (with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the ghayn). As for ṣaghura (with fatḥa on the ṣād and ḍamma on the ghayn, and likewise ṣaghira with kasra on the ghayn), it is the opposite of "to be big" and "to be great". [Translator's note: the vowel marks in the source's description of these forms are partly unclear; the forms are rendered as the description states them.]

* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ جَعَلْنا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكابِرَ مُجْرِمِيها) A resumptive speech, to begin dividing people into the strong and the weak; and He singled out the great ones for crime because they are most able to spread crime and corruption. It was also said to be a conjunction on what precedes it, and there is nothing to prevent that. وكذلك is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, as has preceded. وجعلنا is a verb and fāʿil; وفي كل قرية is the second object of جعلنا; وأكابر is the first object of جعلنا; and مجرميها is a muḍāf ilayhi to أكابر.
(لِيَمْكُرُوا فِيها وَما يَمْكُرُونَ إِلَّا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَما يَشْعُرُونَ) The lām is for giving a reason; it was also said to be the lām of consequence or of becoming (ʿāqiba, ṣayrūra), and both are correct; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعلنا. The wāw is a ḥāl wāw; ما is negative; ويمكرون is an imperfect verb, and the sentence is accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يمكروا; إلا is a particle of restriction; and بأنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يمكرون. The wāw is a ḥāl wāw; ما is negative; and the sentence ما يشعرون is in the position of the accusative from the pronoun of يمكرون.
(وَإِذا جاءَتْهُمْ آيَةٌ قالُوا: لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ حَتَّى نُؤْتى مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيَ رُسُلُ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a coordinate conjunction on what has preceded; إذا is an adverb of future time attached to قالوا; the sentence جاءتهم is in the position of the genitive by annexation; وآية is the fāʿil; and the sentence قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. لن is a particle of negation, subjunctive and futurity; ونؤمن is an imperfect verb, accusative because of لن, and the sentence is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl. حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; ونؤتى is a passive imperfect verb, accusative through an implied أن after حتى, its nāʾib fāʿil being latent; ومثل is the second mafʿūl bihi; ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation; the sentence أوتي has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative; and رسل الله is the nāʾib fāʿil.
(اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسالَتَهُ) الله is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم is its khabar. As for حيث:
The opinions of the grammarians differ on it. One group said: it is not an adverb, because it is not for Him the Exalted to be more knowing in one place than in another, and because His knowledge does not differ with the difference of places. It is rather a mafʿūl bihi of a verb indicated by «أعلم», that is: "He knows the place fit for placing His message, and these are not people worthy of having it placed in them."
Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Baḥr: "The apparent view is to leave it as a figurative adverbial, with «أعلم» containing the sense of a verb that governs an adverb, so that the implied form is: Allah is the most effective in knowledge where He places, that is, His knowledge is effective in this place in which He places His message." Al-Safāqusī said: "The apparent view is that it stays in its adverbial sense, and the difficulty arises only from the implication (mafhūm) of the adverb; and how many places there are in which the implication has been abandoned because of evidence for it, particularly as that evidence is present in this place." The sentence يجعل رسالته is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and رسالته is the mafʿūl bihi.
(سَيُصِيبُ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا صَغارٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَعَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِما كانُوا يَمْكُرُونَ) The sentence is resumptive, introduced to explain what will reach them on the Day of Resurrection. The sīn is a particle of futurity; ويصيب is an imperfect verb, nominative; الذين is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the sentence أجرموا has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative; وصغار is the fāʿil; وعند الله is an adverb attached to يصيب, or a naʿt of صغار, that is, "established with Allah"; وعذاب شديد is conjoined to صغار; the bāʾ is a preposition of causation; ما is a maṣdar particle or a relative in the sense of "that which"; the sentence كانوا has no grammatical position in either case; and the sentence يمكرون is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

dervis-irab:125-126.t:
* I'rab:
(فَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلامِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; من is a conditional noun, jussive-governing, a mubtadaʾ; ويرد is the protasis and الله is its fāʿil; أن يهديه is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative because it is a mafʿūl bihi, that is, "guidance" (هداية); ويشرح is the apodosis; وصدره is the mafʿūl bihi; and للاسلام is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشرح. The protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من».
(وَمَنْ يُرِدْ أَنْ يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقاً حَرَجاً كَأَنَّما يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّماءِ) The wāw is a conjunction; من is a conditional noun, jussive-governing, conjoined to the first «من»; أن يضلّه is an interpreted maṣdar, the object of يرد; ويرد is the protasis; ويجعل is the apodosis, jussive; وصدره is the mafʿūl bihi; وضيقا is the second mafʿūl bihi; وحرجا is a naʿt of «ضيقا»; the comparative sentence beginning كأنما is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from صدره, or from the latent pronoun in «ضيقا», where (كأنما) is restrictive and restricted (kāffa and makfūfa); ويصعّد is an imperfect verb; and في السماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يصّعد.
(كَذلِكَ يَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ الرِّجْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) The sentence is resumptive; and كذلك, the preposition and its genitive noun, is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar; ويجعل is an imperfect verb; الله is the fāʿil; الرجس is the mafʿūl bihi; وعلى الذين is in the position of the second object; and the sentence لا يؤمنون is the ṣila of the relative.
(وَهذا صِراطُ رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيماً) The sentence is resumptive, introduced to explain that what Muhammad ﷺ follows is Islam. وهذا is a mubtadaʾ; وصراط ربك is the khabar; ومستقيما is a ḥāl confirming the sentence (ḥāl muʾakkida), and the operator in it is the demonstrative, in view of the sense of a verb in it, for it means "I point" (أشير).
(قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ) The sentence is resumptive; قد is a particle of confirmation; فصلنا الآيات is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; ولقوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فصّلنا; and the sentence يذكرون is a naʿt of قوم.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «كأنما يصّعد في السماء» there is a representational simile abstracted from several things, that is: the state of one whose breast has been made narrow and constricted is like the state of one who is charged with climbing into the sky. Its like has passed before.

dervis-irab:145-146.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَسْفُوحاً): Al-safḥ: pouring. Safaḥa comes both intransitive and transitive; one says: safaḥa so-and-so his tears and his blood, i.e. he shed it; except that the difference between them is made by the difference of the maṣdar: in the transitive one says safḥan, and in the intransitive one says sufūḥan.
