In this verse it occurs transitively, because the passive participle is formed only from a transitive verb. And as an intransitive example is what Abū ʿUbayda recited for Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
أقول ودمعي واكف عند رسمها ... عليك سلام الله والدمع يسفح
(I say, with my tears dripping by her abode: Peace of Allah be upon you, while the tears flow.)
And of the figurative use in this root: وبينهم سفاح, i.e. fighting or mutual slaughter (of camels), because they shed one another's blood; and سافحها مسافحة: he committed fornication with her, because each of them pours out his fluid and wastes it. Among their sayings: «في النكاح غنية عن السفاح» ("in marriage there is sufficiency from fornication").
This root has already been mentioned, together with the characteristics of the sīn and the fāʾ being the first and second radicals of the word.
(الْحَوايا): The intestines and bowels.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: لا أَجِدُ فِي ما أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً عَلى طاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ) A resumptive statement introduced to explain what Allah the Exalted forbade to them. The clause لا أَجِدُ is the content of the saying; فِيما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أَجِدُ; the clause أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; إِلَيَّ is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of a nominative as the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) of أُوحِيَ; مُحَرَّماً is a direct object of أَجِدُ, i.e. "a forbidden thing"; and عَلى …
(إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَماً مَسْفُوحاً أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنزِيرٍ) The exception is connected (muttaṣil). طاعِمٍ is a preposition's genitive noun attached to مُحَرَّماً (with the preposition عَلى), and the clause يَطْعَمُهُ is an adjective of طاعِمٍ, because it is an exception from the genus, and its position is accusative; it is also permissible that it be a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because it is an "occurrence" and what precedes is a substance, and its position is accusative also. مَيْتَةً is the khabar (predicate) of يَكُونَ, and its noun is latent, referring to His words «مُحَرَّماً»; the exception clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). دَماً is conjoined to مَيْتَةً, and مَسْفُوحاً is an adjective, i.e. flowing, like blood in the veins, not like the liver and spleen; and أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنزِيرٍ is conjoined likewise.
«[Translator's note: the source text in the first clause breaks off at "وعلى"; it is rendered as printed.]»
(فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقاً أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ) The fāʾ is for justification; inna and its noun; رِجْسٌ is its khabar; أَوْ is a conjunction; فِسْقاً is conjoined to لَحْمَ خِنزِيرٍ; the clause أُهِلَّ is an adjective, أُهِلَّ being a past verb; لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; بِهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أُهِلَّ; and the clause «فإنه رجس» is a justification with no position.
(فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ باغٍ وَلا عادٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The fāʾ is resumptive; مَنِ is a jussive conditional noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); اضْطُرَّ is a passive past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, i.e. "then there is no blame on him". The meaning of اضْطُرَّ is: necessity befell him, calling him to partake of something of what was mentioned. غَيْرَ باغٍ is a ḥāl, i.e. not unjust; وَلا عادٍ is conjoined to باغٍ, i.e. not a transgressor. A similar statement has been verified in Sūrat al-Baqara. The fāʾ is for justification; inna and its noun; غَفُورٌ is a first khabar and رَحِيمٌ a second khabar; and the clause of the protasis and its apodosis is the khabar of «مَنِ».
(وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ) A resumptive statement introduced to explain the reason for the prohibition of everything with a hoof/claw (ẓufur) to the Jews, because of their wrongdoing; the verification of that has preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara. It includes everything with a ẓufur, namely the ostrich, the camel and the like of animals, and everything that does not have split digits among beasts and birds, such as the camel, the ostrich, the goose and the duck. عَلَى الَّذِينَ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حَرَّمْنا; هادُوا is a verb and an agent; حَرَّمْنا is also a verb and an agent; كُلَّ is a direct object; ذِي is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement); and ظُفُرٍ is genitive by the annexation of «ذِي» to it.
(وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ وَالْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُما) The wāw is a conjunction; مِنَ الْبَقَرِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حَرَّمْنا, and الْغَنَمِ is conjoined to الْبَقَرِ; عَلَيْهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حَرَّمْنا; and شُحُومَهُما is a direct object. The meaning is that He forbade to them the meat of everything with a ẓufur, and its fat, and everything from it, and left cattle and sheep/goats permitted, and forbade from them only the pure fats, namely al-thurūb, i.e. the thin fats that cover the paunch and the intestines, and the fat of the kidneys. (The kidneys are) the plural of kulya or kulwa, with ḍamma on the kāf in both.
(إِلَّا ما حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُما أَوِ الْحَوايا أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ) إِلَّا is a particle of exception; مَا is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as a connected exception from al-shuḥūm; the exception clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); the clause حَمَلَتْ has no position because it is a ṣila; أَوْ is a conjunction and الْحَوايا is conjoined to ظُهُورُهُما; أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ: أَوْ is a conjunction, and مَا is a relative noun conjoined to ظُهُورُهُما; اخْتَلَطَ is a past verb, its agent being "he" (latent); and بِعَظْمٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اخْتَلَطَ.
(ذلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ بِبَغْيِهِمْ وَإِنَّا لَصادِقُونَ) The clause has no position because it is explicative (mufassira), to explain the reason for the prohibition. ذلِكَ is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ; the clause جَزَيْناهُمْ is the khabar; بِبَغْيِهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جَزَيْناهُمْ; a pronoun must be supposed, i.e. "we recompensed them with it, because of their transgression". More of the i'rab of this expression will come. The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and صادِقُونَ is the khabar of inna.

* Benefits:
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "ذلك is in the position of an accusative by جَزَيْناهُمْ; and it is said: a mubtadaʾ, the estimate being 'we recompensed them for it' (جزينا هموه); and it is said: a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. 'the matter is that'." It is noticed that Abū l-Baqāʾ did not explain on what basis it is accusative: is it as a maṣdar or as a direct object? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ذلك is the recompense with which we recompensed them, and it is the prohibition of good things", and its apparent sense is that it is accusative in the manner of a maṣdar. Abū Ḥayyān said: "Ibn Mālik claimed that a demonstrative noun does not become accusative, being used to point to the maṣdar, unless it is followed by the maṣdar; so you say: قمت هذا القيام, and قعدت ذلك القعود. It is not permissible to say: قمت هذا, nor قعد ذلك." On this basis it is not sound for «ذلك» to be accusative as a pointing to the maṣdar. I say: Sībawayh and the majority held that this is not a condition, and among the speech of the Arabs: «ظننت ذلك», by which they point to the supposition.

dervis-irab:127-128.t:
* I'rab:
(لَهُمْ دارُ السَّلامِ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) A resumptive sentence with no grammatical position, as if it came as an answer to a questioner asking what Allah has prepared for them, and he was told that. It is also possible that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يذكرون. ولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced khabar; ودار السلام is a postponed mubtadaʾ; وعند ربهم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl from «دار السلام», the operator in it being the sense of abiding latent in «لهم»; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; وهو is a mubtadaʾ; ووليهم is the khabar; the bāʾ is a preposition of causation; ما is a relative noun or a maṣdar particle; the sentence كانوا has no grammatical position in either case; and the sentence يعملون is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
(وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعاً يا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ قَدِ اسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ)
The wāw is resumptive; ويوم is an adverb accusative through an omitted verb, that is: "and remember the day We gather them" (واذكر يوم نحشرهم); the sentence نحشرهم (with nūn or yāʾ, both being readings) is in the position of the genitive by annexation after the adverb; and جميعا is a ḥāl. Abū Ḥayyān said: "Some made «يوم» a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted اذكر. It is preferable that the adverb be governed by the verb of saying with which the vocative is quoted, that is: 'And the day We gather them, We say: O assembly of the jinn' ; and this is preferable to what some permitted, namely making it accusative through اذكر as a mafʿūl bihi, because it takes it out of being an adverb." ويا معشر الجن is a vocative muḍāf, the maqūl of an omitted saying, that is: "and We say to them: O assembly of the jinn". قد is a particle of confirmation; واستكثرتم is a verb and fāʿil; and ومن الإنس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استكثرتم.
(وَقالَ أَوْلِياؤُهُمْ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ رَبَّنَا اسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنا بِبَعْضٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; وقال أولياؤهم is a verb and fāʿil; ومن الإنس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; وربنا is a vocative muḍāf from which the vocative particle has been omitted; واستمتع بعضنا is a verb and fāʿil; وببعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استمتع; and the sentence is in the position of the accusative as the saying.
(وَبَلَغْنا أَجَلَنَا الَّذِي أَجَّلْتَ لَنا) The wāw is a conjunction; وبلغنا is a verb and fāʿil; وأجلنا is the object; والذي is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of «أجلنا»; the sentence أجلت has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative; and ولنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أجلت.
(قالَ النَّارُ مَثْواكُمْ خالِدِينَ فِيها إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ) The sentence is resumptive, introduced to convey Allah the Exalted's answer to them. وقال is a past verb whose fāʿil refers to Allah; والنار is a mubtadaʾ; ومثواكم is the khabar; the nominal sentence is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl; وخالدين is a ḥāl from the kāf in «مثواكم»; وفيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالدين; and وإلا ما شاء الله: إلا is a particle of exception, and ما is a relative noun or a maṣdar particle in the position of the accusative as an exception of the same genus, taking into account time, or place, or the punishment, since خالدين indicates them, that is: "abiding for every period of the periods, except the time of Allah's will", or "abiding in a specific place and punishment, unless Allah wills to transfer them to something other than the two". More discussion of this astonishing exception will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ) إن and its ism; حكيم is its first khabar and عليم its second khabar; and the sentence has no grammatical position because it is in the nature of a giving of reasons.

* Rhetoric:
We spoke in the section on i'rab about the astonishing exception, in accordance with what the context and the grammatical texts guide to. But the seeker of the ideal rhetoric is not satisfied with such facility, and for this reason the rhetoricians took care over this verse and its sister from Sūrat Hūd, as will come, and the disagreements and discussions around it multiplied; we shall content ourselves with the most important of what we reached.

The view of al-Zamakhsharī:
1- Al-Zamakhsharī has a fine view, far from forced interpretations and nearer to precision. He said: "Or it may be of the speech of the one who has been wronged (mawtūr) who has gained the upper hand over his oppressor and keeps gnashing his teeth at him, while he is asked to ease the grip on his throat: 'May Allah destroy me if I ease it for you, unless you will' , and he knows that he wills only to take his satisfaction from him with the utmost he is able to of harshness and severity. His saying 'unless you will' is thus among the severest of threats with mockery of the one threatened, because it comes out in the form of an exception that holds out hopes." What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is preferable to the reports and forced interpretations, such as their saying: "It has been reported that they will enter a valley in which there is so much of the zamharīr (freezing cold) that it separates some of their limbs from others, so they howl and ask to be returned to the Hellfire."

The view of al-Zajjāj:
We have come upon a fine view of al-Zajjāj's that quenches thirst, but it is truncated and needs clarification and disclosure. Al-Zajjāj said: "What is meant, and Allah knows best, is: except what He wills of increase of punishment." However he, that is al-Zajjāj, did not make clear how the exception is sound, and the excepted on this interpretation does not differ from the excepted-from in ruling. It is apparent that punishment is of varying degrees, differing ranks and unequal measures, and as if what is meant is that they are held in the prison of punishment, except what your Lord wills of an increase that reaches the extreme and surpasses the limit, until, for its reaching the farthest extremes, it is almost counted as outside punishment, as though it were not of it nor within its sphere. It is known of the Arabs in the ways of their speech that they express a thing by its opposite when it reaches the extreme. So it is as if these tormented people, with affliction having overwhelmed them, and having reached the extreme of severity and the end of hardship, have arrived at a limit that almost takes it out of absolute punishment, so that treating it in expression as something different became permissible. This is a leap of al-Zajjāj's whose import we perceive only through this elaboration, whose understanding requires fineness of taste and transparency of nature. And Allah is the granter of success.

dervis-irab:129-130.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نُوَلِّي): from wilāya, that is, authority (imāra). One says: wallā fulānan al-amra tawliya: he made him a governor over it. Its origin is from waliya (with the lām lightened and with kasra), yalī wilāya (with kasra on the wāw) and walāya (with fatḥa): the thing, and ʿalayhi: he undertook it and took possession of its affair; and waliya al-balad: he gained mastery over it.

* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ نُوَلِّي بَعْضَ الظَّالِمِينَ بَعْضاً بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; and كذلك is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, as has preceded in its like. It is also permissible that the preposition and its genitive noun be in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "The matter is like the appointing of some of the wrongdoers over others" (الأمر مثل تولية بعض الظالمين); to this al-Zajjāj inclined. ونولي is an imperfect verb; وبعض الظالمين is its first object; وبعضا is its second object, or accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "over some" (على بعض), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to نولي. وبما: the bāʾ is a preposition, ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نولّي; وكان and its ism; the sentence يكسبون is its khabar; and the sentence كانوا is the ṣila of the relative.
[Translator's note: in the source text of the following passages, the opening of each Qur'anic quotation is cut off or fused with the end of the preceding sentence (for example «امَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ», «صفةَقُصُّونَ», «الُوا شَهِدْنا», «َ غَرَّتْهُمُ»). They are translated below as the verses they evidently quote: (يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ), (يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي وَيُنْذِرُونَكُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا), (قالُوا شَهِدْنا عَلى أَنْفُسِنا), (وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا وَشَهِدُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كافِرِينَ).]
(يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ)
يا is a vocative particle; ومعشر الجن is a vocative muḍāf; the vocative sentence is the maqūl of an omitted saying, that is: "it is said to them"; and the omitted saying is a resumption introduced to relate the state of their rebuke. The hamza is for rhetorical, rebuking questioning; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion; ويأتكم is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لم; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; ورسل is the postponed fāʿil; and منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here, at «صفة»; the sentence evidently continues as «صفة لرسل» ("a naʿt of رسل")].
(يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي وَيُنْذِرُونَكُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا)
The sentence يقصون is a second naʿt of رسل; وعليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقصون, or to an omitted ḥāl, so that the indefinite noun is specified by the description. وآياتي is the mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is a conjunction; the sentence ينذرونكم is conjoined to يقصون, the wāw being the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; ولقاء is the second mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ينذرونكم; ويومكم is a muḍāf ilayhi; and هذا is a naʿt of ليومكم, or a badal from it.
(قالُوا شَهِدْنا عَلى أَنْفُسِنا)
The sentence is resumptive, introduced to serve as an answer to a question, as though it were asked: "What did they say after the rebuke?" The sentence شهدنا على أنفسنا is in the position of the accusative as the content of their saying; and على أنفسنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شهدنا, that is: "we acknowledged and affirmed".
(وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا وَشَهِدُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كافِرِينَ)
The wāw is parenthetical, and the sentence غرتهم الحياة الدنيا is a parenthetical one to show the extent of their persistence in delusion. He repeated their testimony against themselves because in the first He related their saying, and how they say and confess, while in the second He intended merely to censure them, to declare their opinions foolish, and to brand them with scant reflection. أن and what follows it are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "that they were disbelievers" (بأنهم كانوا كافرين); the sentence كانوا is the khabar of أن; and كافرين is the khabar of كانوا.

dervis-irab:147-148.t:
* I'rab:
(فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ رَبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ واسِعَةٍ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and إِنْ is conditional; كَذَّبُوكَ is a verb, an agent and a direct object, and it is in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is a connective for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); قُلْ is an imperative verb; رَبُّكُمْ is a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject); ذُو رَحْمَةٍ is the khabar (predicate); and واسِعَةٍ is an adjective of رَحْمَةٍ; the clause is in the position of an accusative as the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause of the saying and what is within its scope is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis.
(وَلا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُهُ عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the nominal clause, entering the scope of the saying; يُرَدُّ is a passive imperfect verb; بَأْسُهُ is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); عَنِ الْقَوْمِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يُرَدُّ; and الْمُجْرِمِينَ is a naʿt (adjective) of الْقَوْمِ.
(سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا: لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أَشْرَكْنا وَلا آباؤُنا) The clause is resumptive, introduced to report what will issue from them in speech. The sīn is a particle of futurity; يَقُولُ is an imperfect verb; الَّذِينَ is the agent; the clause أَشْرَكُوا has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; the clause لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ is in the position of an accusative as the content of the saying; لَوْ is conditional; شاءَ اللَّهُ is a verb and an agent, and the object of the willing is omitted, i.e. "had He willed that we not associate partners", and parallels to it have preceded. وَلا آباؤُنا is conjoined to the pronoun in أَشْرَكْنا, and the conjunction was permitted because of the presence of «لا».
(وَلا حَرَّمْنا مِنْ شَيْءٍ) It is conjoined to ما أَشْرَكْنا, and مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida) in the direct object.
(كَذلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) The kāf is a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and this has preceded, i.e. "those before them denied with a denial like that denial".
(حَتَّى ذاقُوا بَأْسَنا قُلْ: هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنا) حَتَّى is a particle of limit and of genitive, i.e. "they persisted in denial until they tasted"; بَأْسَنا is a direct object; هَلْ is an interrogative particle; the adverb is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; مِنْ is redundant in the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is the content of the saying. The fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation; تُخْرِجُوهُ is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أَنْ after it; the wāw is the agent and the hāʾ a direct object; and لَنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تُخْرِجُوهُ.
(إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَخْرُصُونَ) The clause is resumptive; إِنْ is negative; تَتَّبِعُونَ is a nominative imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent; إِلَّا is a particle of restriction; الظَّنَّ is a direct object; the wāw of وَإِنْ is a conjunction; إِنْ is negative; أَنْتُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; إِلَّا is a particle of restriction; and the clause تَخْرُصُونَ is the khabar of أَنْتُمْ.

dervis-irab:149-150.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبالِغَةُ) The clause of the saying is resumptive, and the fāʾ is the eloquent one (faṣīḥa), because it disclosed an implied condition, i.e. say: "if you have no proof, then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof". لِلَّهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; الْحُجَّةُ is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and الْبالِغَةُ is an adjective, i.e. the one that has reached the utmost limit of finality and clarity and cut off every excuse of the one against whom the proof is brought; and the clause is the content of the saying.
(فَلَوْ شاءَ لَهَداكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and لَوْ is conditional; شاءَ is a verb with a latent agent, and the direct object is omitted, i.e. "your guidance"; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لَوْ; هَداكُمْ is a verb with a latent agent and a direct object; the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and أَجْمَعِينَ is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the pronoun; the ruling on emphasis with أجمع will come in the section on Benefits.
(قُلْ: هَلُمَّ شُهَداءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ هذا) The clause is resumptive; قُلْ is an imperative verb; هَلُمَّ is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of command, and a discussion of it will come in the section on Benefits; شُهَداءَكُمْ is a direct object, for a verbal noun works like what it names, whether transitive or intransitive; الَّذِينَ is an adjective; the clause يَشْهَدُونَ is a ṣila; أَنَّ اللَّهَ is أَنَّ and its noun, in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition; and the clause حَرَّمَ هذا is the khabar of أَنَّ.
(فَإِنْ شَهِدُوا فَلا تَشْهَدْ مَعَهُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and إِنْ is conditional; شَهِدُوا is a past verb and the wāw is the agent, in the position of a jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ is a connective for the apodosis; لا is prohibitive; تَشْهَدْ is an imperfect verb made jussive by لا, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and مَعَهُمْ is an adverb of place attached to تَشْهَدْ.
(وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تَتَّبِعْ is an imperfect verb made jussive by لا; أَهْواءَ is a direct object; الَّذِينَ is a relative noun in the position of a genitive by annexation; بِآياتِنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كَذَّبُوا, and the clause is the ṣila.
(وَالَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ وَهُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and الَّذِينَ is conjoined to the preceding relative noun; the aim is to enumerate their ugly attributes. The meaning: do not follow the whims of those who combine the denial of the signs of Allah with disbelief in the Hereafter and the association of partners with Him. The clause لا يُؤْمِنُونَ is the ṣila of the relative; بِالْآخِرَةِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يُؤْمِنُونَ; the wāw is a conjunction; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يَعْدِلُونَ is its khabar; and بِرَبِّهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يَعْدِلُونَ.

* Rhetoric:
In applying the name of testimony (shahāda) to submission to them and agreeing with them and confirming them in the false testimony, there is an explicit, derivative metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya); and it is also sound that it be a free figurative expression (majāz mursal), from applying the necessary concomitant while intending what necessitates it, because testimony is among the concomitants of submission.

* Benefits:
When it is intended to strengthen the emphasis, the word «أجمع» is brought after the word «كله», and after the word «كلها» the word «جمعاء», and after the word «كلهم» the word «أجمعين», and after the word «كلهنّ» the word «جمع». You say: جاء الصفّ كله أجمع ("the whole class came, all of it"), and جاءت القبيلة كلها جمعاء ("the tribe came, all of it"); the Exalted said: «فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون»; and جاءت النساء كلهن جمع ("the women came, all of them"). Emphasis may also be made with أجمع, جمعاء, أجمعين and جمع even when the word «كل» has not preceded them, and from that are the words of the Exalted: «لأغوينهم أجمعين».
It is not permitted to form the dual of أجمع and جمعاء, there being no need for that, given the two words كلا and كلتا. Ibn Mālik, in his Alfiyya, summarised the rule of أجمع:
وبعد كل أكدوا بأجمعا ... جمعاء أجمعين ثم جمعا
ودون كل قد يجيء أجمع ... جمعاء أجمعون ثم جمع
(After kull they emphasise with ajmaʿ, jamʿāʾ, ajmaʿīn, then jumaʿ; and without kull there may come ajmaʿ, jamʿāʾ, ajmaʿūn, then jumaʿ.)
Halumma: a word in the sense of calling to a thing; it is thus intransitive, and it may be used transitively, as in: هلم شهداءكم, i.e. bring them. It is among the verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl), in which the singular and plural, the masculine and feminine are the same; and they conjugate it by making it a verb and attaching the pronouns to it, so they say in the dual: هلما; in the feminine: هلمي; in the masculine plural: هلموا; and for women: هلممن; and the first is more eloquent. It may be linked with the lām, so one says: هلمّ لك, like their saying: هيت لك. The heavy nūn of emphasis may be attached to it, so one says: هلمّنّ يا رجل, and هلمنّ يا امرأة, and هلمّانّ يا رجلان, and يا امرأتان, and هلمّنّ يا رجال, and هلمنانّ يا نسوة.
